Certain sounds, such as the uvular and glottal consonants, can be difficult for English speakers. Word order (object-verb-subject) may also take time to internalize. Finally, its practical use is limited, since it serves mainly as a hobby and cultural pursuit rather than a language for broad communication.

世界语由柴门霍夫于1887年创制，定位是一门中立、易学的国际辅助语言。它的优点比较突出：语法规则统一，几乎没有不规则变化；词缀系统清晰，掌握词根后能较快扩充词汇；拼写与发音基本一致，入门门槛低。不少学习者认为，它也能为之后学习其他外语打下一定基础。此外，世界语社群有较强的交流氛围，线上资源和国际聚会也比较丰富。

不足同样明显。使用人数有限，实际应用场景集中在爱好者圈层，难以替代英语等通用语言在学习、工作中的作用。词汇和语法主要取材于欧洲语言，对非欧洲语言背景的学习者而言，“中立”程度有所折扣。另外，它的文学、影视等原创内容总量不大，长期学习的外部支持有限。

总体来看，世界语适合作为兴趣学习、语言实验和跨文化交流的选择，但若以实用回报为首要目标，需要理性评估。

Typefaces are the only art form where a thousand designers spend years obsessing over the exact curve of a letter, and the audience's entire response is "I dunno, it looks fine."

You know who notices the difference between those two nearly identical lowercase "g"s? Nobody. Not even your mom. Not even the guy who made them. He just says "the terminals are more optimistic" and everyone nods like he's describing wine.

Every typeface claims to be "clean, modern, and timeless." That's three lies in one sentence. Clean means boring, modern means it'll look dated in four years, and timeless means it was already on a pharmacy sign in 1970.

And the ones that try to be fun? They look like a birthday party at a dentist's office.

Letters had one job: be read. Now they have personalities, backstories, and a licensing fee. Honestly, that's the most human thing about them.

克林贡语是由语言学家马克·奥克兰为《星际迷航》设计的人造语言，如今已发展为一套相对完整的体系。它的优点在于规则清晰：语序为宾语—谓语—主语，并通过丰富的前缀与后缀表达语法关系，结构有较强的内在逻辑。发音上，它使用喉音和小舌音，风格鲜明，与自然语言区分度高。同时，官方词典、语法资料和爱好者社区较为完善，学习者可以找到系统的入门材料，也有翻译作品和文化活动可供参与。

不足主要在于实用性有限。使用者规模很小，日常交流场景几乎不存在。词汇早期偏重战斗、荣誉等主题，虽然已有扩充，但在表达现代生活、抽象概念时仍显不足。此外，发音和语序对多数初学者并不友好，需要投入较多时间练习。总体而言，克林贡语更适合作为语言兴趣与文化爱好的对象，而非通用交流工具。

Typefaces are the only art form where thousands of people spend years obsessing over the difference between two letters that look identical to everyone else. "Notice the subtle curve on the lowercase g." No, Gerald. I notice you haven't been outside since March.

Every typeface has a personality, apparently. This one is "friendly but authoritative." So is my dentist, and he's never made me feel like a ransom note. Some are "elegant." Some are "bold." Some are "playful," which is what designers call it when the letters are drunk.

And the names! Every typeface is named like a boutique hotel or a divorced Swiss man. Then there's the one everybody hates, the one that shows up on a restaurant menu and a haunted-house flyer and a legal warning, like it's doing a tour of poor decisions.

Typefaces: they're just letters in costumes, and somehow they still get more credit than the words.

世界语由柴门霍夫于1887年创制，目标是提供一种中立、易学的国际交流工具。它的优点比较明显：语法规则统一，几乎没有例外；词根与词缀组合灵活，词汇积累较快；拼写与发音基本一一对应，入门门槛低。它也有助于理解语法结构，可作为学习其他语言的过渡。

不足同样存在。使用者数量有限，主要集中在爱好者群体和少数组织中，实际应用场景与职业价值不高，学习资源也少于主流语言。此外，其词汇主要源自欧洲语言，对非欧洲语言背景的学习者而言，“中立”程度仍有讨论空间。总体而言，世界语更适合作为兴趣与文化交流的选择。

克林贡语由语言学家马克·奥克兰为《星际迷航》设计，体系完整，是完成度较高的人工语言。它采用宾语—动词—主语的语序，并通过前缀和后缀表达语法关系，结构清晰，对语言爱好者颇具研究价值。官方词典、教材和学习社群也较齐全，入门资料不难获得。

不足在于，词汇最初围绕剧情需要设计，战斗与荣誉相关的表达丰富，日常和抽象概念的词语相对有限。喉塞音及部分辅音对初学者不太容易，大小写在拼写中也有区分作用，需要适应。此外，使用者较少，交流场景多局限于爱好者圈子。总体而言，它更适合作为兴趣与文化体验，而非日常沟通工具。

Typefaces: the only art form where people spend thousands of dollars on something they insist you shouldn't notice. "Good design is invisible," they say, while charging a licensing fee per pageview for the invisibility.

Every typeface has the same personality: "I'm clean, but with character." That's not a personality, that's a dating profile.

Designers will look at two letters that differ by half a pixel and gasp like they've found a body. Meanwhile, normal people are reading a menu, a ransom note, and a tax form in the same thing and surviving.

And the names! Every one sounds like a French baby, a cologne, or a Swiss bank. Then there's the "free" ones, which are free the way a puppy is free.

Typefaces are just the alphabet in costumes, and somehow it's still twenty-six letters.

Typefaces are the only group of things that can make you feel judged by a sandwich menu. Every one of them claims to have "personality," but really they're just letters in different outfits. It's the same twenty-six people at a costume party.

Serifs wear tiny shoes on every letter and think that's a personality. Sans-serifs are the guys who say "I just like things clean" while owning one gray sweater. Script fonts are for weddings, divorces, and a bakery that's definitely closing. Then come the "fun" ones, designed by someone who looked at a capital E and said, "What if it were drunk?"

And the naming! Typefaces sound like a law firm, a Swiss watch, or a retired pirate. Designers will spend six months arguing over a curve you'll never notice, then someone's uncle puts the whole wedding invitation in the font that looks like it's melting.

Typefaces: the only art form where everyone's an expert, and nobody can name the thing they hate.

我发现字体是人类最大的集体幻觉。全世界有几十万种字体，可我肉眼只能分三类：正常的、丑的、看不懂的。

设计师就不一样，他们会说："这个字，呼吸感不对。"字还有呼吸？我写个"明天开会"，它还得先喘两口？

最气的是选字体。PPT内容五分钟写完，选字体选一小时。挨个试，每个都觉得"嗯，差不多"，最后还是选了第一个。那我这一小时干嘛了？给字体面试吗？

更坑的是，你以为字体免费，结果收到律师函："您用的字是我们设计的。"我就写了"特价"两个字！以后我说话是不是也得先付费？

Web programming languages are the only tools where "it works" and "please don't touch it" mean the same thing. Every one of them was designed in ten days, by a committee, or by accident, and you can tell.

They all promise "write once, run anywhere," and then run differently everywhere. Your code works in one browser, panics in another, and in a third just stares at you like a dog watching a card trick.

Nothing stays stable. You learn a language on Monday, and by Friday there are four new ways to do the same thing, three of them deprecated, and one of them is a package that a guy deleted in 2016 and broke the entire internet.

And the type systems? Optional. Like seatbelts in a clown car.

We don't write web code. We negotiate with it.

我真搞不懂字体这个行业。电脑里装着几千个字体，我认识的就两种：能看的，和不能看的。

但设计师不一样。他说：“这个字距不对。”我盯了十分钟，没看出区别。他说：“差了半个像素。”半个像素！我这辈子差得远了，也没人跟我说不对。

还有分类，叫“衬线”和“无衬线”，听着像内衣款式。其实就是字尾巴有没有一小撇。

最气的是老板说：“字体换个高级点的。”我换了，他说：“嗯，有感觉了。”内容一个字没动啊！我写的还是请假条，只是现在看起来像请了个很贵的假。

后来我才知道，好多字体还要收费，一套好几千。我就想问，字是我打的，你收什么钱？你就是把“的”字的钩子弯了一下！

Web programming languages are the only tools where "it works" and "it's a good idea" have never once met. Every one of them was invented in ten days, by someone who swore it was temporary, and now it runs the global economy.

Nothing says "mature ecosystem" like a package that's one line long and has forty million downloads, until its author deletes it and half the internet falls over.

We've got frameworks that expire faster than milk. You learn one on Monday, and by Friday there's a newer one that does the same thing, but "reactively."

And the type systems? Optional. Like seatbelts in a clown car.

Web developers don't ask, "Is it correct?" They ask, "Does it render in the browser my customer is still using from 2011?"

Then they ship it, refresh, and pray. That's not engineering. That's a séance with semicolons.

我最服设计师，他们能盯着两个字看十分钟，然后说：“你看，这个钩子差了半毫米。”我看了半天，只看到字。

字体这东西，就是全世界最大的“找不同”游戏，而且答案只有设计师知道。

更离谱的是，字体还有版权。我一直以为字是仓颉造的，结果是公司的。你随手用一下，半年后收到律师函：您去年那份外卖菜单，侵权了。我一个卖炒粉的，被告字？

还有那些字体的介绍，什么“温柔”“灵动”“有呼吸感”。字还呼吸？我写“明天交报告”，它再温柔，老板也不会温柔。

我每次做PPT，选字体花三小时，内容写了三行。交上去领导说：“字太小，放大点。”

我三小时的审美，输给了一个“放大”。

我发现字体这个行业，就是专门负责让人不满意的。设计师能盯着两个字看半小时，然后说：“你看这个转折，情绪不对。”我看了半天，俩字一模一样啊！他说：“差了零点五个像素的忧伤。”

老板更绝，开会就一句：“这个字不够高级，换个高级的。”字还分穷人字和富人字？换完他点点头：“对，就是这个味。”我问跟刚才哪不一样？他说：“贵。”

最气的是，你熬夜做个文档发给别人，对方一打开，全乱码。因为他电脑里没有你的字体。字还挑电脑，你说势不势利？

现在更过分，字体还收费。我就写个“开业大吉”，法务找上门了。我敲的每个字，居然都有人在收租。

Web programming languages are the only tools where "it works" and "please don't touch it" mean the same thing. Every one of them was built in ten days, for one small job, and now runs the entire planet. It's like handing a kid a sparkler and waking up to find he's operating a power plant.

They've got types, except when they don't. They've got errors, except when they quietly shrug and keep going. You add a number to a word and the language says, "Sure, here's a sandwich."

And the ecosystem! To print "Hello, World," you install four hundred thousand packages written by a guy who deleted one of them out of spite and broke the internet.

Every year there's a new framework that fixes everything. By Thursday, it's legacy.

Web languages aren't programming. They're group therapy for semicolons.

Web programming languages are the only tools where "it works on my machine" is considered a deployment strategy. Every few months, someone announces a new one that's "simple, fast, and finally fixes everything," and by Tuesday there are forty-seven competing ways to print "Hello World," three of which require a build step.

These languages were designed in ten days, by committee, or by accident, and you can tell. Half the features exist because of a mistake someone was too scared to remove. The other half exist to fix the first half, and those need their own fixes.

The documentation says "intuitive." The error message says "undefined." Your career says "I've spent six hours centering a box."

And the ecosystem? You don't install a package. You summon fourteen thousand strangers' homework to add two numbers, then act shocked when one of them deletes itself.

It's not a tech stack. It's a group project nobody wants to grade.

Web 编程语言有个共同点：不是设计出来的，是逼出来的。别的语言是先画图纸再盖楼，Web 语言是半夜发现房子漏水，拿胶带先糊上，糊完发现能住，就开始收房租了。

而且它们特别"宽容"。你拿一个数字加一句话，正经语言直接报错骂你：你疯了吧？Web 语言说：懂你。然后给你一个谁都看不懂的结果。这不是宽容，这是纵容！就像那种永远不拒绝你的朋友，你说要辞职创业，他说有魄力；你说要抵押房子，他说支持你。

最惨的是还改不了，因为要向后兼容。二十年前糊的胶带，现在不叫胶带，叫"历史传统"。

Electron-beam resists, ladies and gentlemen. The only material that takes forty hours of writing time to draw a line, then shows up to the party and says, "Actually, I'm going to swell."

You spend all night with a beam of electrons carefully tickling your resist, and in the morning it develops like a Polaroid of your worst decisions. Proximity effect? That's not physics, that's your resist gossiping. Every electron scatters around telling its neighbors what the others are doing.

And the trade-offs! Want high resolution? Cool, enjoy sensitivity so low you'll be exposing until the heat death of the universe. Want sensitivity? Great, your features look like they were drawn by a toddler with a mitten on.

Then there's etch resistance, which is a lie the category tells itself. "I'll protect your substrate." Two seconds into plasma, it's gone. Ghosted you like a college roommate.

And they cost more per gram than saffron. For a spin-coated puddle that dies if someone looks at it wrong.

Electron-beam resists: the divas of nanofabrication. You spend eight hours writing a pattern one tiny dot at a time, because apparently light is too fast and too cheap for you. Then you pour your heart into a ten-nanometer feature, and the resist says, "Cool, I'll swell in the developer and collapse like a soufflé."

You're either so insensitive that exposure takes a geological era, or so sensitive that a stray electron looks at you funny and you cross-link. There's no middle. It's like dating.

Proximity effect? Electrons bounce around inside you like a pinball machine, then you blame the neighbors for the damage.

And storage requirements! Keep cold, keep dark, keep away from moisture, keep expectations low. My grandmother's sourdough starter is less needy.

Then comes the grand finale: lift-off, where you promise a clean pattern and deliver a metal-flake blizzard across the entire wafer.

Thanks for the resolution, though. Truly. Shame about everything else.

我特别佩服做 Web 开发的朋友，他们是一群在流沙上盖房子的人。

别的行业，学一门手艺管十年。他们不行，早上醒来发现昨天学的东西已经过时了。我说才一天啊？他说，在我们这儿，昨天就是上古。

而且这类语言特别宽容。你让它把数字和文字加一起，它不报错，还给你个结果。你问它这是啥，它说：我尽力了。

别的语言是你错了它骂你，这类是你错了它陪你一起错，错到上线，再让用户来告诉你。

最离谱的是，同一段代码，换个浏览器，效果还不一样。这不叫编程，这叫给十个脾气不同的人写同一份说明书，还要求他们理解一致。

这哪是写代码啊，这是搞外交。

我发现 Web 编程语言有个共同点：都不是设计出来的，是"长"出来的。就像小区里的违章建筑，今天有人加个阳台，明天有人搭个棚子，最后住户说：千万别动，一动全塌。

而且这类语言特别包容。你让数字和字符串相加，它不报错，它还帮你圆一个结果出来，一副"我尽力了"的表情。这哪是编程语言，这是职场老油条，从不说"不行"，只给你一个看着像答案的东西。

更新还特别快。我早上刚学会一种写法，中午就有人告诉我："哥，这已经是过时的做法了。"我写代码不是写代码，是追剧，每季都有新番，旧的还没完结。

我就想学点稳定的，朋友说："那你得去学考古。"

我发现Web编程语言有个共同特点：都不太认真。你让它算一个数字加一个字符串，它不报错，它给你个答案，还特别自信。就像你跟导航说“我要去机场”，它说：“好的，已为您导航到我外婆家。”你说不对啊，它说：“放心，我没报错。”

更绝的是，这类语言永远不能改错。因为全世界的网页都在跑，你改一个bug，三亿个网站集体罢工。所以它的bug不叫bug，叫“历史遗留特性”，听着像文物。

后来大家受不了了，发明了新语言来修复它。怎么修复呢？新语言写完，再翻译回那个有问题的语言。这不叫治病，这叫给病人请了个翻译。病还在，只是现在他有口译了。

Electron-beam resists: the only material that charges you more per square centimeter than a Manhattan landlord and still delivers nothing on time.

You want a ten-nanometer feature? Sure, just write it one pixel at a time, like a monk copying scripture with a single eyelash. Eight hours later, you develop it, and the whole thing collapses like a soufflé in an earthquake.

These things are so sensitive, a stray electron looks at them funny and they cross-link out of spite. But ask for sharp lines, and suddenly they're stubborn. Pick one: fragile or tough! They chose "fragile, but only when you need them tough."

Resolution, sensitivity, etch resistance: pick two. Actually, pick one, and it'll be wrong.

And the proximity effect? Electrons scatter everywhere, so your tiny pattern gets exposed by its neighbors. It's the only material with a built-in gossip problem.

Spin-coat, bake, expose, develop, cry. Repeat.

Electron-beam resists, ladies and gentlemen. The only material that takes eight hours of exposure to draw a line, then says, "Actually, I'd like to be a blob."

You spend a week writing a pattern one tiny dot at a time, like a monk copying scripture, and the resist's feedback is: "Too thick. Too thin. Too hot. Too cold. Have you tried not existing?"

They're the divas of nanofabrication. Sensitivity? Terrible. Resolution? Great, but only if you whisper to it, bless the developer, and sacrifice a graduate student. Want high sensitivity? Sorry, that's the rough-edge package. Want smooth edges? Enjoy your dose of 4,000 microcoulombs and a retirement party before the write finishes.

And the shelf life! They expire like milk, but cost like saffron. Your wafer sits there collecting proximity effects, scattering electrons into neighboring features like gossip at a wedding.

Then, after all that, liftoff fails. Every time. Because the resist is also clingy.

Text editors: the only software category where people have gone to war over how to close the program. Some of you have been trying to exit one since 2009 and are still in there, living in it, like a haunted house.

Every editor claims to be "lightweight." Then you install forty plugins, a theme called "Midnight Sorrow," and a package manager to manage the packages, and suddenly your lightweight tool needs more RAM than the space shuttle.

And the configuration! People spend six hours customizing their editor so they can save eleven minutes a week. That's not productivity, that's a hobby with a monospace font.

The diehards say, "I only use keyboard shortcuts." Great. You've memorized 400 commands to avoid moving your hand eight inches to a mouse. That's not efficiency, that's a hostage situation with muscle memory.

And somehow, after all this, every one of you still writes "final_v2_REALfinal.txt."

Text editors: the only software where people will fight to the death over how to type the letter "e."

Every editor claims to be "lightweight," then loads 400 plugins and takes eleven seconds to open a grocery list. Others are so minimal you need a PhD and a laminated cheat sheet just to leave. People have been trapped in some of these for years. We don't call it a bug. We call it "a workflow."

And the users! They'll spend forty hours customizing their setup to save four minutes a week. That's not productivity, that's a hobby with a dark theme.

Tabs versus spaces. Light mode versus dark mode. Every argument ends the same way: someone says "well, it's just a preference," and then spends three hours explaining why yours is wrong.

At the end of the day, it's all the same thing: a blinking cursor, silently judging you, waiting for you to write something worth saving.

搞微纳加工的人都知道，电子束光刻胶是材料界的相亲对象。分辨率高，就灵敏度低，你得一颗一颗电子喂它，一写写一晚上。灵敏度高了，线边缘又粗糙得像我的发际线。高分辨率、高灵敏度、低粗糙度，三样只能选两样，这不叫材料，这叫择偶。

价格还离谱，一小瓶比我一个月房租贵，用的时候就滴几滴，剩下的锁冰箱。我冰箱里光刻胶的待遇，比我的菜强多了。

显影多一秒，图形糊了，少一秒，没显干净。我这辈子对感情都没这么精确过。

最气的是，你熬通宵写了八个小时，早上一显影，图形全塌了。它不是塌，它是在礼貌地告诉你：“你的剂量，我不接受。”

做微纳加工的人最懂什么叫“渣男”，就是电子束光刻胶这一类。你想要高分辨率？可以，但它灵敏度就低，你得用大剂量哄它。哄得太用力，邻近效应就来了：你写一条线，旁边的线也跟着糊，它还管这叫“友情赞助”。

而且它特别娇气，得冷藏，保质期还短，比我家酸奶都讲究。你熬一整晚，才写出指甲盖那么大一块图。早上显影，一看，全倒了。你问它为什么，它说：“你剂量不对。”

谈恋爱吵架还能各打五十大板，在它这儿，永远是你的错，而且认错的方式就是重新排队，再熬一晚上。

做微纳加工的都知道，电子束光刻胶是实验室里最难伺候的东西。它有个“三选二”定律：分辨率高，就不灵敏；灵敏，边缘就毛；又清晰又灵敏，对不起，贵，还得放冰箱，保质期比我的恋情还短。这不是材料，这是相亲对象。

你拿电子束一点一点给它写图案，一写写一晚上，就为画个比指甲盖还小的东西。第二天早上显影，一看，歪了。为什么？邻近效应。就是你写这儿，它旁边也跟着有感觉。这像不像办公室八卦，我明明没碰它，它自己也曝光了。

最后线宽差了五纳米，导师说：“没事，误差。”我说：“老师，五纳米，对它是误差，对我是延期毕业。”

Text editors: the only software category where people have fought holy wars over where to put a cursor.

Think about it. Their entire job is to let you type letters. Humanity figured that out with the pencil. Yet somehow there are thousands of these things, and every user insists theirs is the one true path.

Some are so minimal they basically hand you a blank page and a shrug. Others are so bloated they have a built-in email client, a weather widget, and a therapist, but still can't open a 20 megabyte file without sobbing.

And the people who use them! Folks will spend forty hours configuring their setup to save eleven seconds a week. "I'm so productive now," they say, from inside a settings file they've been editing since Tuesday.

Meanwhile, the one thing everyone wants, a way to exit without Googling, remains a premium feature.

Text editors: where the real writing is the config file, and the actual work is always tomorrow.

Text editors: the only software category where people will fight to the death over how to type letters into a box.

Some are so minimal they open in a blank void and dare you to figure out how to leave. People have been trapped in there since the nineties. Their families hold a vigil.

Others have so many plugins you need a second editor just to edit the settings for the first one. You spend three weekends configuring your perfect setup, and zero weekends writing the thing you were going to write.

Then there's the "lightweight" ones that somehow eat four gigabytes of RAM to display a grocery list.

And the loyalists! Ask a developer which one they use and they respond like you asked about their religion, their ex, and their tax situation at once.

Every editor promises productivity. What they deliver is a personality, a keyboard shortcut you'll forget, and a dark theme you changed nine times today.

Nobody's writing code. We're all just decorating the room.

我最佩服电子束光刻胶这一类东西。它不是印，是画。人家光刻是一巴掌拍下去，一整片全有了；电子束是一个点一个点写，相当于拿毛笔在邮票上抄《红楼梦》。

而且它有个铁律：想要精细，就得慢；想要快，就得糊。这不就是我写论文吗？慢工出细活，赶工出毛刺。业内管这个叫“线边缘粗糙度”，我们管这个叫“我的人生”。

还有邻近效应，电子打进去会乱散射，旁边的图形互相串门。你想画两条线，它给你整出个“友谊地久天长”，连上了。

熬了一整夜，显影完拿显微镜一看：写好了！面积，指甲盖的四百分之一。

导师看完点点头：“不错，下周写大一点。”

我说大一点？老师，这玩意儿再大一点，我就得住在机房了。

你们发现没有，文本编辑器这玩意儿，本职工作就一件：让你打字。结果它给你整出一百个功能。

我就想写个“收到，谢谢”，它先弹个窗：“是否开启智能写作助手？”我谢谢你，“谢谢”两个字我自己会写。

我打个“嗯嗯”，它给我划条红线，说我拼错了。我嗯我的，你红什么？

最离谱的是格式。从别处复制一段字粘过来，字体变了，字号变了，行距也变了，整段话像是偷渡过来的。你想把它改回去，越改越歪，最后只能全选，删掉，重打。

所以编辑器最强的功能根本不是编辑，是让你对“撤销”这个键产生宗教般的信仰。

可惜撤销撤得回一切，唯独撤不回你关窗口时，手一抖点的那个“不保存”。

Spreadsheet software is the only product where a billion-dollar company says, "Here's a blank grid. Run your entire business off it." And somehow, we all said, "Perfect."

It's a calculator that went to business school and developed a God complex. Every spreadsheet starts as "just a quick list" and ends as a seventeen-tab monster named "FINAL_v4_REALfinal_USE THIS ONE."

The formulas are written by a guy named Gary who left in 2014. Nobody knows what column Q does. Nobody's brave enough to delete it. It's load-bearing.

And the error messages? Pound sign, pound sign, pound sign. That's not an error, that's a tic-tac-toe game the software gave up on.

Meanwhile, one misplaced decimal and suddenly the company owes the Moon money.

It's not software. It's a haunted house with cells. And we all live there, whispering, "Please don't recalculate."

我发现文本编辑器是世界上最奇怪的软件。它唯一的任务就是让你打字，结果人类花在研究它上面的时间，比打字还多。

换主题，装插件，调字体，折腾三个小时，终于配得漂漂亮亮。一看，今天要写的东西，一个字没写。

还有自动更正。我明明打对了，它非要给我改错，还一脸“我是为你好”。你说它像谁？像我妈。

撤销键是最治愈的，它是唯一一个肯对你说“没事，咱回到五分钟前”的东西。可你一激动按多了，它真就一路退回去，连你昨天写得最好的那句也给撤没了。

最离谱的是关闭的时候，它还弹个窗问：“是否保存？”

大哥，我对着你敲了两个小时，你问我要不要保存？你以为我是来练手速的吗？

Spreadsheet software is the only product where a billion-dollar company says, "Here's a blank grid. Run your entire business on it."

And we do! Every company on earth is held together by a file called "Final_v7_REAL_final_USE THIS ONE." Nobody knows who built it. The guy who did left in 2016. His formulas are now sacred scripture.

It's a calculator that went to college, got ambitious, and now thinks it's a database, a project manager, and a calendar. It's none of those. It's a Jenga tower with cell borders.

One misplaced comma and your quarterly forecast says the company owes the moon.

And the color coding! Yellow means "pending." Green means "done." Orange means something only Deborah understands, and Deborah is on vacation.

It has a thousand functions, and you use four. The rest are just there to scare you.

Spreadsheets: where data goes to become a rumor.

Spreadsheet software is the only product where "I just need to add up a column" ends with you three hours deep in a formula that looks like a ransom note written by a calculator.

It's a grid. That's the whole idea. Humanity looked at graph paper and said, "What if this could ruin marriages?"

Every company runs on one spreadsheet nobody understands. Dave built it in 2009. Dave is gone. Dave's file is called "FINAL_v7_REAL_final_USE THIS ONE." If you change one cell, payroll becomes a rumor.

And the error messages! "#REF!" That's not an error, that's a text from your ex. "#VALUE!" Thanks, I'll tell my therapist.

It promises organization, then hands you 40 tabs, 12 colors, and a freeze-pane that freezes the wrong thing.

It's not software. It's a very polite way of losing your weekend.

Spreadsheet software is the only tool where a billion-dollar company and a guy named Gary use the exact same thing to run everything, and Gary's version is somehow more stable.

It's a calculator that went to business school and came back thinking it's a database. Every spreadsheet starts as "just a quick list" and ends as a 47-tab monument to nobody's retirement. Tab one is data. Tab two is also data, but different. Tab thirty-one is called "FINAL_v3_USE THIS ONE" and tab thirty-two is called "actually final."

One wrong click and your entire budget turns into a row of pound signs, like the program is cursing at you. Meanwhile, it will auto-convert a gene name into a date, because why not.

And the formulas? Nobody knows how they work. Someone who quit in 2016 wrote them. We just pray, never scroll right, and whisper "please don't recalculate."

你们有没有发现，文本编辑器是世界上最没自信的东西。我关窗口的时候，它还问：“是否保存更改？”我写了三个小时，你问我要不要保存？我是来这儿练手速的吗？

还有那个红色波浪线。我写朋友名字，它画红线；写网络用语，它画红线；我真打错了，它还自作主张，帮我改成一个更离谱的。

最离谱是排版。我就想把一行往右挪一点点，整篇文章像地震了：图片飞到下一页，标题跑到结尾。它仿佛在说：“行，那我顺便帮你重新安排一下人生。”

唯一让我感动的是“撤销”。要是生活里也能按一下，我肯定回到十分钟前，不发那句“收到，马上”。

文本编辑器这玩意儿，功能就一个：打字。人类几千年前刻在石头上都没出过问题。现在呢？我打个“你好”，它给我改成“你号”，我改回来，它又改回去。这哪是编辑器，这是跟我抬杠的语文老师。

还有自动保存，我没让它保存，它天天偷偷保存。等我真想保存了，它问我：“确定要覆盖吗？”我说确定。它说：“真的确定吗？”我结婚都没被问过这么多遍。

最离谱是关窗口。我就打开看了一眼，什么都没动，它蹦出来：“是否保存更改？”我说我没改啊！它说：“那也问问你。”

所以我现在写东西都用纸。纸有个优点：我撕它的时候，它不会问我“确定要放弃吗”。

我发现，表格软件是人类史上最成功的编程语言，因为它能让你觉得自己没在写代码。你以为你在做个表，其实你在写程序，还是没有注释、没法调试、全公司只有一个人看得懂的那种。

那个人一离职，这张表就成了古墓，谁也不敢动。你手一抖改了一个数，满屏就开始飘红，一串报错像在骂你。

更可怕的是文件名。“最终版”，“最终版2”，“最终版改”，“最终版这次真的不改了”。

这哪是文件管理啊，这是一个打工人的精神状态变化曲线。

我发现，电子表格软件是人类发明过最危险的东西。它看着就是一堆格子，人畜无害。结果全公司拿它干大事：记账、排班、做项目管理，还有人拿它画画。

你输个身份证号进去，它特别热心，帮你变成科学计数法。大哥，我是登记个人信息，不是计算银河系距离。

而且这东西，会写个公式就是公司大神。同事过来说：“老师，帮我看一眼。”你一看，八层引用套在一起。你改一个数，其他表集体崩溃，满屏井号，像在骂你。

最绝的是文件名：“终版”“终版改”“终版改2”“终版这次真的是终版”。

这哪是文件啊，这是一个人逐渐崩溃的心路历程。

Windows versions are the only product line where every release is either "the one everyone hated" or "the one everyone's finally forgiven." There's no middle. Just a never-ending cycle of apology and amnesia.

Every launch, Microsoft says, "This time, it's different." Sure. Different like a new haircut on a guy who still won't return your calls.

They move the Settings menu every time, like a landlord rearranging your furniture while you sleep. Want to change your display? Great, here are three places to do it, and none of them has the option.

And updates? "Restarting in 15 minutes." Buddy, I was in the middle of something. "Installing update 1 of 1." It has said that for forty minutes.

Still, we keep coming back, like a toxic relationship with a taskbar. We complain, we upgrade, we complain again. That's not an operating system. That's Stockholm syndrome with a Start button.

Windows versions are the only product line where every new release is announced like a miracle and remembered like a hostage situation.

Every few years Microsoft says, "This one's different. It's faster, cleaner, more secure." Then you install it and your printer files for divorce.

They fix things nobody asked them to fix and move things you just learned how to find. The Settings menu has been "coming soon" since I was young. There are two control panels, and they hate each other like divorced parents at a graduation.

And the updates! "Restarting to install updates, 37%." Sir, I have a deadline. "Still 37%." Sir, I have a family.

Every version has a fan club that insists, "Honestly, it's the best one yet," which is what you say about a dentist who only used a little drill.

Somehow, we keep upgrading anyway. It's not loyalty. It's Stockholm syndrome with a start menu.

我发现一个规律：全世界的公司，最核心的系统都不是花几百万买的，而是一个表格。文件名叫“最终版”，旁边还有“最终版2”“最终版改”“这次真的最终版，别动”。

表格里有个公式，是三年前离职的同事写的，没人看得懂，但全公司的工资都靠它算。大家态度特别统一：别碰，它现在还能跑，就是奇迹。

还有颜色标记。黄色代表“待确认”，浅黄代表“待确认但不急”，橙色是老板那天心情不好随手涂的。

最离谱是合并单元格。你想排个序，它说：“不行。”你想求个和，它说：“你再想想。”这哪是软件，这是个有原则的门卫。

最后你发现，嘴上说是我们用表格管理数据，其实是表格在管理我们。

我特别佩服简历上写“精通电子表格”的人。你精通什么呀？不就是会把第一行加粗，再涂个黄色吗？

真正精通的人，是公司里那位写了十七层嵌套公式然后离职的同事。现在全公司的工资都靠那个公式活着，没人敢动。大家路过那个单元格，都得低头默哀，跟路过祖坟一样。

而且这玩意儿特别会骂人。你公式写错了，它不说“你错了”，它给你甩一个井号，后面跟一串英文，连感叹号都懒得给。这种冷暴力，谁受得了？

最气的是合并单元格。有人觉得好看，一合并，排不了序，筛不了选，整张表当场社会性死亡。

然后老板过来一句：“你帮我把表拉一下。”拉一下？这哪是拉表，这是给公司做心脏搭桥啊！

Windows versions are the only product line where every release is announced as "the most secure, most reliable Windows ever," like that's a high bar. It's the fastest turtle. The tallest hobbit.

Every few years they redesign the Start menu, because apparently the one place you've learned to find things was too convenient. The Control Panel has been "being replaced" for so long it has tenure. You can still dig through five layers of settings and find a dialog box that looks like it was drawn in a hostage video from 1998.

And the updates! "Restarting to install updates, 30% complete. Don't turn off your computer." Sir, I have a presentation. "Working on it. 30% complete." It's been an hour. "30% complete."

Windows isn't an operating system. It's a long-term relationship where you keep saying, "It'll get better," and it keeps saying, "Please wait."

Windows versions are like a family of siblings where every one of them promises to be the responsible one, and every one of them shows up to Thanksgiving crashing into the furniture.

Every release comes with a big announcement: "This one's faster, cleaner, and more secure!" Then you install it and it asks you to restart. Then it asks again. Then it restarts itself during your presentation, because it knows.

Each version moves the settings menu to a new location, like a toddler hiding your keys. There are two control panels now. Two! One is modern, one is old, and the one you need is always in the other.

And the updates? "Working on updates. Don't turn off your computer." Sir, I've aged four years. My computer isn't working on updates. My computer is having a spiritual journey.

Still, we keep upgrading. Because nothing says loyalty like abuse.

我特别佩服Windows，每次出新版本都说：“这是有史以来最好的一版！”那上一版是什么？骗我的？这跟前任一模一样，每一个分手时都说“我变了”。

而且它更新特别有仪式感。你正赶方案呢，它弹个窗：“我们正在为您准备一些东西。”准备什么？准备让我今天什么都干不成吗？

最离谱的是，每个版本都有人怀念。你问他为啥喜欢那版，他说：“我年轻时用的就是那个。”那不是系统好，是你那时候好。

现在找个设置，简直是考古。设置里找不到，去控制面板；控制面板里点两下，又把你弹回设置。两个部门互相踢皮球，你就是那个球。

我发现Windows的版本有个规律：新的一出来，全网都在骂，说还是以前那个好用。结果用了三年，习惯了，官方一宣布停止支持，大家又集体痛哭：“你不能杀它，它是我的孩子！”那你当初骂它的时候怎么不想想今天呢？

而且每一版发布会都说“史上最稳定、最安全、最流畅”，跟相亲简历一样，写得都特别好。见面才发现，爱好是“突然更新”。

更新还特别会挑时间。你正开会，PPT 讲到最后一页，它弹出来：“我们正在准备一些东西，请勿关闭电脑。”准备什么？惊喜吗？我怕准备的是惊吓。

还有设置，新旧两套并存。控制面板里找不到，去设置里找；设置里没有，又把你送回控制面板。这哪是系统啊，这是两个前任在抢同一个孩子的抚养权。

Pizza is the only food where every region insists they invented perfection and everyone else is committing a crime. It's bread, sauce, and cheese. That's it. That's the whole pitch. And somehow we've turned it into a civil war.

Every city has a style, and every style comes with a personality disorder. Some are so thick you need a nap and a lawyer. Some are so thin they're basically a cheese-flavored rumor. Some are cooked so fast they're still arguing with the oven, and some are so proud of their own history they come with a lecture.

And the people! Nobody gets as defensive about a food that costs twelve dollars and ends up on their shirt. Ask someone about their hometown pizza and watch a calm adult turn into a cult spokesperson.

Meanwhile, at 2 a.m., every one of you eats whatever's still warm.

Pizza is just bread, sauce, and cheese, yet somehow it has more factions than a fantasy novel. Every region has its own version, and every region insists theirs is the only real one. Ask someone where they're from, then ask about pizza, and watch a calm adult turn into a cult spokesperson.

Some are so thin you need a permit to call it food. Some are so thick it's a casserole with abandonment issues. Some are folded like a wallet. Some are cut into squares, like the cook gave up on geometry halfway through.

And everyone swears their pizza is "technically the original." Buddy, it's dough that went to the oven. Nobody's defending a thesis.

Meanwhile, every style ends the same way: 11 p.m., standing over an open box, eating a cold slice off the counter like a raccoon with a mortgage.

Windows 每出新版本，发布会上都说：“这是有史以来最好的版本！”那你是在承认前面都是半成品吗？

它的升级逻辑也很神奇。用户说：“挺好的，别动我。”它说：“不行，我要停止支持你了。”这不叫升级，这叫拆迁。

新版本装完第一件事：找东西。设置在哪？控制面板呢？哦，它还在，躲在设置后面，像退休老干部，没人理，但真出事了还得去求他。

最离谱的是，每个版本刚出来都被骂，等下一个来了，大家又说：“还是上一个好。”合着它的优点，必须等被淘汰以后才能显现。这哪是操作系统，这是前任。

我觉得 Windows 的每一代版本，都像前任。新的一出来，官方就说：“这次真的不一样了。”哪不一样？把你熟悉的功能搬了家，藏到三层菜单后面，还美其名曰“更现代”。

你去问客服，客服说：“这个要去新的设置里找。”我说新的设置里没有。他说：“那您回旧的控制面板。”我说那到底哪个是新的？他说：“都是，您两边都得会。”这不是系统，这是异地恋。

最神奇的是，每个版本都有人怀念上一个。可上一个出来的时候，你们不也骂吗？这就跟夸前任一样，分手以后，全是优点。

还有更新，永远挑你最忙的时候。屏幕上写着“请勿关闭电脑”，我就坐那儿盯着转圈圈，像在产房门口等孩子。等了四十分钟，护士出来说：“恭喜，换了个图标。”

Pizza is just bread, sauce, and cheese, yet somehow it has more factions than the Middle Ages. Every region invented its own version, then built a personality around it. Nobody's saying "I like pizza." They're saying "I'm a pizza person," like it's a political affiliation.

Every style insists it's the original. Every style insists the others aren't "technically pizza." Sir, it's a flat bread with toppings. Calm down.

Some are so thick they're basically casserole in a costume. Some are so thin they're a cracker with ambition. Some are square, because apparently circles were too easy. Some need a fork. Some need a nap. Some need a lawyer.

And the arguments! Grown adults, screaming over dough like it's custody court.

Pizza: the only food where everyone's right, nobody agrees, and everyone's still eating it cold at 2 a.m.

我真搞不懂，披萨为什么要分流派。流派！不就是一个圆面饼，抹点酱，撒点奶酪，烤一烤，搞得跟武林门派似的。

现在吃个饭还得先站队。你刚说一句“这饼底有点厚”，对面立刻冷笑：“你懂什么叫披萨吗？”我不懂啊，我只知道我饿。

而且每个流派都觉得别的流派不正宗。薄的说厚的是蛋糕，厚的说薄的是饼干，最后大家只在一件事上达成共识：外卖送来的这个，都不正宗。

最好笑的是，吵得最凶的那帮人，凌晨一点喝完酒，蹲在路边，捧着一块凉透的披萨，吃得热泪盈眶。

那一刻哪还有什么流派，只有碳水，只有和解。

现在连披萨都分流派了。一个圆饼上撒点奶酪，居然能吵出宗教战争。

每个流派都坚信自己才是正宗，别人家的那不叫披萨，叫"面饼的误会"。你跟他们说"我就想吃口热的"，他们看你的眼神，就像你在教堂里问Wi-Fi密码。

最离谱的是规矩。这个流派规定绝对不许放这个，那个流派规定必须放那个，还有人拿尺子量边，说直径差两厘米不合格。哥们，你是在吃饭还是在验钞？

而且你发现没有，吵得最凶的，从来不是做披萨的，是点外卖的。人家师傅在后厨一边揉面一边想：我就想下班。

不过没事，等外卖送到，披萨都凉了。凉了之后，所有流派终于和解了。这才是真正的世界和平。

Pizza styles are the only food category where everyone fights over the same three ingredients. Bread, sauce, cheese. That's the whole product. Yet every city acts like it personally discovered fire.

Every style has a guy. You know the guy. He'll tell you the other kinds aren't even pizza. Sir, you're holding a casserole with a superiority complex.

And the rules! Fold it this way. Never use a fork. Never use ketchup. Cut it in squares, cut it in triangles, cut it like a divorce lawyer. People treat pizza like a constitutional democracy, and it's a circle of dough you ordered in your pajamas.

But here's the beautiful part. Every style ends the same way: 1 a.m., cold, standing over the sink, eating it off the box lid like a raccoon with a mortgage.

Different crusts. Same shame.

现在吃披萨，得先站队。你说想吃披萨，旁边立马有人问：哪个流派的？我说就……圆的，热的，有奶酪的。他看我的眼神，像我说"我信教，随便哪个"。

这帮人吵起来还特别专业。厚的说薄的是饼干，薄的说厚的是蛋糕，吵到最后达成共识：只有我吃的这个叫披萨，其他的都是"面饼承载配料的行为艺术"。

你想想，这玩意儿不就是面饼、酱、奶酪吗？三样东西，愣是吵出了世界大战的气势。人类和平不是毁在什么大事上，是毁在一块饼到底该多厚。

我是真的不懂。我饿的时候，"正宗"的定义特别简单：现在，马上，能吃到嘴里的，就是正宗。

Tropical fruits. You're the only food group that shows up to dinner wearing armor. Spikes, fuzz, shells like a medieval siege weapon. I need a machete, a YouTube tutorial, and a signed waiver just to have a snack.

And the attitude! You grow in paradise, then fly to my grocery store for nine dollars a pound. You've logged more air miles than I have. You arrive hard as a rock, then you're perfectly ripe for exactly four minutes before turning into a science fair project on my counter.

Every one of you comes with a "hack" for cutting it. If your food needs a tutorial, it's not food, it's IKEA furniture.

And the smell. Some of you smell like heaven, some like a gym bag in a hospital. There's no middle ground.

Honestly, you're a vacation: expensive, overhyped, and I come home sticky, sunburned, and slightly poorer.

现在最离谱的，就是披萨流派之争。你说这玩意儿，不就是一个面饼，抹点酱，撒点芝士，扔进烤箱吗？结果吃披萨的人硬是分成了好几个教派，每个教派都有自己的圣经。

你说一句“我就想吃口披萨”，他们看你的眼神，像你在教堂里点外卖。

最好笑的是，每一派都觉得别的派“那不叫披萨”。厚的说薄的是饼干，薄的说厚的是蛋糕。两边吵得不可开交，一看有人拿刀叉吃，立刻联手，一致对外。

披萨本来是穷人为了填饱肚子发明的，现在吃一口还得先考个资格证。

我点外卖，页面上写着“正宗”两个字，价格直接贵三十。正宗是什么？就是老板敢跟你吵架的底气。

Tropical fruits. You're the influencers of the produce aisle. Every one of you arrives with a passport, a huge markup, and an attitude that says, "I've been places you haven't."

And the armor! Spikes, scales, hairy shells, skin like a medieval weapon. It takes a machete, a YouTube tutorial, and an urgent care co-pay just to reach the snack. Regular fruit says, "Here, take a bite." You say, "First, prove you deserve me."

Then there's the ripeness window: eleven minutes. Rock hard on Tuesday, science experiment by Wednesday. I've bought you at "perfect" and watched you rot while I looked for a knife.

You cost nine dollars, you flew in first class, and your greatest contribution to society is a cocktail with a tiny umbrella in it. Meanwhile, the apple sits in a bowl for a month, loyal, asking for nothing.

Be more like the apple.

Tropical fruits, you're the influencers of the produce aisle. You're expensive, you're overseas, and you act like it's a personality. Every one of you showed up with a passport and a superiority complex.

You're armored like medieval knights. Spikes, scales, shells, fuzz. I need a machete, a YouTube tutorial, and a signed waiver just to get a snack. Meanwhile an apple says "bite me" and means it.

And the ripeness window? Forty-five seconds. You're rock-hard on Tuesday, perfect for one blink on Wednesday, and a science experiment by Thursday. I've had shorter relationships, but never more expensive ones.

You're also the only food whose marketing is "It tastes like vacation." No. I'm in my kitchen, bleeding, holding a smoothie that cost eleven dollars. You've never been to a beach. You were picked green, put on a boat, and gassed into pretending.

Paradise, my foot. You're just sugar with a travel budget.

热带水果这个东西，我真的搞不懂。你说它是水果，它长得像防御工事。又是刺，又是壳，又是硬皮，我吃个水果，还得先做个工程评估。

温带水果多亲民啊，洗洗就啃。热带水果不行，它出身就高冷，从小在太阳底下晒大的，脾气都大。吃它要过三关：第一关，打开；第二关，判断熟没熟，这个全靠玄学；第三关，忙了半天，发现能吃的就那么一小块，剩下全是垃圾桶的业绩。

还贵。一小盒标价跟卖首饰似的。人家是飞几千公里来的，坐的头等舱，待遇比我出差好。我坐经济舱，到了它还要我供着。

最气的是，我花大价钱，剥得满手是汁，朋友问：“好吃吗？”我说：“还行，主要是长见识。”

这哪是水果啊，这是研学。

Tropical fruits, you're the only food group that shows up to dinner dressed for a luau and expects us to be impressed. You grow on beaches, you've never worked a day in your life, and somehow you still need a machete, a YouTube tutorial, and a tetanus shot to get through your front door.

You come with armor, spikes, and fuzz. Who hurt you? I just wanted a snack, not a hostage negotiation.

And the ripeness window? Rock-hard on Tuesday, soup by Wednesday, with a lovely forty-five seconds of perfection while I'm in the shower. You travel four thousand miles to get here, so you show up bruised, jet-lagged, and charging nine dollars.

You're "exotic," which is just Latin for "overpriced and sticky." You live on vacation, and you want me to pay for it.

Still, you're delicious. That's the worst part.

热带水果这一类东西，我是真看不懂。说它是水果吧，它活得像个保镖。外壳不是带刺就是硬得像头盔，我吃个水果还得先备工具，这哪是吃饭，这是拆弹。

好不容易拆开了，里面就那么点肉，还跟核长一块儿，我啃半天，感觉是在跟它谈判。

价格更离谱。听说在产地，它们跟咱们这儿的白菜一个待遇，路边随便捡。到了咱这儿，一个够我吃三顿饭。它这一路是坐头等舱来的吗？

挑的时候还特别玄学。老板拍着胸脯说“保熟”，我买回去一开，要么生得像石头，要么熟得像事故现场。他保熟，但没说保甜。

最后吃完，手是黏的，桌子是黏的，心里还有个疑问：我是不是被一个水果PUA了？

Pungent Chinese street food is the only cuisine that announces itself like a hostage negotiator. You smell it a full block before you see it. Your nose files a formal complaint, your eyes start watering in solidarity, and somewhere a stray cat turns around and goes home.

These foods don't have flavor, they have a criminal record. They smell like a gym bag fermented in a swamp, yet the line is forty people deep, and every one of them is smiling. Nobody smiles in line at a dentist.

And the vendor stands there calm, like a man who lost his sense of smell in 1994 and never looked back.

Then you take one bite and it's delicious, which is the real insult. Your nose says run. Your mouth says marry it. Your body is a house divided, and the kitchen is winning.

Pungent Chinese street food doesn't wait for you to find it. It finds you. You're a block away, enjoying a nice evening, when the smell walks up, grabs you by the nostrils, and says, "We need to talk."

These foods have no inside voice. Every other cuisine says, "Come closer, taste me." This category says, "Cross the street, coward." It's the only food with a restraining order built in.

And the vendors just stand there, calm and smiling, like a lifeguard at a sewage plant. "Try some!" Sir, my eyes are watering from the free sample you're giving the whole neighborhood.

Yet somehow it's delicious. That's the real betrayal. It smells like a gym bag lost a fight with a swamp, but tastes like a hug. Your nose files a complaint, and your mouth ignores it and asks for seconds.

热带水果这一类东西，我真是搞不懂。先说包装，不是长刺，就是带硬壳，要么就是一层你不确定能不能吃的皮。这哪是水果，这是安保系统。

我就想吃口甜的，结果得先学三十秒拆弹。网上教程说"很简单，轻轻一掰"。我轻轻一掰，指甲断了，水果毫发无损。

价格也很热带。一小盒三个，九十九。我问老板你这是水果还是首饰？老板说："这是空运的。"我说那它坐的是头等舱吧，难怪肉这么嫩。

最气的是，好不容易剥开了，里面还有个核，大得像它才是主角，果肉只是赞助商。

我们北方人吃苹果，咬一口就完事，诚实，朴素，不骗人。热带水果呢，从买到吃，全程跟你玩心理战。

我就搞不懂热带水果。水果不就是让人吃的吗？它们不这么想。你看那一个个，有的带刺，有的带甲，有的裹着一层硬壳，像出厂就配了防弹衣。我买个水果，还得先学拆弹。

而且贵。标签上写着“空运”，我当场就沉默了：你一个水果，坐得比我还高级。我上次坐飞机还是经济舱，它坐头等舱，到了我这儿，还得我给它付钱。

最气的是，费那么大劲剥开，里面永远只有一句话：“很甜。”甜是它唯一的优点，其他一概没有，跟渣男一模一样。可偏偏就是有人吃这一套，吃完手还黏半天。

所以我现在只吃苹果。皮薄，不装，咬一口就行。人也一样，别太复杂，谁也没空陪你拆。

Pungent Chinese street foods are the only cuisine that files a complaint before you even see it. You smell it from three blocks away, and your nose sends a formal resignation letter. It's the only meal that comes with its own weather system.

These foods don't have flavors, they have *intentions*. Locals line up happily, while tourists stand downwind negotiating with their own survival instincts. "It tastes better than it smells," they promise, which is the most terrifying review a dish can receive. That's not a recommendation, that's a hostage negotiation.

The vendors are completely unbothered. They've been marinated in the aroma for so long they're basically a menu item. Meanwhile, I once ate some and my clothes held onto the smell for three days. My jacket now has a personality, and it's worse than mine.

Still delicious, though. Annoyingly delicious. I hate it.

我发现中国有一类小吃，它不是食物，是一场社会实验。你还没看见摊位，鼻子先报警了。这种东西不用打广告，味道就是传单，方圆三百米，全体免费试闻。

最神奇的是老板，表情特别淡定。我们捏着鼻子绕路，他端着碗一脸“这不挺香的嘛”。他不是闻不到，他是已经修炼成仙了。

再看吃的人，你问他好吃吗，他说：“你不懂，就是那个味儿！”什么叫那个味儿？这叫案发现场好吗！

最离谱的是，他们还劝你：“你试一口，第一口难，第二口就上瘾了。”大哥，这话我只在两个地方听过，一个是传销，一个就是这种小吃摊。

中国有一类小吃，我管它叫“气味先到，人后到”。你还在街口，味道已经替它报了名。

最神奇的是，所有爱吃的人都说同一句话：“闻着臭，吃着香。”这话你细品，这不是诈骗话术吗？“来，进来坐，进来就不臭了。”

而且他们还特别骄傲。你说不吃，他还怜悯你：“你没吃过好的。”好像我拒绝的不是一口小吃，是人生。

最狠的是，一桌只要有一个人点了，全桌都得入伙。空气是公共资源，我连拒绝的权利都没有。

吃完我去坐电梯，一进去，所有人都看我。我想解释：“不是我，是衣服！”可没人信，因为衣服也是我穿的。

Pungent Chinese street food is the only cuisine that files a noise complaint with your nose. You smell it from three blocks away, and your brain says, "Something died." Then your stomach says, "Order two."

These foods don't have aroma, they have intentions. It's a smell with a criminal record. Vendors swear it tastes better than it smells, which is also what people say about their cousin's new boyfriend.

The whole category is basically a dare with a two-dollar price tag. Fermented, funky, fried, and completely unapologetic. Every bite is a trust fall with your own immune system.

And the loyalty! Locals will cross a typhoon for a serving, while tourists hold their breath like they're walking past a swamp. Nobody is neutral. You either love it, or you're a witness.

Honestly, I respect it. It's the only food that tells you exactly how it's going to treat you, and then still gets a line around the block.

Plant-based milks are the only products that got famous by defining themselves as what they aren't. "Not milk" is the whole pitch. Imagine a dating profile that just says "Definitely not my ex."

It's the only beverage aisle where the ingredients list reads like a chemistry final: water, a rumor of a vegetable, and eleven things ending in "-gum." You're not drinking a nut or a grain. You're drinking the memory of one, filtered through a sock.

And the price! Four dollars for what is essentially expensive water that went to a farmers market once.

Then there's the barista edition, because apparently regular plant milk couldn't handle the pressure of foaming. It needed a special version, like an emotional support carton.

Still, it's great in coffee. It separates, curdles, and ruins your morning, just like a real relationship.

我发现中国有一类小吃，设计理念就是"先劝退，再征服"。你离它还有三百米，鼻子就报警了："前方疑似化学事故！"结果走近一看，排队的人比银行还多。

这类东西最神奇的是，所有人安利你都是同一句话："你就尝一口，闻着臭，吃着香！"这话耳熟吧？渣男也这么说："你就试一下，不会怎么样的。"

吃完更惨，你整个人都被腌入味了。进电梯，同事集体沉默；回到家，狗往后退半步，眼神里写着："你是不是在外面有别的狗了？"

可你问我下次还吃吗？我吃。人这辈子，总得有点明知道会后悔、还非要再来一份的东西。

Plant-based milks are the only products in the world that are defined entirely by what they're not. "Not milk." That's the whole pitch. Imagine a restaurant advertising "Not Steak."

Look at the carton. It's got a farm on it, a cartoon sun, and a font that says "grandma's kitchen," but the ingredient list reads like a chemistry final. Water, one nut that was briefly in the room, and gellan gum. Who's Gellan? Why is he holding this together?

And it's a "barista blend," which means it's been engineered to foam, because apparently regular coffee wasn't pretentious enough.

It costs six dollars, tastes like a glass of cold, sweetened drywall, and separates in your coffee like a bad breakup. But you'll defend it at brunch like it's your child.

"It's creamy!" No. It's beige. There's a difference.

中国有一类小吃，我管它们叫“嗅觉恐怖袭击”。你说它好吃吧，确实好吃；你说它好闻，那你是在对自己的鼻子撒谎。

这类东西的老板都爱说一句：“你别闻，你直接吃。”这话就很诡异，好像我的鼻子和嘴不是一个人的。哪有食物一上来就要求我跟自己的鼻子断绝关系？

吃的人还特别骄傲：“第一口你肯定接受不了，多吃几口就爱上了。”兄弟，这不是美食，这是斯德哥尔摩综合征。

最可怕的是吃完以后，它不会放过你。它跟你回家，跟你上班。开会的时候，同事不说话，只是默默把窗户打开，然后看着你，眼神里全是体谅。

Plant-based milks are the only products where the first ingredient is "water" and they still charge you six dollars. That's not milk, that's a beige rumor.

The carton says "barista edition," which means it was engineered to not curdle in coffee. Every other milk alternative just ruins your latte on its own, in front of everyone.

And the shaking. "Shake well." Why? What happened to it overnight? It's a carton that separates like a couple in therapy.

Check the label: "Made with real vegetables." Sir, it's a liquid. Nothing in my cereal should have a farm backstory and a chemistry degree.

And the people who drink it are so proud. "I switched." Great. You've turned breakfast into a hostage negotiation between your cereal and a glass of sad, expensive oatmeal-colored weather.

Still, I'll keep buying it. Because nothing says "I care about the planet" like paying a premium to be mildly disappointed every morning.

Plant-based milk is the only product that's proud of what it isn't. "Look, no cow!" Congratulations, you've invented water that went through something.

The ingredient list reads like a hostage note: "Water, a nut we once saw, sunflower oil, gums, and natural flavors." Gums? I'm drinking something that could also hold a poster to a wall.

And the price! You pay six dollars for a carton that's 98% tap water with a good publicist. Somewhere a farmer is crying, and so is your wallet.

Then there's the "barista edition," because regular versions curdle in coffee like they've seen a ghost. It's the only drink with stage fright.

And every carton insists it's "creamy." That's not a description, that's a plea. It's like a substitute teacher saying, "I'm basically a real teacher."

But sure, tell me again at brunch how it "tastes the same."

现在去咖啡店，店员问我："加奶，还是加植物奶？"我愣住了。"植物奶"这名字本身就是个悖论。奶是哺乳动物的事，植物要是能产奶，那它得先怀个孕吧？

说白了，就是把一把种子泡水里，磨碎，过滤，装瓶，贴上"奶"字。这不叫奶，这叫种子的洗澡水。

最离谱的是价格，比真奶还贵。我多花钱，买一杯"没有任何动物参与"的水。

而且它们还特别努力地想像奶：加增稠剂，加香精，加钙。就像一个人拼命想活成别人，还活得挺累。

喝一口，那个味道怎么形容呢？像牛奶托梦跟你说："我走了，你要好好的。"

现在去咖啡店，店员都会问：“要不要换成植物奶？”我就想问，奶这个字，本来是动物的专利。你管这个叫奶，就像管塑料花叫鲜花，只是不好意思说它是假的。

这东西的流程是：把一堆能磨的东西泡水里，磨碎，过滤，然后宣布：这是奶。那我家洗米水是不是也能申请一下？

更离谱的是还要加价，多收我三块。我没喝牛的，反而更贵？原来环保就是让我的钱包先减排。

我还认真看了配料表：水、一点原料、增稠剂、乳化剂、香精。也就是说，人类动用了整个化学系，才模仿出一头牛天生就会的事。

牛要是知道了，估计都得感动：“原来你们这么努力地想我。”

Casino cities are what happens when a town looks at its own reflection and says, "What if we were a hangover?" Everything is open 24 hours, because nothing good happens at a reasonable time. There are no clocks and no windows, just carpet designed by someone who lost a bet with a kaleidoscope. The buffet is "all you can eat," which is a dare, not a promise. Every hotel has a fountain, a fake skyline, and a guy dressed as a pirate who's clearly reconsidering his life choices.

And the math! The whole economy runs on people saying, "I'm up forty dollars, so the machine likes me." The machine doesn't like you. The machine is a refrigerator with a gambling problem and better lawyers.

You arrive with hope and a suitcase. You leave with a souvenir shot glass, a sunburn, and a deep new understanding of the word "variance."

现在去咖啡店，店员问我：“要不要换植物奶？加五块。”我就懵了，我花五块钱，是为了让奶里没有奶？

这东西还叫“奶”，牛同意了吗？你要是真有底气，就叫“植物浑浊水”，我看谁买。

而且现在什么都能榨成奶，磨碎，兑水，过滤，齐活。照这个标准，我把小区绿化带榨一榨，也能上架：“草坪奶，限定款，口感清新，带一点泥土的倔强。”

最离谱的是包装上写着“零乳糖，零胆固醇”。废话，它本来就没奶啊！这就好比卖拖鞋的在包装上写：“本产品不含脚气。”

你说它健康吧，配料表比我前任的借口还长。

Casino cities are what happen when a town looks at its own personality and says, "Let's replace that with a buffet." Every one of them is a desert mirage built on math. No clocks, no windows, and the carpet looks like a migraine that got a design degree. They pump in oxygen and pretend it's atmosphere. It's not atmosphere, it's a hostage situation with free ginger ale.

Their economy runs on one principle: hope is cheaper than a plane ticket home. Everybody's there to win, and the only guaranteed winner is the guy who owns the building shaped like a giant pyramid, castle, or other thing that has no business holding a slot machine.

And the tourism slogans! "What happens here stays here." Yes, because it's your savings account. Meanwhile, the locals drive past a replica Eiffel Tower to get to the dentist. It's the only place where you can lose your shirt, then pay twenty dollars for a shrimp cocktail to feel better about it.

Casino cities are what happens when a place looks at its own geography and says, "What if we built an adult Chuck E. Cheese, but the tickets are your rent?"

Every one of them is a desert, a swamp, or a parking lot with a dream. There's no sunlight, because sunlight lets you know it's Tuesday and you've been here since Friday.

The buffet is "all you can eat," which is the only gambling where you actually win something: salmonella.

The carpet looks like a migraine, designed so you can't look down and see what you've done with your life. The air smells like cigarettes, perfume, and the quiet despair of a man named Gary who is "up forty dollars" and has been for six hours.

And the hotels are gorgeous, because nothing says "we respect you" like a marble lobby paid for by your nephew's college fund.

The slogan is always "What happens here stays here," which is true, because so does your 401(k).

现在咖啡店点单，店员都会问：“要不要换植物奶，加五块。”我就想不通了，花五块钱，换的是什么？是口感吗？不是，是一种“我很环保”的感觉。这哪是奶，这是道德感拿铁，喝完不用买单，朋友圈替你结账。

你看那包装，写得特别努力：“零乳糖、零胆固醇、零负担。”零来零去，我就想问，有东西吗？

最绝的是它还管自己叫“奶”。牛奶是牛生产的，它呢？是一堆植物被打成浆，再被迫转行。这就好比我把黄瓜榨成汁，说这是“瓜妈妈的乳汁”，你敢喝吗？

可偏偏就有人喝得特别虔诚，喝一口还要说：“嗯，有股淡淡的……豆……坚果……草的灵魂。”兄弟，那叫“没味儿”。

Casino cities are what happens when a town says, "What if we built a place where time doesn't exist and neither does hope?" No clocks, no windows, just a carpet designed by someone who hates your eyes. It's the only place on Earth where a buffet is both the best deal in town and a cry for help.

Everything is "free." Free drinks, free rooms, free parking. Sure, and a bear trap comes with free cheese. They'll comp your suite because they've already calculated how much of your retirement they're taking home.

And the people-watching! A guy in a tuxedo T-shirt feeding twenties into a machine shaped like a cartoon wolf. A bachelorette party crying in a hallway. Somebody's grandmother, in the zone like a Navy SEAL, with an oxygen tank and a rewards card.

These cities have one business model: sell you the dream, then charge you for the nap.

我特别佩服赌城这种地方。进去没有窗户，没有钟，连个日出日落都不给你。人家怕你知道几点了。这比我妈管我还狠，我妈至少还会喊我回家吃饭。

而且赌城的自助餐都特别便宜，我一开始还挺感动，后来想明白了：这不是餐厅，这是加油站。吃饱了才有力气接着输。

还有筹码，你发现没有，它不叫钱，叫筹码。一块塑料片，扔出去一点都不心疼。让我一张张递现金，我手都哆嗦；换成塑料片，我能扔出个潇洒的弧线来。

最绝的是老虎机。赢一块钱，灯也闪，歌也唱，跟我中了五百万一样；输一百块，它一声不吭。这不就是我上一段感情吗？

人家还说，小赌怡情。我就想问，怡的是谁的情？反正肯定不是我的。

我特别佩服赌城这种地方。全世界最聪明的数学家坐一块儿，就为了一个目标：让你高高兴兴地把钱交出来。

进去没有窗户，没有钟。我以为是设计疏忽，后来明白了，人家是怕你想起来：哦，我该回家了。

还送免费饮料。我喝了一杯免费可乐，输了两千，这是我喝过最贵的可乐，还没气。

最贴心的是ATM机，就摆在赌桌旁边，像亲妈一样。你输光了一转身，它说：“儿子，不够再取点。”

所有人进去都说：我就玩一百。出来都说：我就差一百。

那酒店盖得金碧辉煌，我就想，这哪是酒店啊，这是用我的钱给我盖的墓，还留了张床，让我躺着瞻仰。

Planned capital cities are what happen when a committee says, "What if a city had no history, no personality, and no reason to exist?" Then everyone claps.

They're designed from above, which you can tell, because nobody who has ever walked anywhere was consulted. The boulevards are so wide that crossing the street is a three-day commitment. Everything is "a short walk" from everything else, if you're a camel.

There's always a giant empty plaza built for parades. Today it hosts one pigeon and a man selling flags to nobody.

The neighborhoods are labeled like a spreadsheet: Ministry Zone, Embassy Zone, Zone Where Fun Was Supposed To Go.

And the architect always says, "Wait until you see it from the air." Sir, I live on the ground. The air is not paying rent.

Meanwhile, the old cities everyone actually likes were built by accident, by drunks, near a river. That's the secret: charm can't be scheduled.

Planned capital cities are what happens when a government says, "What if a city had no past, no personality, and no reason to exist?" and then gives it a budget.

Every one of them looks incredible from a helicopter. That's because the architects designed them for helicopters. On the ground, you're a tiny sweaty ant crossing a twelve-lane boulevard to reach a ministry that's "just there," according to a map that lies about distance.

They're built around grand axes, vast plazas, and monuments to ideas nobody asked for. Meanwhile, there's no corner store, no good bar, and no street where anything unplanned has ever happened. Even the pigeons seem to have filed paperwork.

And the whole thing was finished in four years, which is why the first thing every resident learns is where the other city is, the real one, with food, where everyone flies out to on weekends.

It's urban planning by someone who has never actually met a person.

我特别佩服赌城的设计师。整个城市没有窗户，没有钟，连白天黑夜都给你取消了。这哪是度假，这是把你关进一个"时间不存在"的房间，还按小时收费。

而且那地方什么都是假的。假的金字塔，假的运河，天花板上画着假的蓝天。全城最真的东西，就是你卡里的余额，还是限时体验。

他们还免费送酒。一个商家请你喝酒，能图什么？图你喝完以后觉得"我再押一把，这次稳了"。这不叫赌博，这叫酒后融资。

最绝的是输光的人出门，还有九块九的自助餐等着，吃回本。先让你亏，再让你觉得吃饭能赚。

所以我觉得，这种地方不该叫赌城，应该叫"成年人自愿捐款处"。区别只是，别的地方捐款的人走的时候是平静的，这儿的人走的时候还在说："我就差一点。"

Planned capital cities are what happen when a government says, "What if a city had no past, no personality, and no reason to exist?" Then they hire an architect who's never been to a party.

Everything is built on a grid, so you can get lost with precision. There are wide boulevards designed for parades and traffic that never shows up. The city looks gorgeous from a helicopter, which is great, because nobody lives in a helicopter.

Every one has a monument to the future, built in 1960s concrete, which is how the future looked back then: sad and weirdly sloped.

Real cities grow from trade, rivers, and people making questionable decisions. These grew from a committee. You can tell because the nightlife closes at 9 p.m. and the best restaurant is inside a ministry.

They're the only places where the tour guide says, "And this empty field is where the culture will go."

Planned capital cities are what happens when a government says, "What if a city had no history, but we gave it a really big roundabout?"

They're designed from above, which is why they look great in the brochure and like a screensaver in person. Every one has a ceremonial avenue wide enough to land a plane, and nobody on it. You can see your destination from the hotel, but it's a forty-minute walk because the architect hated sidewalks.

The population is 90% civil servants, so the nightlife is a PowerPoint. The best restaurant is a hotel buffet. The "vibrant arts district" is a sculpture of an abstract idea, placed in a field.

Meanwhile, the old, chaotic city three hours away has the food, the music, and the personality. The planned capital has a master plan, and you can tell. It's the only place where getting lost feels like a clerical error.

我特别佩服赌城的设计师，他们能让你进去以后，彻底不知道现在几点。没窗户，没钟，灯光永远是下午三点的那种亮。这哪是酒店，这是让你想不起家里还有人的结界。

而且这种地方特别爱仿造。左边是假罗马，右边是假巴黎，中间一条假运河，头顶还飘着一片假天空。我就想，你们这么会造假，能不能顺手把我输的钱也造出来点？

还有免费饮料。你以为人家大方？钓鱼的也给鱼免费吃饵啊。

都说小赌怡情，对，怡的是老板的情。

最后你走出来，太阳一晃眼，你才恍然大悟：哦，原来外面还有天，是真的。

你们去过那种规划出来的首都吗？就是有人拿尺子在地图上一画：这儿政府区，这儿商业区，那儿生活区。生活还得单独分个区，你就知道这城市多不会生活。

航拍特别好看，横平竖直，像块电路板。可你走进去就明白了，人就是电路板上的电阻，还是接触不良的那种。

马路宽得离谱，过个街得带干粮。两栋楼看着挨着，走过去四十分钟，中途还得立遗嘱。

最惨是半夜饿了。别的城市下楼左转是烧烤摊，这儿下楼左转是一个巨大的广场，和一个巨大的月亮。想买包烟，得先申请一辆车。

人家老城市是先有人住，再有路。这种城市是先有路，再请人来住。就像请客吃饭，桌子摆了五百米长，客人还在路上。

Nothing says "I own my kitchen" like a machine that only works with pods sold by the people who made the machine. It's not an appliance, it's a subscription with a heating element.

You pay four dollars for a thimble of coffee, packaged in enough plastic to build a small Tupperware cathedral. Then you throw the pod away, because apparently the planet has a lot of room left.

And the machine itself? Sold at a loss, like a drug dealer's free sample. The real product is you, standing in the aisle, realizing your fancy gadget only accepts one brand of tiny cylinder, and that cylinder is out of stock.

Meanwhile, my grandmother made soup, bread, and a dozen kids' dinners with a pot and a spoon. Neither one ever required a firmware update.

Proprietary pods: because freedom is great, but have you tried paying monthly for hot water with flavor?

Nothing says "freedom" like owning a machine that only accepts snacks from its own parents.

You buy a coffee maker, and suddenly you're in a long-term relationship with a cardboard box. The machine costs forty bucks. The pods cost forty bucks a week. It's a printer with better PR.

And the pods! Each one is a tiny plastic thimble containing one-fifth of a spoonful of coffee, engineered by a team of forty people to be impossible to recycle. Somewhere, a landfill is hosting a thimble convention.

Then there's the "ecosystem." Ecosystem is a fancy word for "you can't leave." The smoothie pod doesn't fit the soup pod machine. The soup machine doesn't talk to the baby formula machine. Your counter looks like a hostage negotiation between small appliances.

And when the company discontinues your pod line? Congratulations, you own a very expensive, very loud paperweight that still blinks hopefully at you every morning.

你们去过那种规划出来的首都吗？就是一帮人坐在会议室里，拿尺子在地图上画出来的城市。从空中看，太美了，横平竖直，对称得像强迫症的梦。可是人不是住在空中的啊！

走在地上你就懂了，马路宽得像要起飞，过个斑马线我都想先办个签证。路边导航说“目的地就在前方”，我一看，前方四公里，中间一棵树都没有。

而且所有建筑都特别严肃，一栋楼写着“部”，另一栋楼写着“委”，连个卖煎饼的都没有。你想吃口热乎的，得先打车，打完车发现司机也是公务员。

晚上八点，整座城市安静得像被按了静音键。你在街上喊一声，回声都觉得尴尬：“不好意思，我也不是本地的。”

真正的城市是先有人活着，再有路。这种是先有路，再请人来假装生活。

你们去过那种“规划出来的首都”吗？就是一群人在会议室画张图：这儿放政府，这儿放议会，中间来一条特别宽的大街。画完，真建了。

那种城市马路宽得像跑道，我怀疑不是给车开的，是给外宾专机备降的。我过个马路，绿灯刚亮我就出发，走到一半红灯了，我在马路中间站着过了个年。

而且所有东西都对称，左边一个部委，右边一个部委，像强迫症摆的积木。

最绝的是晚上六点，公务员一下班，整座城市直接关机。我想找个夜宵摊，规划图上写着：“此处未来将有生活气息。”

未来？我现在就饿啊！

正常城市是先有人，后有路，路是人踩出来的。规划首都是先有路，再等人。那些路就在那儿干等着，特别尴尬，像办了一桌酒席，客人还在路上，而且没人确定他们真的会来。

Nothing says "I'm an adult" like paying forty dollars a month for a machine that only accepts its own little plastic thimbles.

These appliances are the printer ink scam, but with a smoothie. You buy the machine cheap, and then you're married to the pods forever. It's a razor-and-blades business model where the razor makes coffee and the blades are a tiny landfill.

And the pods! Each one contains roughly one tablespoon of something, wrapped in the packaging of a space shuttle component. Somewhere a engineer spent six months designing a foil lid that you'll peel off in two seconds and throw away.

Then the company discontinues your machine, and suddenly you own a very expensive paperweight that smells faintly of hazelnut.

You could make the same thing with a spoon, some beans, and hot water. But no, we need a gadget that connects to Wi-Fi to tell us the pod is empty. Sir, I can see that. I'm holding it. It's light.

Nothing says "I love convenience" like paying four dollars for a thimble of coffee that comes in a plastic tomb the size of a hot tub for ants.

These machines only eat their own brand of pod, like a picky toddler with a lawyer. You can't use regular coffee. You can't use regular detergent. You can't use regular anything. It's the only relationship where you're legally required to buy your partner's special food.

And the pods! Each one is a tiny, non-recyclable sculpture titled "Guilt." Your trash can looks like a Lego store after an earthquake.

The machine breaks after fourteen months, and the replacement uses a *different* pod. Of course it does. That's not an appliance, that's a subscription with a heating element.

My grandmother made coffee with a pot, a flame, and spite. It was free, and it had flavor.

有些国家嫌老首都太乱，干脆推倒重画一个。从零开始，功能分区：政府区、商业区、居住区，整整齐齐。从天上看，像一只展翅的大鸟，特别美。但设计师是给坐飞机的人设计的啊，住在里面的人没有翅膀！

马路宽得像跑道，绿灯亮了，我走到一半，下一个红灯都快来了。隔壁部门明明就在眼前，走过去要四十分钟，因为中间隔着一块“未来的商业区”，现在叫草坪。

规划师还安慰我：烟火气会有的，慢慢来。可烟火气这东西，是人乱来乱出来的！你每一块地都规定好了用途，连个卖煎饼的位置都没留。

所以下班以后，全城只有一个活动：回家。因为这座城市唯一的夜生活，就是路灯。

Let's talk about divisive footwear. You know the type: shoes people either worship or want banned by city ordinance. There's no middle ground. Nobody says, "Those are fine."

These shoes have a fanbase with the energy of a cult that meets in a parking lot. They'll tell you the comfort is life-changing, and you'll nod, because you don't want to be recruited.

The rest of us just stare at them like someone showed up to a wedding in a snorkel. Meanwhile, the wearer is glowing, saying, "My arches have never been happier." Sir, your arches don't have feelings, and they're not the ones people are looking at.

Every one of these brands has the same business model: make something so strange that half the world argues about it online. It's marketing by feud. They don't need ads. They need you to type, "Who is this for?" in the comments.

Spoiler: it's for them. It's always been for them.

现在的厨房电器，最狠的不是贵，是便宜。机器卖你一百九十九，还包邮，我都怀疑老板是不是倒贴。后来才明白，人家根本不是卖电器，人家是卖“会员”。机器是门票，耗材才是正片。

说明书第一页就写着：本机仅支持原厂专用配件。什么意思？就是这台机器只跟原配谈恋爱。你想换个别家的，它立马亮灯报警，那个感叹号就像前任发来的消息：“你变了。”

最离谱的是那一小包专用耗材，比我午饭还贵。我算了一下，我不是买了台电器，我是领养了个孩子，还是每个月都得交学费的那种。

而且它特别会过日子：机器能用十年，耗材三年停产。到最后机器摆在台面上，像块纪念碑，上面写着：“这里，曾经有爱。”

Let's talk about divisive footwear. You know the type: shoes people either love or hate, with no middle ground. Nobody has ever said, "Oh, those? They're fine."

These shoes are a personality test you wear on your feet. Someone walks in wearing them and you instantly learn three things: their opinions, their confidence level, and how much they enjoy telling you about arch support.

The owners always say, "They're so comfortable." Sure, so is a bathtub, but I don't wear that to a wedding.

And the defense is always the same: "You just have to try them." No, I don't. I've never tried a sword either, and I'm doing great.

Half the world sees a fashion statement. The other half sees a clerical error at the factory. Meanwhile your feet are in there like, "Please, we have rights."

But hey, commit to the look. Nothing says confidence like walking into a room and making everyone quietly check your ankles for a court-ordered monitor.

现在有一类厨房电器，特别会做生意。机器本身卖得便宜，便宜到你都替老板担心：这是不是亏了？你别替他操心，人家不是卖电器的，人家是发展下线的。你买回家的不是电器，是个充值入口。

最绝的是那个"专用"。什么叫专用？就是全世界的东西它都能用，唯独不让你用别的。你拿个差不多的试试，它立马亮灯报警："检测到非原装。"一台电器，比丈母娘还挑。

耗材包装得跟首饰一样，小小一个，按克算比黄金还贵。我就纳闷，我这是做饭呢，还是养了个电子宠物？不喂就罢工，还得是指定口粮。

所以我现在买电器，先不看功能，就问一句：这东西需要续费吗？需要，我不买。我家已经有一个要不断充值才肯干活的了，我的健身卡。

现在的厨房电器都学会了一招：机器便宜，甚至送你，钱全在后面。

盒子上写着“一键搞定”。对，就一键，但前提是你得买它指定的胶囊、料包、原装滤芯。你以为自己买了个电器，其实是办了张会员卡，还是铁疙瘩材质的，占台面。

最气人的是，那个耗材跟普通东西就差两毫米，你拿别的怎么都塞不进去。这不叫设计，这叫在锁孔里请了个门卫。

我算过账，用它一年，耗材的钱够我把厨房重新装修一遍。机器倒是一直很耐用，毕竟它不能坏，它坏了谁来消耗我呢？

这玩意儿跟谈恋爱一样，前期特别大方，什么都送你，等你离不开了，开始一笔一笔收。

到最后我才明白，那机器不是我买的，是我入职的。我就是它的耗材，还是原装的。

现在有一类厨房电器，特别会做生意。机器本身便宜得离谱，抱回家还觉得自己赚了。结果一拆开，说明书第一句："请使用原厂专用耗材。"

这哪是买电器啊，这是领养孩子。机器是白送的，耗材是每个月的奶粉钱。而且这孩子只认亲妈的奶粉，你给它换个别家的，它直接亮红灯，滴滴滴，翻译过来就是："你是不是外面有人了？"

最离谱的是那个耗材，小小一个，包装得跟首饰似的，一个顶我一顿午饭。我算了笔账，用一年，耗材的钱够再买三台机器。

所以这根本不是电器，是会员卡。办卡免费，充值无底洞。最后你还会发现，自己不是在做饭，是在给人家的 KPI 做饭。

Divisive footwear brands are the only products where the customer base is half cult, half hostage negotiation. You either wear them proudly or you stand ten feet away, whispering "why?" like you're watching someone eat soup with a fork.

These shoes show up at a party and immediately split the room into two political parties. One side says, "They're so comfortable!" The other side says, "So is a bathtub, but I don't wear that to brunch."

Owners will tell you the shoes are "an experience." Sir, so is a root canal.

They're always either shaped like a loaf of bread, a boat, or a sad dolphin. And the price? Somehow both ridiculous and non-negotiable. You're paying premium money for a shoe that looks like it was designed during a fire drill.

But hey, nothing says confidence like walking into a room and having everyone's eyes drop to your feet and then slowly rise back up, full of questions.

Divisive footwear brands are the only products where the marketing strategy is "half of you will scream at us, and honestly, that's the business model." Their shoes look like they were designed during a dare. You either wear them with fanatical devotion or cross the street to avoid them.

And the fans! They're never just customers. They're a cult with arch support. Ask them why they own six pairs, and they say "comfort," while their face says "hostage."

Meanwhile, the haters make it their whole personality. Nobody has ever calmly said, "Not for me." It's always a TED Talk about your feet.

These brands treat "ugly" as a feature. "It's not that we can't design a normal shoe. We just chose violence."

Somewhere there's a boardroom of people high-fiving over a cease-and-desist from good taste.

现在有种鞋特别两极分化。喜欢的人说：“你不懂，这是灵魂的舒服。”不喜欢的人说：“这不是鞋，这是脚的事故现场。”

最离谱的是，穿的人还觉得自己有态度。哥们，那不是态度，是你的脚在求救。

我朋友买了一双，说穿上以后感觉被全世界包容了。对，全世界确实包容你，因为大家都不想跟你说实话。

这种鞋现在最大的功能就是筛人。大街上两个人一对视，先看脚，然后点头，要么是同类，要么是想报警。

相亲就更方便了，都不用聊，低头一看，价值观合不合，三秒出结果。

Board games are the only hobby where you spend ninety minutes reading rules, forty minutes arguing about the rules, and then discover you misread the rules at the start. Nothing says "family bonding" like watching your dad flip a table over plastic houses.

Every box promises "fun for ages 8 and up," but the game lasts six hours and ends when someone cries or the dog eats a piece. Speaking of pieces: there are always exactly one fewer than you need. You're playing with a button, a coin, and a tiny hat your cousin swears is "close enough."

And the box lid? Designed to rip at the corners the moment you open it, then stored on a shelf where it supports the weight of eleven other boxes and its own regrets.

Board games: proof that humans will invent elaborate suffering, then call it a Friday night.

Classic board games are the only products where the instructions say "ages 8 and up" and the experience says "ruins friendships forever." Every box promises family fun, and every family ends up screaming over a missing piece that is definitely under the couch with the dog's chewed-up remote.

The rules are twelve pages long, written by someone who hates you, and the one person who read them is a dad who now acts like a Supreme Court justice. "Actually, page nine, subsection C says you lose a turn." Sir, it's a Tuesday.

And the games last four hours, but you only learn on hour three that you lost in the first ten minutes. You're not playing anymore. You're a hostage with a little plastic hat.

The box is the best part, honestly. Nothing fits back in after you open it. It's a suitcase packed by a toddler, and it lives in a closet until the next power outage.

现在有一种鞋，特别两极分化。喜欢的人说：“太舒服了，我想穿着它走完这一生。”不喜欢的人说：“你离我远点，我还要吃饭。”

最神奇的是，从来没人说“还行吧”。这种鞋不是信仰，就是案发现场。

穿的人还特别爱安利：“你试试，真的舒服！”我说我不试。他说：“你试了就知道了。”大哥，这是鞋，不是传销，我凭什么先交一只脚？

而且人一穿上就变了，特别坦然。以前出门还化个妆，现在整个人写着一行字：“我已经想通了，你们随意。”

后来我明白了，丑不是缺点，是门槛。丑到一定程度，穿的人自动成党。大街上两个人撞鞋，互相点点头，不说话，跟地下组织接头一样。

我就站在旁边，穿着一双“还行吧”的鞋，突然觉得自己像个叛徒。

现在有一类鞋，特别有意思，叫“两极分化”。就是这鞋一出现，全世界立刻分成两派。

穿的人说：“太舒服了！你试试，你试一下就回不去了！”这话听着耳熟吗？这不是穿鞋，这是传销。

不穿的人说：“丑，丑得我眼睛疼。”还有人更狠：“我宁愿光脚。”兄弟，光脚你也不一定赢，人家穿的人是真舒服，你光脚是真硌脚。

最离谱的是，这两派还都特别真诚。穿的人觉得自己是在传福音，看的人觉得自己是在报警。

然后你发现，最后买单的往往是第三种人：本来没想买，就是为了在评论区反驳对方，说“我就试一双，我客观评价一下”。结果穿上说：“嗯，真香。”然后继续说：“但还是丑。”

这就是这类鞋的最高境界：让你一边穿着它，一边骂它。

你们有没有发现，现在有一类鞋，全世界对它只有两种态度：爱，和报警。

穿的人说：“你不懂，舒服！”我懂，我看得出来你舒服，你脸上写着“我已经放弃了”。

这种鞋的设计理念很特别，它不是让你好看，是帮你筛选朋友。你一穿出来，谁真心谁假意，立马分清。真朋友会憋半天说：“你这鞋……挺有个性的。”这句话翻译过来就是：“我需要时间处理一下。”

最离谱的是，每次大家都说它要过气了，结果过两年它又回来了，更丑了，还联名了。联名你知道吧？就是丑，但是贵。

所以穿这种鞋的人，都有一种迷之自信。你不用问他，他脚下那一双就是他的态度：“我不怕你们看，我就怕脚累。”

这不是鞋，这是一份声明。

Classic board games are the only products where "some assembly required" means a 40-page rulebook written by a lawyer who hates you. Every box promises "fun for the whole family" and delivers a three-hour hostage negotiation with your cousin over whether that counts.

The game pieces are tiny, designed specifically to be lost, and the one you need is always in the vacuum cleaner. The dice roll under the couch, where they join the dice from 1997. The box lid is held together by tape and denial.

These games were built for a simpler time, when entertainment meant waiting your turn for forty minutes while someone counts out play money slowly, like a hostage negotiator.

And the rules? Nobody's ever read them. We play by "how Dad remembers it," which is wrong, but he'll die on that hill.

Somehow, we keep buying them. Every holiday, new box, same fight. It's not a game. It's a family therapy session with a spinner.

Classic board games are the only products where the instructions say "fun for the whole family" and the real outcome is a family meeting with a lawyer. You open the box and it smells like 1987 and disappointment. Half the pieces are missing, and the replacements are a button, a Lego, and your cousin's retainer.

The rules are 40 pages long, written by someone who hates you. Every game has that one guy who "just needs to check the rulebook" for 45 minutes. Meanwhile the game takes four hours, and the winner was decided in the first ten minutes. You just keep playing out of politeness, like a hostage situation with cardboard money.

And the dice! Your entire fate depends on a tiny plastic cube that rolls under the couch, where it joins the other dice from every game you've ever owned. Nobody's winning. We're all just waiting for someone to flip the table so we can go home.

你们发现没有，经典桌游都是"经典"到没人想玩，但过年必须玩。

每次家里聚会，总有个长辈从柜子里掏出一盒，盒子软得像被踩过，打开一看，少了一个小人，骰子是拿麻将牌代替的。然后开始读规则，说明书四十页，全家只有我二舅读过，还是二十年前的版本。所以我们家的规则叫"二舅说了算"。

玩到一半，人都变了。平时温柔的表姐，为了棋盘上一个格子，把亲弟弟逼得原地蹲了三轮，还说"游戏而已"。游戏而已？你刚才数格子的时候眼睛都是红的！

最离谱的是时长。盒子上写"约60分钟"，我们从年三十玩到初二，没分出胜负。最后不是谁赢了，是大家饿了，宣布平局。

所以经典桌游根本不是用来玩的，是用来检验亲情的。能玩完一局不掀桌子的，才是真亲戚。

Speculative collectibles are the only hobby where you buy something you love, then never touch it because you're afraid to ruin the thing you bought to enjoy. It's a pet rock with a retirement plan.

Everyone says "it's an investment." Sure. Your portfolio is a closet of sealed boxes, and your financial advisor is a guy in a forum named "TruthSeeker_99."

The pitch is always the same: "Limited edition!" Limited to what? Eleven million units? That's not scarcity, that's a Tuesday.

And the plastic sleeves. Nobody protects their actual valuables like this. My grandmother's wedding ring wasn't in a UV-resistant acrylic case, but a cartoon cardboard rectangle is?

Then comes the grand finale: the market crashes, and you're stuck holding a warehouse of "future heirlooms" that your kids will politely donate to a thrift store, where a stranger will buy them for a dollar and actually play with them.

Which, honestly, is the only return anyone ever gets.

Speculative collectibles are the only hobby where you spend your life savings on something, then are legally forbidden from enjoying it. "Don't open it! Don't touch it! Don't breathe near it!" You didn't buy a toy, you bought a very small hostage.

Every collector says, "It's not about the money," while checking the price four times a day like a nervous parent at a recital.

And the pitch is always the same: "They'll be worth a fortune someday." Someday! The most dangerous word in finance. It's the same logic as buying a lottery ticket, except the ticket is a plastic figurine in a sealed box that smells like regret.

The whole market runs on one belief: that a stranger in the future will love this thing more than you do. You're not investing, you're writing a love letter to a guy who doesn't exist yet.

And when he finally shows up, he'll say, "Is this worth anything?" And you'll say, "It was."

现在的经典桌游，我真的服了。盒子上写着"2到8人，适合全家"，翻译一下：适合全家一起吵架。

每次开玩之前，必须有个人研究规则，那个人一般是我爸。他看说明书的认真劲儿，比当年看我成绩单还认真。我们在旁边等了四十分钟，手机刷到电量变红，他抬起头说："行，大概明白了。"大概！

开局又发现少了一颗骰子。整个盒子里塞得满满当当，就缺最关键的那个。最后我们拿一颗花生米顶上，结果谁掷出花生米，谁就是全场最大的赢家，因为大家想吃。

玩到一半，我姑说："我们家规则不一样。"好家伙，这不是桌游，这是联合国，每家一部宪法。

所以经典桌游最大的功能，就是让一家人坐在同一张桌子上，各自想回家。

你们发现没有，经典桌游的盒子上，永远印着一家四口，笑得特别灿烂，一看就是花钱请的演员。真实情况是，玩到第二个小时，妈妈把牌摔了，爸爸说"不玩了"，孩子在哭，而游戏还没有结束。因为经典桌游有个特点：它不会结束，只会被中途掀桌。

还有那本说明书，十二页，字比药品说明书还小，全家没人看过。每次都靠一个亲戚说"我小时候是这么玩的"。结果每个人小时候的玩法都不一样。开局前先吵半小时，吵什么呢？立法。

最绝的是，打开盒子，永远少一个小零件。于是一家人拿个瓶盖当棋子，继续玩。这哪是娱乐啊，这是考古，我们是在复原一个已经失传的文明。

Nothing says "financial genius" like buying a limited edition thing whose entire value depends on strangers being dumber than you in the future. That's not investing, that's a chain letter with a cardboard box.

You keep it in mint condition, sealed in plastic, locked away where nobody can enjoy it. Congratulations, you've invented a pet that's dead but needs a climate-controlled apartment.

The packaging says "Limited Edition." Limited to what? Every person who read that sentence and thought, "Me, I'm the smart one"?

And the pitch is always the same: "This will be worth a fortune in twenty years." Sir, in twenty years you'll be explaining to your spouse why the garage has a better humidity setting than the nursery.

The only guaranteed return is a very detailed spreadsheet and a dead-eyed stare at the closet. Meanwhile, your retirement plan has a barcode and a tiny "collect them all!" on the back.

Speculative collectibles are the only hobby where you spend your retirement on something and then are told, "Whatever you do, don't enjoy it." Don't open it. Don't touch it. Don't look at it too long, because your eyes have oils.

It's a sealed box of potential. That's all it is. You're not a collector, you're a landlord for a plastic tenant who pays no rent and judges you silently from a shelf.

Every one comes with a story: "They'll be worth a fortune someday." Someday is doing so much work in that sentence. Someday is the most overleveraged word in the English language.

And the market is a beautiful system. Everyone's waiting for someone dumber to show up. It's a chain letter with better packaging. When the bubble pops, you won't have an investment. You'll have a very well-preserved lesson, in mint condition, and for the first time, you'll actually want to throw it away.

所有"经典桌游"都有同一个设计理念：折磨。

先说盒子，大得像搬家。打开三百个小零件，永远少一颗棋子，最后拿个瓶盖顶上，玩得像考古现场。

规则书二十页，一看就是法务写的。全桌人等那个"我来讲一下"的人，他讲了二十分钟，说："边玩边学吧。"那你讲这二十分钟干嘛？

包装上写"30到60分钟"，我们玩了四个小时。因为这种游戏，输的人早就输了，但规则不让他走。他还得假装很投入，像参加自己的葬礼。

为什么叫经典？就是一百年没人敢改。bug不修，叫传统。

最后总有人掀桌。不是游戏好玩，是终于有了吵架的理由。

现在有一种东西，叫“投机性收藏品”。买的人说：“这是热爱。”卖的人说：“这是投资。”结果谁也没拿它干过正事。

它的价值全靠一句话：“以后会更值钱。”以后是哪天？没人知道，反正比你的房贷短不了。

而且这东西你不能用。一拆封就贬值，所以买回来只能供着。花钱买个东西，最后自己成了东西的保安。

最离谱的是“限量”。限量一万个，意思就是一万个人坐在家里，互相等着对方来接盘。这不叫收藏，这叫击鼓传花，只不过鼓一停，你手里这个还带防尘盒。

我朋友说他不是炒，是“长期持有”。我说，长期持有，就是被套住了的文明说法。

他还不服，说：“你不懂，这是情怀。”行，情怀好，情怀不用交易手续费，就是赎不回来。

我特别不理解那种"投资型收藏"。买回来不用、不拆、不摸，还得恒温恒湿地供着，比我妈对我都上心。

我问他图啥，他说升值。我说那你喜欢吗？他说："不重要，重要的是别人喜欢。"

好家伙，你买了个东西，还雇了全世界替你喜欢。

这类东西的宣传语永远是"限量"。限量多少？一万件。一万件也好意思叫限量？这不叫限量，这叫工厂今天干到这儿，下班了。

最惨的是，大家都在等下一个人接盘，就是击鼓传花，只不过这花特别贵，还不能闻。

鼓一停，花在你手里，价值归零。可你还不能扔，因为你已经跟你老婆说了，这叫"资产"。

现在有一种东西，叫“投机性收藏品”。这名字很诚实：一半投机，一半收藏，唯独没有“使用”。

买的时候，卖家说：“限量的，以后肯定升值。”我问限量多少，他说一万件。一万件你管它叫稀有？我们小区业主群都不止一万人。

而且这东西你还不能碰。不能拆，不能摸，不能对着它呼气。花大价钱买回来，结果自己成了它的保安。

最绝的是，每个人都说“我是真喜欢才买的”。可他们盯的不是东西，是价格曲线。真喜欢一个东西，谁天天看K线啊？

说白了，这就是现代版击鼓传花，只不过那朵花是塑封的，还带编号。鼓一停，你手里捧着的，就叫“情怀”。

Workplace chat software promised to kill email. Congratulations, it did. Now we have email, plus a thing that screams at us in real time.

Remember when you could ignore a coworker for three hours? Now there's a little green dot snitching on you. "Active" just means my laptop's open and I'm staring at a wall.

And the typing indicator. Three dots appear. Disappear. Appear again. Somebody in accounting is writing a novel, deleting it, and settling on "Sounds good!"

Every company has that one channel called "random" that's seventy percent birthday GIFs and thirty percent a guy named Doug posting articles nobody asked for.

We've got threads, side threads, threads about threads. A simple question like "What time's the meeting?" generates forty replies, six thumbs-ups, and a raised-hands emoji from someone who wasn't invited.

It's a tool designed to save time, and it's very good at it. It just immediately hands that time to a notification that says "Quick question?" which has never once been quick.

Workplace chat software promised to kill email. Congratulations, it did. Now instead of one inbox you ignore, you have fourteen channels you ignore, each with a red notification badge screaming like a toddler at a funeral.

Everything's "quick question." Nobody has ever asked a quick question. Nobody types "hey" and then waits. Just "hey." Like a hostage note from someone who needs a spreadsheet.

The green dot means I'm available. The green dot is a lie. The green dot means my laptop is open and I'm in the bathroom.

Threads were supposed to organize conversation. Instead, we've got seventeen replies deep on a lunch order, while the actual layoff announcement is buried under a thumbs-up emoji.

And the search function? Unmatched. I can find a typo from 2019, but never the file Dave swore he posted "right here."

We didn't build better communication. We built a way to be interrupted by people we like, about things we don't care about, at all hours.

现在有一种东西，叫"投机性收藏品"。翻译成人话就是：没人想用，但人人都想转手。

正常东西是买来用的，这种是买来"等"的。等什么？等一个比我更傻的人。学名叫"博傻"，听着像个游戏，玩的时候也确实挺像。

还有人买回来不拆封。花大价钱买个东西，原封不动供着，这跟一块砖有什么区别？不对，砖还能盖房子。

我朋友跟我说："这个以后肯定值钱。"我问："以后是多久？"他说："等我卖出去那天。"

他还问我：你懂不懂收藏？我懂。收藏就是把钱变成一堆东西，然后用余生祈祷它们变回钱。

Workplace chat software promised to kill email. Congratulations, it did. Now we have email, plus a thousand tiny emails that scream at us in real time.

Nothing says "productivity" like a red bubble with a number on it. Forty-seven unread messages! Forty-six are thumbs-up emojis. One is Gary asking if anyone has "a quick sec," which is how every horror movie starts.

Every company has a channel called "random," where one guy posts a link to an article about sourdough, and nobody has ever responded, and he's never stopped.

And the green dot! The little light that says "I'm available," or in practice, "I'm trapped." Step away to use the bathroom and suddenly you've gone yellow, and your manager is watching you like a nature documentary.

We built a tool so we'd never have to have meetings. Now we have meetings to discuss what was said in the chat.

Workplace chat software promised to kill email. Congratulations, it did. Now instead of one inbox you ignore, you have forty channels you ignore, each with a little red badge screaming for attention like a toddler at a funeral.

Remember when a colleague could just walk over and ask you something? Now they type "Hey," and then vanish. Just "Hey." No question. Just a cliffhanger. I've aged six years waiting for the dot-dot-dot to resolve.

And the green status light! A tiny dot that says, "I'm available," when what I mean is, "I'm physically here but spiritually in witness protection."

Every channel is named something like "general-random-announcements-misc," where a thread about a birthday cake has 214 replies, and the one message about the server being on fire got a thumbs-up emoji.

It's not communication. It's a 24/7 group project where everyone's talking and nobody's working.

现在上班最大的变化，就是老板不用走过来了，他只需要@你。

手机一震，红点，点开，就俩字：“在吗？”

这俩字比“你被开除了”还吓人，因为你不知道后面是什么。可能是改方案，可能是催周报，也可能他就是手滑。

还有那个“已读”，太缺德了。我看了没回，他知道；我回“收到”，他回“好的”，我再回个“👌”。两个成年人为了结束对话，互相发了十分钟表情包，下班路上还在互道“不客气”。

最离谱的是工作群，三百个人，一个人讲话，剩下二百九十九个在接龙“收到”。

这哪是沟通啊，这是集体点名。

Document preparation systems promise you'll just type and it'll look professional. Then you insert one picture and the entire document has a stroke. The image jumps to page nine, the bullet points breed, and a heading you never touched turns into a ransom note.

These systems come in two flavors. In the first, what you see is what you get, except what you get is never what you wanted. In the second, you write code to make a paragraph, and one missing bracket gives you an error message in the language of a dying star.

Every one of them has a "styles" menu nobody understands, and a page break that shows up exactly when you delete the thing it was breaking.

You came to write a memo. You'll leave as a typesetter, an exorcist, and a person who just whispered "please" to a margin.

Document preparation systems promise you'll focus on your ideas. Then you spend six hours convincing a picture to stay on the same page as the sentence that mentions it. The picture has its own plans. It floats. Everything in these programs floats except your deadline, which is anchored.

Some systems are "what you see is what you get," which is a bold claim from software that shows you one thing on screen and prints another.
