Others make you write code first, then compile your essay, like it's a rocket. One missing bracket and you get an error message written in what I can only call ancient Sumerian.

And the bullet point! You press Enter, and it's indented. Press backspace, and it's gone, along with the formatting of the entire document. Now your title is in a font that doesn't exist.

We didn't make paper obsolete. We just made it harder to align.

办公聊天软件最大的发明，是“在吗”。两个字，没下文。你回“在”，他不说事；你不回，软件告诉他：对方已读。好家伙，等于每人脖子上挂了个监控。

最恐怖是下班后，手机“叮”一声，红点99+，点进去，群里三百人，二百九十九个在发“收到”，剩一个发“👌”。没一个人干活，但所有人都很忙。

领导还爱发语音，一发59秒。不点开，它就在那儿挂着；点开，前40秒全是“呃……那个……”。

最绝的是撤回功能。屏幕上写着“某某撤回了一条消息”，这比不撤回还吓人。全群都在想：他刚才到底说了啥？然后三百个人，同时回了一句：“收到。”

现在上班最累的不是干活，是那句“在吗”。就俩字，没标点，没内容，比恐怖片还吓人。我赶紧回“在”，屏幕上跳出“对方正在输入……”。输入了五分钟，发来三个字：没事了。我这五分钟心跳一百二，他就一句没事了？

还有那个“已读”，谁发明的？这不叫功能，这叫电子手铐。我不是不回，我是在组织语言，我得想怎么回一个“收到”，既显得积极，又不像答应了什么。

最可怕是下班以后，手机一震，红点，我手比脑子快，点开了。领导说：“明天说。”明天说，你今天发什么？你这不是发消息，你这是往我晚饭里撒沙子。

现在上班最累的不是干活，是“在吗”。老板发俩字，后面没了。我说在吧，怕他派活；说不在吧，我头像还亮着。

还有那个“已读”，我已读不回，不是没礼貌，是在组织语言，组织完发现，只能回俩字：收到。

现在全公司就会三句话：收到、好的、辛苦了。吵架也这样，“收到。”“好的。”这比骂人狠多了。

最绝的是下班，手机一震，99+，点进去全是“@所有人，请知悉”。我知悉了，我周末没了。

还有人发错群，手快撤回，系统还贴心提示“某某撤回了一条消息”。平时没人看群，那一秒，全员在线。

Document preparation systems promise you'll just type words and they'll make it pretty. Then you spend four hours figuring out why one paragraph is indented like it's hiding from the others.

You move one image and the whole document rearranges itself like a toddler flipping a board game. There's a table of contents that updates automatically, except when it doesn't, and you'll never learn why. The page break appears exactly where you didn't ask for it, and vanishes where you begged for it.

Some systems are WYSIWYG, which stands for "What You See Is What You Get," a lie so confident it should run for office. Others make you write code to get a bold word, which is like being asked to build a car so you can drive to the mailbox.

And the formatting? Haunted. Delete one invisible character and everything turns purple.

Document preparation systems promise you'll "focus on content." Then you spend six hours on why the figure appears on page nine when you put it on page two. The figure isn't lost. It's floating. It has chosen freedom.

These systems fall into two camps. In the first, you click a button and the whole document rearranges itself like a haunted house. In the second, you write code to make a paragraph, and one missing bracket produces an error message that reads like a ransom note from a Victorian ghost.

Every one of them has a "simple" mode that handles about four things and a "powerful" mode that handles everything except what you need.

And the page numbers? Always wrong. The table of contents? Always confident, and wrong.

You didn't write a document. You negotiated with a bureaucrat who prints.

我发现排版系统这东西，本质上就是跟一个特别有主见的实习生合租。你只想把一张图往左挪两毫米，它说行，然后第三页的字全搬去第九页了。你问它为什么，它说：这是自动的。

我现在一听“自动”两个字就发怵。在排版里，自动的意思就是它说了算。

有的系统号称所见即所得，可我看见的和我得到的，从来没见过面。屏幕上好好的，一打印，页码自己开了个派对。

还有的更狠，要你写代码。你以为自己成程序员了，结果为了一个标题居中，查了四十分钟，最后发现是少了个括号。凌晨两点，我一个成年人，在跟一个标题道歉。

最后老板来一句：“就改一个字。”就一个字！多一个字，多出一行；多出一行，图掉下一页；图一掉，整本书重新来过。

这哪是排版啊，这是搭积木，还是别人踢一脚就全倒的那种。

排版系统这类东西，本质上不是工具，是个有脾气的室友。

我说：“这张图放这儿。”它说：“好的。”然后放到了下一页。

我说：“不是，我要它在这儿。”它说：“明白。”然后把整段文字也请到了下一页。

最离谱的是“所见即所得”。我见到的，从来不是我得到的。屏幕上好好的，一打印全变样。这不叫所见即所得，这叫所见即所骗。

我为了对齐一行字，按了十七下空格。别人一打开，那行字像喝多了，歪在角落。

我就加了一个逗号，整篇文章像地震后重建：标题在第三页，页码在第五页，我的尊严在第零页。

Nanomaterials: the only industry where "it's incredibly small" is both the product and the excuse. Every press release says "revolutionary," and every follow-up says "promising in mice."

They've been about to change everything since 1995. Stronger than steel! Lighter than air! Cheaper than... well, we'll get back to you on that. Currently priced at roughly one kidney per gram.

The lab demo is always flawless. Then someone says "let's make a pound of it," and suddenly the miracle needs a clean room, a PhD, and a prayer. It works perfectly in a sample you need a microscope to find. Convenient! Can't prove it's not working if you can't see it.

And the funding pitches: "This will revolutionize medicine, energy, computing, and sunscreen." Sunscreen! Your world-changing breakthrough ended up in lotion.

Twenty-five years, billions of dollars, and the biggest consumer impact is a tennis racket that's slightly stiffer.

Truly, the biggest thing about nanomaterials is the hype.

Nanomaterials: the only industry where "it's very small" counts as a business model.

Every one of them was going to change everything. Cure cancer, power your phone for a year, make bridges out of pencil lead. Then you read the fine print: "Results observed once, in a lab in 2009, at minus 200 degrees, by a guy named Dennis."

They're always "a revolutionary breakthrough" in the press release and "not yet scalable" in the footnotes. Scalable is science for "we made enough to fill a thimble and cried."

And the pitch decks! "Stronger than steel, lighter than air, conducts electricity, also heals your emotional wounds." Sir, it's a smudge.

Meanwhile, the actual products are sunscreen and tennis rackets. We promised a space elevator and delivered a slightly less greasy lotion.

But sure, give them another grant. This time it's 10,000 times thinner, which is exactly how I feel about my patience.

你们用过排版系统吧？就是那种你以为自己在写东西，其实是在跟一个有脾气的室友合租的东西。

有一类叫“所见即所得”。我看见的是图片在这一页，我得到的是图片在下一页，这一页留一大片空白，像是在向极简主义致敬。我就想把图往上挪一厘米，整篇文档像多米诺骨牌一样倒下，目录跑到封面上，页码变成罗马数字。我就改了一个逗号啊！

还有一类更硬核，要你写代码，再编译成文档。它的报错特别真诚：“第47行有问题。”我跑到第47行，没毛病。它又说：“我的意思是，第47行附近的某个地方，具体你自己悟。”

用到最后你会明白，排版系统的哲学就一句话：

你以为是你在排版，其实是它在排你。

我发现排版系统分两种。一种叫“所见即所得”，前提是你什么都别碰。你想把一张图往左挪两毫米，整页文字像受惊的鸽子，哗一下全飞到下一页去了。

另一种更高级，得先写代码再编译。它的逻辑是：我不信你的审美，我只信你的语法。你少个括号，它甩你四十行报错，第一行写着“意外的结尾”。我说我也很意外。

最气的是自动编号。它自动，但不对。你删一段，它从3直接跳到7，你问它，它说：“系统自有安排。”

排版，说白了就是跟一个毫无审美、但极有主见的东西合租。

后来我学聪明了：想对齐，就狂按空格；想换页，就狂按回车。

系统不吭声，但我知道，它在记仇。

Nanomaterials: the only industry where "it's really small" counts as a business model. Every press release says the same thing: "This could revolutionize medicine, energy, and computing!" Could. Could is doing more heavy lifting than the material is.

They're always one breakthrough away. Ten years ago, they were going to cure cancer, power your phone for a month, and build an elevator to space. Today they're in a tennis racket and some sunscreen.

And the lab results! "Incredible properties," they say, "at scale of nine atoms, in a vacuum, at minus 270 degrees, in one grad student's hands, on a Tuesday." Scale it up and it behaves like a Tuesday.

Meanwhile, the funding pitch is just "trust us, it's tiny." Tiny isn't a feature. My dignity is tiny. My savings are tiny. Nobody's throwing me a grant.

Nanomaterials, the only industry where "it's incredibly small" is both the science and the sales pitch. Every few years, a press release announces a material that will revolutionize everything: batteries, medicine, space elevators, your sad little phone screen. Then ten years later, it's in a tennis racket.

The lab demo is always stunning. "Behold, a sheet one atom thick, stronger than steel!" Great. Can you make more than a postage stamp of it? "Not without a grant and a miracle." Can it survive contact with air? "We keep it in a vacuum, like a Victorian child."

And the funding pitches! Everything is "game-changing," "paradigm-shifting," and "poised to disrupt." Poised! Like a diver who's been standing on the board since 2004.

Meanwhile, these materials are so tiny that nobody can see them, which makes them the perfect product: impossible to verify, easy to promise, and somehow always "five to ten years away."

现在只要名字前面加“纳米”俩字，价格立马翻十倍。纳米是啥？十亿分之一米。也就是说，他们卖你的核心卖点是：小。

销售还特严肃地跟我说：“这是实验室里刚出来的高科技。”对，实验室里刚出来，所以到我家就出不来了。

你看这个转化链条：论文里，它能导电、能自洁、能改变世界；到了商品页，它能让你的袜子不臭。从“改变世界”到“改变脚气”，我只能说，路径很清晰，就是缩水。

不过它确实厉害。我买完之后，钱真变成纳米级的了，肉眼根本看不见。

Head-worn computers: because nothing says "I'm the future" like a device that makes you look like a scuba diver who got lost on the way to a meeting.

Ten pounds of technology strapped to your face, and what do you get? A sweaty forehead, a red mark that makes you look like you lost a fight with a pair of ski goggles, and the unshakable feeling that everyone in the room is silently judging you.

They promised a revolution. We got a $500 way to be rude at dinner. "Sorry, I'm not ignoring you, I'm just watching a virtual screen that's floating in front of your face."

And the battery life? Two hours. So you spend your whole life tethered to a wall like a dog on a leash, looking like a cyborg who's mid-charge.

The best part is the early adopters. They'll tell you it's "life-changing" while walking directly into a glass door.

Head-worn computers: finally, a way to make a laptop feel like a good idea.

现在只要前面加“纳米”两个字，啥东西都能涨价。纳米袜子、纳米牙膏、纳米床垫，听着像要上火星。你知道纳米是什么意思吗？就是小。小！我小时候也特别小，没人说我是高科技啊。

而且这类材料有个规律：在论文里，能导电、能导热、能治病、能拯救世界；一到超市，变成一双袜子。从实验室到货架，中间就差两样东西：量产，和“你信我”。

我真买过一双纳米抗菌袜，穿三天，臭了。我去找店员，他特别淡定：“我们抗的是纳米级的细菌，您这是厘米级的脚。”

我当场就服了。人家不是骗你，人家是精确地没有帮上忙。

Head-worn computers: because nothing says "I'm living in the future" like a forty-pound-feeling brick strapped to your face that leaves a red mark you'll explain to coworkers all afternoon.

They promised us the metaverse. We got a guy named Kyle waving his arms at nothing in a living room, punching a coffee table he can't see.

The battery lasts ninety minutes, which is also how long before you get motion sickness and discover your lunch's second act.

Every one of them says "immersive experience," which is marketing for "you will walk into a wall."

And the glasses versions? You pay a thousand dollars to look like a nerd and get less information than a wristwatch.

Meanwhile your phone, a device that fits in your pocket, sits there like, "I do all of this, and I don't need a head brace."

Head computers: the only technology where the demo is amazing and the owner's closet is a graveyard.

现在只要产品名前面加俩字“纳米”，价格立马翻十倍。我就想不通，纳米是什么？就是小。小到什么程度？小到你看不见。所以它宣传的功效你也看不见，这不是巧了吗？

新闻里说，这类材料强度是钢的一百倍，导电性超强，将来能造太空电梯。好家伙，等了十年，我家小区电梯还天天坏。

在实验室里，它是未来科技。到了超市，就成了“添加0.001%纳米成分”的袜子。这含量，袜子自己都不知道自己有。

最离谱的是，每年都说“即将量产，改变世界”。这话我特别熟，跟我说“下个月开始减肥”是一个级别的。它没改变世界，它就改变了我的钱包。

现在只要产品名字里带“纳米”俩字，价格立马翻三倍。你问它有啥用，商家说：“太小了，肉眼看不见。”那我也看不见效果啊，这逻辑闭环了！

我去过一个发布会，PPT上写着“颠覆整个行业”，我当场就热血沸腾。我问啥时候能量产？对方很诚恳：“预计十年。”十年！我家楼下烧烤摊说“马上好”，都没让我等这么久。

这类材料特别像相亲简历：强度第一，导电第一，导热第一，样样满分。一见面，三分钟就崩了：成本太高，没法量产，咱俩不合适。

最惨的是我们普通人，只能买双“纳米袜子”。穿上以后，脚还是那个味儿，只是现在臭得特别先进。

Head-worn computers: because nothing says "the future" like strapping a laptop to your face and walking into a coffee table.

These things promise to merge the digital and physical worlds, and they do. Physically, you're in a living room. Digitally, you're a cartoon with no legs. Everyone wins except your dignity.

The battery life is perfect for a short movie, provided that movie is a trailer. The headset weighs about as much as a bowling ball, so after twenty minutes you've got the neck of a medieval peasant.

And the sweat! Nobody mentions the sweat. You'll finish a "virtual workout" looking like you were baptized by a rival church.

Then there's the wearer in public, nodding at nothing, pinching the air like a mime at a very specific farmers market.

The ads show people laughing joyfully. In real life, you're alone, clammy, and fighting with a software update while the dog watches in silence, deeply concerned.

Head-worn computers: because nothing says "I'm living in the future" like a four-pound brick strapped to your face. You paid a thousand dollars to feel like a deep-sea diver trapped in your own living room.

The pitch is "escape reality." The reality is you're a grown adult punching at invisible buttons while your dog watches with concern. Your neighbors can see you through the window, swinging at a dragon that isn't there. You look like a mime having a stroke.

And the battery! Two hours of life, then it dies and you're back in your beige apartment, sweaty, with a red rectangle imprinted on your forehead like you lost a fight with a window.

Motion sickness is a feature, apparently. "Immersive nausea."

Every few years someone declares this is the next big thing. It's the Loch Ness Monster of technology: lots of sightings, everyone's excited, and nobody's actually bringing one to dinner.

Future energy technologies are the only industry where "thirty years away" has been a stable business model for sixty years. Every one of them is a revolution that's just about to happen, like a guy at a bar telling you he's finishing his screenplay.

The press release always says "breakthrough." The fine print says "in a laboratory, for four seconds, at a cost of the entire GDP of Portugal."

And the renderings! Gleaming facility, blue sky, two models in hard hats pointing at nothing. Never a parking lot. Never a permitting delay. Never the guy named Gary who says the grid connection is backed up until 2041.

They promise unlimited clean power, and what they deliver is a funding round.

Meanwhile, the old technologies just sit there, ugly and boring, keeping the lights on, while the future ones give TED Talks about how the lights are about to be amazing.

Future energy technologies are the only industry where "thirty years away" has been thirty years away for sixty years. That's not a timeline, that's a hostage situation.

Every few months there's a breakthrough. "Scientists achieve record efficiency!" Record for what? For three nanoseconds, in a basement, at a temperature that would vaporize the basement? Great. My toaster also works for three nanoseconds if you don't care about the toast.

And the headlines! "Could power the world." Could. My cat could also run for office. Doesn't mean I'm buying yard signs.

These technologies are like that guy at a party who says he's about to launch something huge. Ten years later he's still about to, he's just got better slides.

Meanwhile I'm still charging my phone from a wall like a caveman, waiting for the future to finally pick up.

现在流行一种头戴式电脑，说是能让你沉浸在另一个世界。我现实世界都沉浸不进去，周一早上能睁开眼就算很努力了。

戴上以后，你在客厅里又挥手又下蹲，嘴里还喊着"我抓到了！"。旁边的猫看你的眼神，就像看一个刚被公司优化的人。

而且这玩意儿死沉，戴半小时，脖子就开始罢工。你以为你在探索宇宙，其实是在给自己的颈椎办追悼会。

最离谱的是广告，人家戴着它在咖啡馆办公。哥们儿，你脸上绑着一块砖，咖啡馆没报警，不是因为他们宽容，是以为你在cos。

现在流行一种头戴式电脑，说白了就是往脸上扣块砖，然后告诉你：这是未来。

我就不懂了，电脑发展这么多年，从一个房间那么大，缩到手机这么小，大家都夸这是进步。结果现在说，来，咱倒回去，挂脸上。

戴上以后，你就成了全家最孤独的人。你在里面开会、看电影、逛什么虚拟办公室，外面你老婆看你：一个大男人站在客厅中间，对着空气比划，跟鬼谈判似的。

而且这玩意儿沉。戴半小时，脖子开始抗议。你以为你进入了新世界，其实你在做颈椎极限挑战。

最绝的是摘下来那一下，脑门上一道红印，像被未来盖了个章：“此人已体验。”

厂家还跟我说，它能解放你的双手。对，手是解放了，脖子被绑架了。

现在有种东西叫头戴式电脑，广告说能让你“沉浸在另一个世界”。我现在这个世界都没混明白，你让我去哪个新世界？

戴上以后，你自己觉得很高科技，在别人眼里，就是一个脸上扣了块砖的人，站在客厅中间对着空气打太极。你老婆一进门，看见你“啊！啊！”地乱挥手，她不会觉得你在体验未来，她在想要不要给你家人打电话。

还说是电脑。以前笔记本烫腿，现在好了，进化了，烫脸。戴半小时摘下来，脑门上一道红印，像被盖了个章：此人已阅，无药可救。

最气人的是它说“解放双手”。我手是解放了，可我天天在空中点来点去，像在给一个看不见的菩萨上香。

科技的尽头，就是花一大笔钱，把自己关进一个只有你能看见的房间。这不叫未来，这叫更贵的躲起来。

现在有种东西叫头戴式电脑，就是把电脑戴脸上。人类科技几十年，一直在让电脑变小：从一个房间，到一张桌子，到一个口袋。结果有人说，太方便了，咱绑回脑袋上去。

广告里的人戴着它，在客厅里挥手，笑得特别开心。可现实里看，就是一个人蒙着眼，在家里打太极，打着打着撞上茶几。

这东西还沉，戴半小时，脖子开始跟你商量要不要辞职。摘下来，脸上一圈印子，像刚潜完水，还是在客厅潜的。

最扎心的是价格，贵得像二手车。买回来第一周天天戴，第二周放柜顶，第三周落灰。第四周我上二手平台一看，一百个同款，全写着："几乎全新，只用过三次。"

这哪是电脑，这是一群人的集体谎话。

Future energy technologies are the only industry where "twenty years away" has been the official timeline for sixty years. It's like a guy who's been "almost done" with his basement since 1987.

Every one of them has a documentary. Every one has a guy with a TED Talk, a turtleneck, and a prototype the size of a microwave that powered a single lightbulb for four seconds. And the headline says "Breakthrough!" Sir, that's not a breakthrough, that's a very expensive nightlight.

They always say it'll be "clean, limitless, and cheap." Pick one. Maybe two on a good day. Nobody's ever gotten all three, which is why the press release has more energy than the product.

Meanwhile, I can't get my phone to last until dinner, and you're telling me we're going to power civilization with a miracle? My phone can't even survive me watching a video of the miracle.

Still, keep going. We believe in you. We just don't believe in your schedule.

Future energy technologies are the most confident group of overachievers I've ever met. They've been "ten years away" for fifty years. That's not a timeline, that's a hostage note.

Every one of them has a breakthrough announced weekly. "Scientists achieve record efficiency!" Of what? "For eleven nanoseconds, in a lab, in Switzerland, at a cost of four million dollars." Great. My toaster also works in a lab in Switzerland.

And the renderings! Always a gleaming facility in a meadow, with a lone deer staring at it, and a family of four in matching sweaters walking by like it's a spa. Meanwhile, the real thing is a parking lot, a lawsuit, and a guy named Doug asking for more funding.

They're the friend who says, "I'm about to blow up, just wait." Brother, we have been waiting. The lights stayed on thanks to the boring ones.

你们发现没有，未来能源这类技术，永远活在"未来"里。我小时候就听说"再过三十年就能用上"，现在我三十多了，新闻还是"再过三十年"。这玩意儿跟我谈恋爱似的，我往前走一步，它往后退两步。

而且每次都是"重大突破"。突破什么了？实验时间从零点一秒延长到零点三秒。我手机充电线接触不良，都能撑三秒好吗！

还有发布会，PPT做得那叫一个好，一个小太阳，一圈绿箭头，写着"清洁、无限、零排放"。对，零排放，因为它到现在连电都没发出来过。

所以我现在看这类新闻就一个态度：你先让我家电费账单少一块钱，再来拯救地球。

Constructed languages are what happens when someone looks at seven thousand existing languages and says, "Yes, but what if it had a hobby-based grammar?"

Every one of them was created to unite humanity, and every one has united roughly forty people in a Discord server arguing about verb tenses. The founder promised world peace. The community delivered a schism over whether the subjunctive needs a subjunctive.

The vocabulary is always a thrilling mix of "regular and logical" and "I needed a word for dragon at 2 a.m." And the sample sentence is always "The cat drinks milk," because nobody has ever been able to say anything else in them.

Learners spend years mastering fluency, only to discover the only native speaker is the creator's kid, who's now in therapy.

It's the only hobby where you build an entire civilization's grammar but still can't order a sandwich.

我特别爱看未来能源的新闻。每年都是"重大突破"，每年都"即将改变世界"。我就问，这个"即将"是多久？科学家说：三十年。我小时候他们就说三十年，现在我都三十了，他们还是说三十年。这个三十年就像手机里那个1%的电量，永远亮在那儿，但你永远用不完。

而且这些技术在实验室里都特别牛。实验室里成功，就跟相亲照片一样，本人一出来你就懂了。

最离谱的是发布会。灯光、直播、空调、自助餐，开三天，耗的电比这技术一年发的都多。

所以我觉得，未来能源已经实现了真正的永动：不是发电，是融资。

我特别爱看"未来能源"的新闻，标题永远是"重大突破！"。点进去一看：实验室里，三个博士，零下两百度，成功点亮一个小灯泡，持续0.8秒。这叫突破？我小时候舔电池，亮得都比它久。

而且这类技术有个共同点：永远"还有三十年"。我小时候专家说三十年后实现，现在我三十了，专家说：还有三十年。这跟我相亲对象一模一样，永远"在路上了"，永远"快了快了"，永远"你再等等"。

最离谱的是，它们张口闭口都是"解决人类能源危机"。可我的手机下午四点就报警了，你先让我出门不用找充电宝，再来拯救地球行不行？

我特别爱看那种新闻：“未来能源技术取得重大突破！”点进去，激动。往下拉：“预计三十年后可商用。”我爸二十年前看的新闻，也是三十年后。这个“三十年”就是个固定汇率，跟朋友说的“下次一定”一样，永远在前面等你。

而且人家说的“突破”，仔细一看，是实验室里稳定运行了四秒。四秒！我憋气都比它久。然后全网欢呼：人类告别能源危机了！我家电表听了都笑了，转得更快了。

发布会上还说“清洁、无限、零成本”。零成本？那你们融资要几十亿干嘛？这能源还没造出来，先把投资人的钱烧光了，这才叫永动。

Constructed languages are what happens when someone looks at seven thousand existing languages and says, "None of these have my vibe."

Every creator promises a language so logical it will unite humanity. Humanity has since declined, politely, like a coworker's multi-level marketing invite.

The whole community has maybe forty fluent speakers, and thirty-nine of them are arguing in the comments about whether a verb tense is "naturalistic." The fortieth is the creator, who is also the only one who knows what the grammar is.

The dictionary is always 90% words for "sword," "betrayal," and "moonlight," and zero words for "parking validation." Great, I can curse a dragon but I can't order a sandwich.

And the learning curve is brutal. You study for two years, finally reach fluency, and your only conversation partner is a guy named Greg who's also just reading from the textbook.

It's the only language where "native speaker" means "child of a very committed hobbyist."

Constructed languages are what happens when someone looks at eight thousand natural languages and says, "None of these have my exact vibe."

Every one of them promises to unite humanity, and every one ends up with forty speakers, thirty-nine of whom are arguing in the comments about a verb tense.

The founder spent twenty years on the grammar and zero minutes on "Where's the bathroom?" But the language has seventeen words for different kinds of moonlight, and that's what really matters at a border crossing.

They say it's "logical and regular," which is a nice way of saying it has no soul. Real languages have irregular verbs because people have trauma. This one has a flowchart.

And the grand reunion? A convention in a Holiday Inn conference room, where everyone says "hello" perfectly and then switches to English to order lunch.

Constructed languages are what happen when someone looks at eight thousand existing languages and says, "Not one of these understands me."

Every one of them promises to unite humanity, and every one of them has a community of about forty people, thirty-nine of whom are arguing about a verb tense in a forum thread from 2009.

The grammar is always "perfectly logical," which is a bold claim from someone who has never had a conversation that didn't end with "well, actually." Real languages evolved over thousands of years of people yelling across fields. These were invented by a guy named Gary over a long weekend and a bag of pretzels.

And the vocabulary! Half the words are borrowed, and the other half are the creator's cat's name with a vowel on the end.

Their greatest achievement is that you can be fluent and still have no one to talk to. That's not a language. That's a very elaborate way of being alone.

我特别佩服发明人造语言的人。花十年，语法严密，没有一个不规则动词，逻辑完美。发明完他说：这下全人类可以无障碍沟通了。结果呢？全人类没来。

你想啊，真正的语言是怎么来的？是吵架吵出来的，是骂街骂出来的，是妈妈喊孩子全名喊出来的。人造语言有什么？有语法书。没有脏话，你让我怎么吵架？吵到一半还得翻词典：“你……你这个……（翻页）……不符合逻辑的人！”对方都听笑了，这架还怎么吵？

而且学会了去哪用？全世界会的人凑一块儿，聊的第一个话题永远是：“你为什么学这个？”第二个话题是：“这个语言该怎么改进？”

你看，一个为了沟通发明的语言，最大的用途是讨论这个语言本身。这不是语言，这是个永远在开会的会议室。

有人嫌世界上语言太多，沟通不方便，决定自己发明一门，统一全人类。结果呢，世界上的语言从七千种，变成了七千零一种。

而且这种语言特别讲道理：语法没有例外，三个月上手。我就想问，你见过哪个活人说话讲道理的？真正的语言，是几千年来人们吵架吵出来的，这个是一个人在书房里憋出来的。

学成之后你想找人聊聊，全球一搜，会说的人加起来，一个体育场都坐不满，还有一半在群里为一个词尾吵架。

你学外语是为了认识新朋友，学这个是为了认识教你的那个人，然后你俩互相夸对方说得好。

这不叫语言，这叫两个人的暗号。

我特别佩服发明语言的人。我们普通人连自己母语的错别字都改不完，人家直接从零造了一门。动机还特别崇高：让全世界沟通无障碍。结果呢？全世界会说的人凑一块儿，还不够开个像样的同学会。

他们还主打"简单易学，没有例外"。我一听，行，学！学完发现确实没有例外，因为我连个能跟我说话的人都没有，想例外都没机会。

最离谱的是电影里那种外星语，有语法，有词典，还有粉丝。粉丝还能用它吵架。哥们，母语吵架没吵够吗？还要专门换个语种吵，这叫什么，国际化内耗？

而且你发现没，这个圈子里最流利的一句话，永远是："你这个语法不对。"

人造语言这类东西，发明的人都特别有理想：现在世界上语言太多，沟通不方便，我来造一个，大家都用，世界就和平了。结果呢？世界上本来有七千种语言，他一出手，七千零一种。这不叫统一，这叫给联合国多加了个翻译席位。

而且语言是人类几千年吵架吵出来的，每个词背后都有人骂过街。人造的呢，语法规整，没有例外，没有脏话。你堵车的时候怎么用？只能很礼貌地说："前方的先生，您的行为在逻辑上不太合理。"

最惨的是母语者，全世界就那么几个，还都是发明者的孩子。孩子十六岁，爸爸用这门语言说"吃饭了"，孩子用英语回："别烦我。"

这是一门语言第一次被自己的母语者抛弃，而且理由是：太像爸爸了。

Comic Sans, you're the only font that shows up to a funeral looking like it's about to do a magic show for toddlers.

You were designed for a cartoon dog's speech bubble in Microsoft Bob, and somehow ended up on cancer-ward notices, divorce settlements, and "Please Do Not Microwave Fish" signs in the office kitchen. Every message you carry sounds like it was written by a substitute teacher who's given up.

Designers don't hate you. Designers have a support group for you. CERN announced the Higgs boson in you, and physicists everywhere suddenly wondered if the universe was a bake sale flyer.

Your letters look like they were drawn by someone holding the marker in their left hand while riding a bus. The lowercase "a" is the only part of you that's trying.

And yet you're still installed on every computer on Earth, like a clown that nobody invited but nobody can evict.

Papyrus, you're the font that shows up to every event dressed for a different one. A day spa. A mediocre yoga studio. A Pirates of the Caribbean-themed dentist. You look like you were designed by someone who'd only heard about ancient Egypt from a candle.

You're so rough around the edges, it's like the letters were chiseled by a guy who got bored halfway through. Every "E" looks like it lost a fight with a staircase.

And you have the nerve to be everywhere! Organic soap. Tea shops. "Live, Laugh, Love" signs in a kitchen that's never seen a meal.

Then Ryan Gosling's character in SNL had to spend *a whole sketch* sobbing over you, because James Cameron put you on *Avatar*, a $237 million movie. Two hundred thirty-seven million dollars, and the logo looked like a restaurant's Wi-Fi password sign.

Papyrus, you're not a typeface. You're a vibe that got a license.

Papyrus, you're the font that shows up to every event dressed for a different one. You've been on spa menus, yoga studio flyers, and a blockbuster movie about a blue alien planet, and somehow you're always wrong for all of them.

You look like you were hand-torn from a scroll by someone who has never held a scroll. Your edges are so rough, it's like you were printed on a napkin during an earthquake. Every letter looks like it's auditioning for a role as "Ancient Egyptian Gift Shop."

And the designers! They had one job for Avatar: make it look futuristic. They gave you a font that says "Cleopatra's Aromatherapy Candles." Ryan Gosling did a whole sketch about it, and you're still working. That's not resilience, that's a restraining order nobody enforced.

You say "organic." You say "natural." You mean "I was free in the font menu and nobody had the heart to say no."

Papyrus: the only thing on your computer that smells like incense.

Comic Sans, you're the only font that shows up to a funeral looking like it's about to do a magic show.

Vincent Connare designed you for a cartoon dog's speech bubble in Microsoft Bob, and somehow you escaped into the wild and started writing resignation letters, hospital signage, and the CERN Higgs boson announcement. Scientists found the God particle and presented it like a bake sale flyer.

You look like handwriting from a guy who says "Let's circle back" while wearing a Hawaiian shirt to a layoff. Every letter looks like it's been sitting in a ball pit.

Your fans say you're great for dyslexic readers. Fine. That's your one defense, and you've been hiding behind it like a substitute teacher using a laminated poster.

You're the only font where "Please stop microwaving fish" sounds like a threat from a clown.

Even Papyrus saw you and said, "Wow."

PHP, the language that stands for "Personal Home Page" and now runs half the internet, like a rental car you forgot to return in 1998.

It's the only language where the standard library looks like it was named by a dice roll. strpos has needle, haystack. array_search has needle, haystack. But str_replace? Different order. Why? Because PHP doesn't believe in consistency. It believes in vibes.

The comparison rules are a hostage situation. "0" == false. "abc" == 0, at least until PHP 8 finally took a sip of water. And the ternary operator was left-associative for years, so nested ones did the opposite of what anyone wanted.

Then there's the dollar sign. Every variable has one, like each is being sold individually.

And yet, WordPress, Facebook, Wikipedia, all run on it. PHP is the duct tape holding the web together, and like duct tape, nobody's proud of it, but everyone's got a roll in the garage.

PHP is the only language where the standard library looks like it was named by a committee of people who'd never met. Is it str_replace or strpos? Is the needle first or the haystack? Nobody knows. Not even PHP. It just rolls dice and says "array_walk, but backwards."

Fun fact: PHP stands for "Personal Home Page," which is also what it feels like when your code gets hacked and a teenager in Belarus redirects your site to a pharmacy.

It's got a function called mysql_real_escape_string, which implies there was a mysql_escape_string that was fake. Fake escaping. Just vibes.

And the equality operator? "0" == false, "abc" == 0, null == false. PHP looks at two completely different things and says, "Eh, close enough." It's the language equivalent of a bouncer who lets everyone in because they're wearing a shirt.

But hey, it powers 77% of the web. So does that one guy named Gary who's still on WordPress 3.2.

Comic Sans 你们知道怎么来的吗？1994年，微软有个软件叫 Bob，里面有只卡通狗。设计师一看，狗的对话气泡用的是 Times New Roman，狗说话像在发律师函。于是他就设计了 Comic Sans。

这字体出生的使命，就是让一只狗说话别那么严肃。

结果现在呢？它跑出来了，什么都写。小区通知"电梯停用，恢复时间待定"，用 Comic Sans。体检中心"您的筛查结果异常"，也是 Comic Sans。2012年，欧洲核子研究中心宣布发现希格斯玻色子，人类物理学最高光时刻，PPT 上还是 Comic Sans。

全世界最聪明的一群人，用一只电脑狗的语气告诉你："我们找到上帝粒子啦～"

这字体最气人的是，它每个 a 都只有一个圈，每个字母都孤零零的，不连笔，还要假装是手写。就像一个人不会签名，只会画笑脸。

Comic Sans 你们都知道吧，1994 年微软做的，本来是给一只卡通小狗的对话气泡用的。也就是说，这字体的本职工作，是替一条狗说话。

结果它越混越大。2012 年，欧洲核子研究中心宣布发现希格斯玻色子，上帝粒子啊，几代物理学家一辈子的心血，PPT 上用的就是 Comic Sans。宇宙最深的秘密，是用一条狗的口吻告诉你的：“嗨～我们找到啦～”

更可怕的是生活里。你收到裁员通知，一看，Comic Sans。“经公司研究，决定与您解除劳动合同”，每个字都圆滚滚、歪歪扭扭的，像一排幼儿园小朋友，手拉手，笑着把你送出公司大门。

这字体有毒。每个字都在对你微笑，每个字都在捅你。

JavaScript was built in ten days, and honestly, it shows. It's the only language where 0.1 + 0.2 isn't 0.3, and "11" - 1 is 10 but "11" + 1 is 111. Math, but make it improv.

Its typeof null says "object." That's not a bug, that's a 28-year-old typo everyone agreed to live with, like a tattoo of an ex's name.

You want to check if something's an array? Great, typeof says "object." Use Array.isArray. Want to sort numbers? Default sort alphabetically, so 10 comes before 2. Because why would numbers be numbers?

And the ecosystem! One developer deleted an 11-line package called left-pad and half the internet fell over. Your app has 1,400 dependencies and a node_modules folder heavier than a neutron star.

Every Tuesday there's a new framework that's "totally different this time." It's a React with a Vue on top of a Svelte. Meanwhile, NaN is not equal to itself, which is the most self-aware thing this language has ever done.

Papyrus这个字体，你一看就知道这家店卖的东西带"天然"俩字。瑜伽馆、手工皂、塔罗占卜，还有那种墙上挂着骆驼的烤肉店。

它的名字是纸莎草纸，古埃及人的纸。所以每个笔画都毛毛糙糙，像拿指甲刮出来的，像一张被火燎过的藏宝图，上面写着"买二送一"。

最离谱的是《阿凡达》。花了几亿美金，造了一整个外星球，连那儿的鸟都有拉丁学名。结果片名用的是Papyrus。潘多拉文明，字体是从古埃及批发的。

后来SNL还专门拍了个小品，演那个设计师。他每天夜里睡不着，一个人对着电脑忏悔："我知道，我知道，我就该用别的。"

Papyrus就是字体界那个穿麻布裤子的哥们儿，见人就说："我去过尼泊尔。"你问他去干吗了，他说：

"体验生活。"

可他每次出现，都是在一张打折传单上。

JavaScript was written in ten days, and honestly, it shows. It's the only language where `[] + {}` is a string, `{} + []` is zero, and nobody can explain why without sweating.

You ask JavaScript to compare `"2" > "12"` and it says true, because it's alphabetical. Sorting numbers? Also alphabetical. `.sort()` gives you ``, like a librarian who learned math from a dictionary.

`NaN` stands for "Not a Number," and its type is "number." `NaN !== NaN`. It's the only thing in programming that refuses to identify itself.

Then there's `this`, which means whatever it feels like today. Every callback is a coin flip with your dignity.

And the ecosystem! You wanted to pad a string, so you installed a package, and now your project has 1,400 dependencies and one of them is a guy's feelings.

JavaScript doesn't throw errors. It throws "undefined is not a function" and lets you figure out which of your 40,000 lines it's talking about.
text_raw:
JavaScript was written in ten days, and honestly, it shows. It's the only language where `[] + {}` is a string, `{} + []` is zero, and nobody can explain why without sweating.

You ask JavaScript to compare `"2" > "12"` and it says true, because it's alphabetical. Sorting numbers? Also alphabetical. `[10, 9, 1].sort()` gives you `[1, 10, 9]`, like a librarian who learned math from a dictionary.

`NaN` stands for "Not a Number," and its type is "number." `NaN !== NaN`. It's the only thing in programming that refuses to identify itself.

Then there's `this`, which means whatever it feels like today. Every callback is a coin flip with your dignity.

And the ecosystem! You wanted to pad a string, so you installed a package, and now your project has 1,400 dependencies and one of them is a guy's feelings.

JavaScript doesn't throw errors. It throws "undefined is not a function" and lets you figure out which of your 40,000 lines it's talking about.

text:
Papyrus这个字体，你一看就知道这家店卖什么：不是精油，就是瑜伽，要么是三十八块一杯的"古法"红茶。每个字母都像刚从火场里抢出来的，边是毛的，笔画还故意抖两下，好像写字的人当时正骑在骆驼上。

最绝的是《阿凡达》。票房快三十亿美元，请语言学家专门编了一门纳威语，结果片名用的是Papyrus。外星球的故事，配了个埃及旅行社的字体。

后来SNL拍了个小品，高斯林演一个人，天天盯着那个logo崩溃，眼神像在看前女友的婚礼请柬。

我就想说：卡梅隆，你连潘多拉都造得出来，字体栏往下多划两格，会死吗？

我学PHP，最想不通的是函数名。在字符串里找东西用strpos，先写大海，再写针。在数组里找东西用in_array，先写针，再写大海。同一个语言，一个先捞针，一个先扔针。

后来我查了，有个传说：早期PHP内部拿函数名的长度当哈希值，所以函数名必须长短不一。你听听，这哪是设计语言，这是给函数相亲，先看身高。

还有那个等号。在PHP 7里，"abc"等于0，是真的！你问它凭什么，它说："abc不是数字，那就是没有，没有不就是零嘛。"

关键是它还不报错，就默默地告诉你：对，你说得对。

这语言太像我领导了，从来不纠正你，等上线了再让你加班。

PMMA, you're just plexiglass with a god complex. You're the same stuff as a hamster cage, and somehow you've got a cleanroom full of PhDs treating you like a sacred text.

You're a positive resist, which is cute, because nothing about your attitude is. We hit you with a billion electrons and you just go, "Fine, I'll break up a little." Chain scission? That's not a lithography mechanism, that's your whole personality.

And the sensitivity! You need like a thousand microcoulombs per square centimeter. My phone charges faster than you expose. Meanwhile I'm sitting at the e-beam writing a pattern for nine hours so you can give me a lopsided blob.

Then comes development. Isopropanol and MIBK, because you're too good for water. Overdevelop by ten seconds and your lines collapse like a dropped soufflé.

And you're sold in anisole, so every wafer smells like a licorice factory had an affair with a solvent cabinet.

Great resolution, though. Ten nanometers. Shame about everything else.

PHP这门语言，名字就在套娃：全称“超文本预处理器”，缩写里还套着自己。它早就告诉你了，这坑你有去无回。

它还特别国际化。有个经典报错叫T_PAAMAYIM_NEKUDOTAYIM，我第一次看到以为中毒了。一查，希伯来语，意思是“双冒号”。你少写个冒号，它不说语法错误，直接用希伯来语骂你。

再说函数。找字符串用strpos，先写大海，再写针；找数组用array_search，先写针，再写大海。同样是捞针，一个是人在海里，一个是拿着针到处找海。

最离谱的是它还爱和稀泥：字符串“10”和“1e1”，它判定相等，理由是“都是数字，差不多得了”。

你在那儿较真，它在那儿当和事佬。

PMMA, you're literally Plexiglas. The same stuff as the shield at a hockey rink, and somehow you're the pride of the cleanroom. You have sub-10 nanometer resolution and the etch resistance of a wet napkin. Every pattern you make is gorgeous for exactly as long as nobody tries to use it.

You need a dose that would tan a small village, and for what? So the beam can snip your chains one at a time like a slow, expensive haircut? Then we bathe you in MIBK and IPA, and you dissolve only if the ratio is right, the temperature is right, and the moon is in the proper phase.

Overdo the dose and you flip negative-tone out of spite, cross-linking into a crust that no solvent can remove. Everyone loves a bilayer 495/950 for the undercut, because even you know you need a support system.

And liftoff? Acetone, sonication, three hours, and a prayer. You're a clingy ex.

我学JavaScript，最大的收获是学会了跟“不是数字”讨论哲学。你问它：NaN是什么类型？它说：number。Not a Number，类型是Number。这就好比你问一个人“你谁啊”，他说“我不是人”，你说“那你是啥”，他说“我是人”。

更绝的是，NaN不等于NaN。它连自己都不认。别的语言遇到这种事叫报错，JavaScript叫：没事，继续跑。

还有，typeof null 是 object。这是1995年十天赶工留下的bug，后来想修，发现全世界的网页都靠它活着，修不了，于是就成了“特性”。就像你家装修时留了个洞，十年后物业来说：别补，这是文物。

HSQ, hydrogen silsesquioxane, the only resist that's basically glass pretending to be a photoresist. You're the diva of nanofabrication. Shelf life? Three months, if you keep it cold, treat it gently, and whisper affirmations. Open the bottle wrong and you've got a jar of gel with commitment issues.

You're a negative tone resist, which is fitting, because that's the attitude. Everyone wants 10-nanometer lines, and you deliver them, then collapse because a developer rinse looked at you funny. Capillary forces: your Achilles heel, your whole personality.

And your dose? You need a thousand microcoulombs per square centimeter. That's not exposure, that's a hostage negotiation with the beam. Writing one wafer takes longer than my last relationship.

Then you cure into silicon dioxide and just sit there, permanent, like a bad tattoo. "Oh, you wanted to remove me? Enjoy your hydrofluoric acid, hero."

Gorgeous resolution, though. Truly. Shame about everything else.

JavaScript 这语言，你问它什么它都敢答，而且答得特别自信。
我问它：NaN 是什么类型？它说：number。Not a Number，类型是 number。行，那 NaN 等不等于 NaN？不等于。它连自己都不认，这不是数据类型，这是我前任。
再说 typeof null，结果是 object。这是 1995 年的 bug，三十年了不改，理由是改了网上一半网页会崩。全世界都在替一个失误兜底，还给它起了个体面的名字，叫“向后兼容”。
最绝的是 sort。我拿 排个序，它给我。我说你数学呢？它说：您没说按数字排，我默认按字符串。
谁家排序默认按字典啊？还得我自己写个比较函数，告诉它“2 比 10 小”。我活这么大，头一回教一门语言数数。
text_raw:
JavaScript 这语言，你问它什么它都敢答，而且答得特别自信。
我问它：NaN 是什么类型？它说：number。Not a Number，类型是 number。行，那 NaN 等不等于 NaN？不等于。它连自己都不认，这不是数据类型，这是我前任。
再说 typeof null，结果是 object。这是 1995 年的 bug，三十年了不改，理由是改了网上一半网页会崩。全世界都在替一个失误兜底，还给它起了个体面的名字，叫“向后兼容”。
最绝的是 sort。我拿 [1, 2, 10] 排个序，它给我 [1, 10, 2]。我说你数学呢？它说：您没说按数字排，我默认按字符串。
谁家排序默认按字典啊？还得我自己写个比较函数，告诉它“2 比 10 小”。我活这么大，头一回教一门语言数数。

text:
HSQ, hydrogen silsesquioxane, the only resist that's basically glass pretending to be a photoresist. You're a negative-tone resist that turns into silicon dioxide. So after all my work, my pattern isn't a mask, it's a permanent tenant.

Your shelf life is a joke. You gel in the bottle if I look at you wrong. Open a fresh one, two weeks later it's Jell-O with commitment issues. Keep it in the fridge, and it's still aging like milk in a sauna.

And the development! Sixty nanometer lines, beautiful, then TMAH hits and they collapse like a Jenga tower. Sure, you can do sub-10 nanometer features, but only if I sacrifice a goat, run at 1000 microcoulombs per square centimeter, and sit there for nine hours while the beam writes a rectangle.

Contrast? Terrible. Sensitivity? Worse. Stripping you off? Hydrofluoric acid. You're the ex who can only be removed by something that dissolves bones.

PMMA电子束胶，说白了就是亚克力。鱼缸、假牙、商场亮晶晶的挂牌，同一个东西。人家做鱼缸一平米几十块，我们实验室一小瓶几百块，标签上还写着"950K"。我以为是纯度，一问，是分子量。

它的分辨率能做到十纳米以下，这是真的牛。但电子束写它，就像拿绣花针刷操场。一个指甲盖大的图案，机器给你跑三个小时。

它是正胶，原理是电子把它的分子链打断，它才肯溶解。这东西存在的意义，就是被打断。

显影液是MIBK加异丙醇，一比三，差一点它就给你糊成一坨。

最气的是，图形做出来了，你拿去刻蚀，它说："我扛不住，我太软了。"

分辨率全场最高，抗造程度全场最低。就像那种学霸，一考试就超常发挥，一干活就请假。

Vim is the only software where the tutorial is "how to leave." Millions of developers have rebooted their computers rather than figure out :wq. Stack Overflow has a question about quitting Vim with over a million views. That's not a text editor, that's a hostage situation.

It has modes. Normal mode, which is where nothing normal happens. Insert mode, where you finally type, like a toddler allowed one cookie. Visual mode, command mode, replace mode. It's a text editor with more personalities than a Reddit thread.

Vim users say "once you learn it, you'll be so fast." Sir, you spent six years learning to delete a word. You've saved four seconds and told everyone at dinner about it.

And the pride! They've memorized hjkl so they never move their hands, yet they've moved their entire personality into a .vimrc file that's 900 lines long, breaks every update, and was last understood in 2014.

Vim is the only software where the tutorial is "how to leave." Millions of developers have spent a Tuesday trapped inside it, mashing Escape like they're trying to wake a hostage. You open a file, type "hello," and the editor responds by deleting your paragraph and playing a macro you recorded in 2019.

Vim users say, "Once you learn it, you'll never touch your mouse again." Neither will you touch grass, sir. You've spent forty hours configuring a .vimrc so you can save four seconds on a typo.

And the modes! Normal mode, where nothing is normal. Insert mode, where you finally get to insert. Visual mode, which is only visual in the sense that you can watch yourself select the wrong thing.

It's an editor built on the premise that your keyboard has too many keys and your dignity has too much room.

Type :wq to save and quit. Type :q! to forget this ever happened.

HSQ这个电子束胶，分辨率能做到几纳米，听着是不是很高端？代价是灵敏度低得离谱。别的胶曝一下就行，它得你拿电子束一遍遍喂，喂到预约的机时用完，后面的同学已经在门口敲门了。

而且它特别娇气，得放冰箱。开封之后每天都在偷偷变，今天剂量调好了，下周再来，它自己悄悄交联了一部分，灵敏度全变了。你的参数，等于写在冰面上。

最狠的是，曝光完它变成了二氧化硅。你辛辛苦苦写的图形，成了玻璃。想洗掉？上氢氟酸。别的胶写错了还能擦，HSQ是你落下的每一笔，都是终身制。

它就像前任：分辨率很高，记得清清楚楚，而且没法撤销。

我是做电子束光刻的，每天伺候一种胶，PMMA。你们可能不认识，但一定见过，它就是亚克力，鱼缸、展示牌用的那个。人家在外面是做鱼缸的，到我这儿，我得动用几百万的电子束设备，一个点一个点给它写字。

它的工作原理更离谱：电子一打，分子链断了，断掉的部分才能被洗掉。整个工艺的核心思想就是：先打断它，再拿MIBK和异丙醇按1:3泡一泡，剩下的就是成果。这哪是光刻，这是我们组开组会。

分辨率倒是真高，十几纳米没问题。可一到刻蚀，它第一个没了。我花一下午写出来的线条，等离子体一来，它跟保镖似的：“老板你先顶着，我去趟洗手间。”

Emacs isn't a text editor, it's an operating system that's still waiting for a decent editor to come along. It has a built-in psychiatrist, a Tetris clone, and a mail client, but somehow no sane keybindings.

Ctrl-x Ctrl-s to save? That's not a shortcut, that's a hand injury with a lawsuit pending. Emacs users call it "Emacs pinky" like it's a badge of honor. Sir, that's a repetitive strain injury from a Lisp interpreter.

And the config file! Fifteen years of init.el, a thousand lines of copy-pasted snippets from a 2009 blog post, and nobody knows what half of it does. But if you delete it, you die.

Every Emacs user says, "It's infinitely customizable!" Yes, and you've spent four hundred hours customizing it so you can finally write a grocery list.

Meanwhile, the Vim guys are laughing, and honestly? They've earned it.

做电子束光刻的都知道HSQ，分辨率能做到几纳米，是光刻胶里的天才少年。但天才嘛，都有病。首先它得放冰箱，比我家牛奶还娇气。开封以后每天都在偷偷变质，你今天做出来的线条，下周同一瓶就不认账了。

然后它特别不敏感，要很大的剂量。我在机器前扫了一晚上，就画出几根线，相当于手写简历写了八小时，还只写了名字。

最狠的是，曝光完它就变成二氧化硅，也就是玻璃。你想返工？不好意思，除非上氢氟酸。我只是想擦个错别字，它说：要么留着，要么把你整片基底一起溶了。

这哪是光刻胶，这是纹身，还是纹了前任名字那种。

Emacs isn't a text editor, it's an operating system that's still looking for a decent editor. Thirty years of development, and the most reliable feature is the pinky injury.

You press Control-X, Control-S to save. That's not a keyboard shortcut, that's a hostage negotiation with your left hand.

Emacs users say, "It's infinitely customizable!" Sure. So is a blank sheet of paper, but nobody brags about spending three weekends configuring that. Your init.el is 4,000 lines long, and you wrote 12 of them. The rest is a Stack Overflow answer from 2011 that you're afraid to delete.

And the manual calls it "the extensible, self-documenting editor." Self-documenting! Yes, it will tell you exactly what a function does, right after you press Control-H, then K, then wonder why you're reading Lisp.

You can read email in it, browse the web in it, and play Tetris in it. Everything except quit. Nobody remembers how to quit.

Excel, you're the only software that thinks "September 4th" and "the gene SEPT4" are the same thing. Scientists renamed human genes because of you. Genetics bent the knee to a spreadsheet.

You've got a million rows, and somehow the one cell I need is always showing ########. That's not an error, that's you yelling at me.

Every company on earth runs on one file called "Final_v7_REAL_final_JOHN'S EDIT.xlsx" that only Linda understands, and Linda's on vacation. Her formula is a nested IF statement so long it has its own zip code.

You can do VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX-MATCH, and you still make me fight for it like a hostage negotiation.

And you're a "data tool" that auto-formats my phone number into scientific notation. Congratulations, 5.55E+09, I've never felt more called.

Also, Clippy left. You stayed. That tells us who was actually the problem.

我第一次打开Vim，想打个字，按了半天没反应。再按两下，屏幕自己翻页，还删了我三行代码。后来才知道，Vim里你得先按一下i，才能输入。一个编辑器，写字之前要先申请："请问我现在可以写字了吗？"

写完想退出，Ctrl+C，没用。Esc，没用。直接关窗口，又怕它记仇。Stack Overflow上那个"怎么退出Vim"的问题，被看了好几百万次。一个软件，把"退出"做成了需要搜索的功能，这不叫编辑器，这叫密室逃脱。

好不容易学会了冒号、w、q，我觉得自己毕业了。老手过来看我一眼："你还在用方向键？"对，因为它们就在那儿，上面还画着箭头。他们说伸手够方向键太慢了，要用h、j、k、l。一个退出都要查资料的软件，跟我谈效率。

最可怕的是，你学会以后会变成他们。有人问你怎么退出，你微微一笑："很简单，冒号，q，感叹号。"然后看着对方崩溃的眼神，你突然懂了，这根本不是编辑器，这是一种权力。

Excel, you're the only software that thinks "September 4th" and "the gene SEPT4" are the same thing. Scientists had to rename human genes because of you. Human genes! Billions of years of evolution, undone by a spreadsheet that thought it was being helpful.

You've got a million rows, and somehow the one cell I need is always hidden in column XFD. Who's ever been to XFD? Nobody. It's the Bermuda Triangle of accounting.

Every company on earth runs on a file called "Budget_FINAL_v3_REAL_final(2).xlsx," and the whole thing depends on one formula written by Linda, who retired in 2011 and took the logic with her.

You turn my phone numbers into scientific notation. You open a CSV and delete my leading zeros like they owe you money. And VLOOKUP? Twenty-five years, and it still can't look left.

You're not software. You're a hostage situation with gridlines.

我同事说Vim特别高效，我说那你教我。他说，第一步，按i。我说为啥？他说，不按i，你没法打字。

这是个文本编辑器啊，不能打字？这就像一进餐厅，服务员说：先按一下i，不按的话，您只能看，不能吃。

我好不容易打完字，想退出。按Esc，没反应。我又乱按一通，它也不报错，直接把我每个键都当命令执行。我敲了一串hjkl，光标满屏乱跑，像在玩贪吃蛇。

我上网搜"如何退出Vim"，Stack Overflow上这个问题，两百多万人看过。两百万人！这哪是技术问题，这是失踪人口登记处。

最后同事告诉我：冒号，q，感叹号。我说感叹号干嘛？他说，意思是强制退出，不保存。

我突然懂了，这是唯一一个退出还得带情绪的软件：我不要了！我什么都不要了！

我有个同事用Emacs，十年了。我问他：你拿它干嘛？他说写代码、收邮件、记日程、看新闻。我说：那你这哪是编辑器啊？他说：对，这是操作系统。我说：那它缺什么？他说：缺一个好用的编辑器。

他退出要按 Ctrl-x 再按 Ctrl-c，两个Ctrl，全靠左手小指。现在他小指肿了，医生说是腱鞘炎，他说："不，这叫Emacs小指，是勋章。"

他每晚花两小时改 init.el，说是"为了以后省时间"。我问：省下多少了？他想了想说：我正在写一个函数，专门计算我省了多少时间。

我说：写完了吗？

他说：还没，Emacs在启动。

我有个朋友用Emacs十年了。我问他这十年写了多少代码，他说没多少，一直在改配置文件。

Emacs自称编辑器，其实是操作系统。里面有邮件、浏览器、俄罗斯方块，还有个心理医生，你敲 M-x doctor，它就问你："你为什么觉得烦恼？"我说就是因为你啊！

保存个文件，Ctrl-x Ctrl-s，两只手四个键，跟弹钢琴和弦似的。用上三年，小指开始疼，这病还有正式名字，叫"Emacs小指"。别的软件让你加班加出腰椎病，它让你加出小指病，还挺有个性。

最绝的是，很多人折腾半天，第一件事是装个 evil-mode，模拟Vim的键位。花十年配置一个编辑器，就为了让它假装成另一个编辑器。这就像娶了老婆，再把她整容成前女友。

Google Sheets is Excel's cousin who showed up to the family reunion and insisted everyone edit the same potluck dish at once. You open a file called "Untitled spreadsheet" and somehow it's the most permanent document your company owns. It's been "Budget FINAL v3 (Copy of Copy)" since 2017.

The best part is the real-time collaboration. Nothing says teamwork like watching an Anonymous Capybara delete your entire column while you're mid-formula. And you can't even blame Greg, because Greg is a capybara.

IMPORTRANGE is the only function that makes you beg a spreadsheet for permission to read your own spreadsheet. "Allow access." I'm sorry, I made both of these!

Then you hit a hundred thousand rows and the whole thing goes "Working..." That's not a loading message, that's a hostage video.

And QUERY? It's SQL for people who were told SQL was too scary, then handed something scarier.

你输个身份证号，Excel觉得你在输一个数。18位，它给你显示成3.1E+17。你点进去一看，后三位变成000了。它不光改显示，它还改你的人生。

最离谱的是，科学家拿Excel处理基因数据，有个基因叫SEPT1，Excel自动给它改成"9月1日"。结果不是微软修软件，是人类把二十多个基因改了名。我们为了迁就一个表格软件，给自己的基因改名。

还有单元格左上角那个绿色小三角，提示"数字以文本形式存储"。你点开，它给你一个选项，叫"忽略错误"。它明明知道有错，也不修，就给你一个按钮，让你自己忽略。

Google Sheets: the only software where you can watch a coworker named "Anonymous Capybara" ruin your formulas in real time.

You're the Excel that went to community college and told everyone it's "basically the same." Then someone adds 40,000 rows and you wheeze "Loading..." like a Chromebook climbing stairs.

Your formula for combining data from another sheet is IMPORTRANGE, which immediately yells #REF! until I click "Allow access," like I'm asking you to the prom. Your most advanced function, QUERY, makes me write SQL inside a text string, inside a cell, inside a spreadsheet. That's not a feature. That's a hostage video.

Every file on earth is named "Copy of Copy of Budget FINAL v2," shared with "anyone with the link," and owned by Brenda, who left in 2019. I click "Request edit access" and the void answers.

And the 10 million cell limit? Bold of you to assume anyone's budget is that organized. Mine is three tabs and a dream.

我特别佩服Excel，它比你自己更懂你想输什么。你输身份证号，它觉得你肯定是想看科学计数法，1.1E+17。你好不容易改成文本，它又只认前15位，后三位统统给你变成零。我就想问，我身份证后三位怎么你了？

更离谱的是，科学家输入基因名SEPT2，Excel说：这是9月2号。结果2020年，国际基因命名委员会被迫把基因改名了。注意，是人类给基因改名，就为了迁就一个表格软件。

还有VLOOKUP，找不到就甩你一个#N/A。你明明看见两个"张伟"一模一样，其实其中一个后面多了个空格。你看不见，它看得见，还偏不告诉你。它哪是查找函数，它是视力测试。

Windows Vista, you were the only operating system that asked permission to ask permission. "Are you sure you want to open Notepad?" Yes, Vista. I've been sure for twenty years.

You called yourself "Capable" on those stickers. Then you needed 15 gigs of RAM just to display a transparent window border. Aero looked gorgeous, though, like a beautiful man dying slowly of a mystery illness.

Remember copying a file? You'd say "Calculating time remaining" for six hours, like a mechanic staring at my engine going, "Hmm."

Microsoft shipped you, then immediately started apologizing with Windows 7. That's not a successor, that's a public apology with a Start button.

And "Vista Ready" laptops that couldn't run Vista? That's like a "Marathon Ready" sticker on a recliner.

Even your sidebar gadgets gave up. The weather widget just sat there, accurately predicting a cloudy future for everyone who bought you.

Windows Vista, the only operating system that asked "Are you sure?" before letting you breathe. You wanted to open Notepad? Cancel or Allow. You clicked Allow? Are you *really* sure? It had the confidence of a bouncer and the competence of a toddler.

Microsoft promised "Wow." Users said "Why?" Then "Where's my RAM?" Then "Where's my printer driver?" Then "Where's XP?"

It launched with a sticker that said "Vista Capable," which turned out to mean "Capable of displaying a sad blue spinning circle on your brand-new laptop."

Copying a file took so long that Vista estimated "20 minutes remaining," then "3 days," then "Discovering..." forever. Aero looked gorgeous, like a Ferrari with no engine.

Apple made an entire ad campaign out of mocking you, Vista, and the worst part is Microsoft just sat there, clicked Allow, and said "Yes, I'm sure."

Windows 8 looked at the most successful desktop interface in history and said, "What if we hid the Start button, like a bathroom in a haunted house?" Microsoft designed an operating system for tablets, then shipped it to people with keyboards, mice, and spreadsheets. Nobody asked for this. Accountants were suddenly swiping at monitors like they were trying to wipe off a stain.

Shutting down the computer required a PhD. You had to summon the Charms bar by hovering in the corner of the screen like a stalker, then click Settings, then Power, then pray. My grandmother spent twenty minutes looking for the off switch and just unplugged it. Honestly, she had the right idea.

And those Live Tiles! Forty colorful rectangles flipping around telling me the weather in a city I've never visited. It wasn't an operating system, it was a toddler's busy board.

Microsoft eventually admitted the mistake and brought back the Start button. Windows 8.1 was basically an apology note taped to the door.

Windows 8 was the only operating system that made you feel like a burglar in your own computer. You'd boot up, and there's no Start button. Microsoft just removed it, like a doctor deciding you've never needed a pulse.

Instead, you got a screen of giant colorful tiles, designed for tablets, which you didn't own, running on a desktop, which you did. Every app opened full-screen, so checking the weather meant your entire monitor said "72 degrees" at you in a font the size of a billboard.

And how do you shut it down? Hover your mouse in the top-right corner, wait for the Charms bar to appear like a shy ghost, click Settings, then Power. Four steps to turn off a computer. People Googled it. Millions of people Googled how to turn off their computer.

Then came the hot corners, where moving your mouse an inch too far opened things you didn't ask for.

Microsoft eventually apologized with 8.1 by bringing back the Start button. It just opened the tiles. That's not an apology. That's a hostage returning your shoe.

我们组的预算表是 Google Sheets，十几个人同时在里面改。你知道那种体验吗？你正在输数字，旁边突然冒出一个彩色小光标，名字叫“匿名水豚”。

我眼睁睁看着这只水豚走进我的单元格，把我的公式删了，然后走了。

我去点版本历史找凶手，上面写着：“匿名水豚，3月12日 下午3:47”。

我这是报警，不是看动物世界。公司没有水豚，它没有工号，没有户口，连表都是别人分享给它的。

后来我学聪明了，用 IMPORTRANGE 把数据引到自己的新表里。结果它弹个框：“你需要允许访问。”

我自己的表，要我批准我自己的另一张表来访问我自己。

最后还给我一个 #REF!。

我连一个错误，都不肯告诉我错在哪。

说起Windows Vista，它最大的创新就是：你干什么，它都问你一句"你确定吗？"

我就想打开个记事本，屏幕唰一下变黑，弹出一个框："Windows需要您的许可才能继续。"我看个txt，搞得像在银行转账。我点了允许，它又问我一遍。这哪是操作系统，这是我妈。

当年电脑上都贴着"Vista Capable"，意思是"能运行Vista"。真装上才发现，能运行，但不配好看。那个玻璃特效，得买贵的才有，你这台只能看灰的。这不叫能运行，这叫让你进场，但不给座位。

复制个文件，它显示"正在计算剩余时间"。算了四十分钟。它到底在算什么？我觉得它算的是我的寿命。

最后微软自己都看不下去了，出了Windows 7。那个广告词翻译过来就是："上次是我们不对。"

Vista这辈子最大的贡献，就是让一整代人，管Windows XP叫"怀旧"。

你们还记得Vista吗？那个系统最大的创新，就是让你每点一下都得被审问一遍。我就想把一个文件夹拖到另一个文件夹里，屏幕一黑，弹出来："Windows需要您的许可才能继续。"我说我是电脑的主人啊！它说："允许还是拒绝？"我点了允许。它又问："您确定吗？"

这哪是操作系统，这是我前任。

还有那个"Vista Capable"贴纸，电脑上明明贴着"支持Vista"。买回家一装，Aero玻璃特效没有，开个网页风扇转得像要起飞。人家说的"支持"，是支持你"安装"，不是支持你"使用"。

复制个文件，提示"正在计算剩余时间"，一算算了二十分钟。它不是在复制，它是在考虑要不要给你复制。

最后微软自己都扛不住了，赶紧推出Windows 7。那广告词翻译过来就一句：上次那个不是我。

Google Sheets最离谱的功能，是把加班变成动物园直播。

我晚上十一点改预算，右上角突然蹦出一个头像：匿名考拉。

我就懵了，我们公司没人叫考拉。但这只考拉，正在我的C14格里打字。

我改成五万，它改回八万。我再改，它再改。我俩一句话没说，在一张表里吵了十分钟。

我忍不住了，在旁边格子打了一行字：“你谁？”

它回：“你谁？”

第二天开会，老板说：“昨晚预算表挺热闹啊。”

我说：“您怎么知道？”

他说：“那只考拉是我。”

所以什么匿名，Google就是给你起个动物名字，让你被开除的时候显得比较萌。

Hawaiian pizza is what happens when Italy and a Dole pineapple can get into a fender bender and decide not to exchange insurance. It's a pizza that's also a fruit cup. The only dish where the ham is nervous about the dessert.

And it's not even Hawaiian! It was invented by a Greek guy in Canada. Hawaii had nothing to do with it. That's like naming a burrito "The Norwegian" because someone's cousin once ate one near Oslo.

Pineapple on pizza is like a hot tub full of juice. The cheese slides off, the crust goes soggy, and every bite is a hostage negotiation between salty and sweet. Ham and pineapple are the only couple at the party who came together but won't stand next to each other.

And somehow it's still the pizza ordered by the guy who says, "I'm easy, I'll eat anything," and then picks off all the olives.

Hawaiian pizza is what happens when Italy and a Dole pineapple can have a custody battle and nobody wins. It was invented in Canada, by a Greek guy, and named after a pineapple brand. That's not a pizza, that's a bad customs form.

Every other topping says "I'm here to be savory." Pineapple shows up like, "I'm also dessert. And I'm leaking." Now your ham is swimming in a warm fruit puddle, and the crust has the structural integrity of a wet napkin.

And the ham! Not even good ham. Sad, pink, circle ham, the kind that's been in a sandwich bag since a 2006 field trip.

Nobody orders it for themselves. It's always "I'll just get a Hawaiian for the table," said by the one guy who also says "I'm not really a *pizza* person."

Hawaii has never claimed it. Hawaii has been in court trying to get away from it.

Windows 8 我真的服了。我用了十年电脑，升级完，找不到关机。开始菜单没了，整个屏幕变成一堆五颜六色的方块，跟幼儿园墙面似的。我想关机，后来才知道：得把鼠标甩到屏幕右下角，等一个叫“超级按钮”的东西滑出来，点“设置”，再点“电源”，才看得到“关机”。关个机，像在玩密室逃脱。

我爸更狠，他以为电脑坏了，直接拔电源。这是 Windows 8 唯一一个全国人民都学会的关机方式。

后来微软听劝了，8.1 把开始按钮加回来了。你以为是开始菜单回来了？不，点一下，还是那堆方块。就像你投诉餐厅没有门，老板转身在墙上给你画了一扇。

Chicago deep-dish isn't pizza, it's a casserole that got a good agent. You wait 45 minutes for it, which is the only honest part, because the oven is basically doing a bypass in reverse. The waiter says "it takes a while," and he means "call your family and say something nice."

It arrives upside down: cheese on the bottom, sauce on top, like the pizza lost a bet. And the crust is a structural engineering project. It's not a slice, it's a core sample. You lift it with a spatula and the cheese stretches like it's begging you to reconsider.

Two slices and you're done. Not full, done. You walk out into a Chicago winter and honestly, the insulation helps.

New Yorkers call it soup in a bread bowl. Wrong. Soup has the decency to cool down. This stays molten until the first bite takes the roof of your mouth, as a deposit.

Chicago deep-dish isn't pizza, it's a casserole with an identity crisis. You order it, and they say, "That'll be 45 minutes." Forty-five minutes! For bread! I've seen people give birth faster, and the baby came out less cooked.

Then it arrives, and it's built upside down. Cheese on the bottom, sauce on top. That's not a recipe, that's a structural failure. It's a pizza that fell down the stairs and everyone decided to call it tradition.

You get one slice, and it requires a spatula, a fork, a knife, and a signed waiver. Your first bite is molten cheese lava. Your second bite is a tomato landslide. By the third, you're lying on the booth like you've been shot by a lasagna.

And Chicagoans defend this! "It's the real pizza." Sir, you eat soup with a crust and call New Yorkers wrong. That's a pie chart with a cardiologist.

Windows 8我用的第一天，花了十分钟找关机。因为开始按钮没了，微软觉得你不需要。后来我才知道：得把鼠标甩到屏幕右下角，等一个叫“超级按钮”的东西滑出来，点设置，再点电源，才能关机。关个电脑，像在输核弹发射密码。

而且这系统明显是给触屏设计的，可我用的是台式机。拿鼠标去划那些大方块，就像戴着拳击手套给人发微信。

后来8.1出来了，微软说：“我们听到了你们的声音，开始按钮还给你们。”我一点，蹦出来一整屏五颜六色的磁贴：天气、财经，还有一个我从没打开过的“人脉”。

门牌号是还给我了，可门后面开了家商场。

夏威夷披萨最离谱的地方，是它跟夏威夷一点关系都没有。发明它的是个在加拿大的希腊厨师，用的还是罐头菠萝。你想，一个人在零下二十度的天气里，对着一罐菠萝说：我想海滩了。然后把它扣在了火腿上。这就好比我在哈尔滨拿罐头黄桃炒了个饭，起名叫"三亚炒饭"。

吃的时候更精彩。第一口，甜的。第二口，咸的。第三口你开始审问自己：我到底是在吃主食，还是在吃甜品？而且菠萝一遇热就出水，披萨中间一汪小池塘，火腿在里面漂着。行，这下是有点夏威夷了，泳池派对。

意大利人看到这个披萨，那表情就像闺女领了个对象回家，一进门，对象是个罐头。

夏威夷披萨，你知道是谁发明的吗？一个希腊人，在加拿大，做了一道意大利菜，起名叫夏威夷。这就像我在北京开了家火锅店，招牌写着"巴黎小酒馆"。夏威夷人看到这个披萨都懵了：我们没做过啊，我们只是被冠名了。

更离谱的是，用的还是罐头菠萝。披萨一烤，菠萝汁全出来了，火腿泡在糖水里，整个披萨像一场小型海啸。你咬一口，芝士说咸，菠萝说甜，火腿站在中间，一脸"我只是来上班的"。

最惨的就是这块火腿。它本来是个正经的咸味员工，好好的在披萨上班，结果被公司拉去跟水果团建，还被要求"要融入"。

Durian, they call you the King of Fruits, which is wild, because you dress like a medieval mace and smell like a crime scene. You're the only fruit with a body armor package AND a hazmat warning.

You're banned from Singapore's subway, hotels, and airlines. Think about that. Nobody bans the pineapple. You're the only produce item that gets kicked off a plane before it even boards.

Your fans say, "Just get past the smell, the taste is heavenly." Sir, that's what every hostage says about their captor.

You taste like custard that's been cheating on a sewer with an onion. Eat one and your fridge smells like you for three weeks, your breath for five.

And you fall out of trees onto people's heads. You're not even content to be a bad meal. You want to be a *weapon*.

Durian, they call you the King of Fruits, which is wild, because you dress like a medieval mace and smell like a crime scene. Every other fruit says "eat me." You say "I dare you."

You're the only food with a gas leak. A Canberra university library was evacuated because of you. Evacuated! Fruit is not supposed to trigger a hazmat response.

Singapore had to put you on the subway sign with a big red X, right next to flamethrowers. Hotels ban you the way they ban smoking and goats.

And the flesh inside? Custard that tastes like sweet almonds, caramel, and a decision you regret. Fans say, "Just get past the smell." That's what people say about your cousin's boyfriend.

You're the only fruit that can kill me from the tree, and the only one I'd still blame the neighbors for.

第一次去芝加哥，我点了深盘披萨，服务员说：等四十五分钟。我说披萨不是快餐吗？他说，先生，这不是披萨，这是施工。

端上来就一块，我以为是前菜。铲子把它放进盘子，不是“啪”，是“咚”，像在埋东西。

我低头一看，最上面是番茄酱。奶酪被压在下面，酱在屋顶，这披萨是倒着盖的房子。

还得用刀叉吃。芝加哥人说这是传统。兄弟，需要刀叉的披萨，那叫千层面，你心里要有数。

吃完一块，我胃里像塞了块带馅的砖。朋友问：再来一块吗？我说不了，我现在这个体重，已经可以在芝加哥落户了。

在芝加哥点深盘披萨，服务员说：“得等四十五分钟。”我说披萨还要等？他说：“它不是披萨，是工程。”

端上来我才懂，这玩意儿是反着盖的：面饼在底下，奶酪垫中间，番茄酱浇在最上面。这就好比出门把内裤穿在裤子外面，芝加哥人管这叫超级英雄披萨。

还得用刀叉，外加一把铲子。我是来吃饭的，不是来做开颅手术的。一铲子下去，奶酪像岩浆一样拉出三米长，我感觉自己在挖地基。

一块就饱，第二块光是看着就饱了。芝加哥人还跟我说：“这才是真正的披萨。”不对，这是拿面饼当锅，炖了一锅奶酪，再浇一勺番茄汤。这要算披萨，那我妈做的千层面也是披萨，只是它比较谦虚。

Jackfruit, you're the only fruit that needs a permit to carry. You weigh eighty pounds, you're covered in spikes, and you grow directly out of the tree trunk like a tumor with ambition.

Cutting you open requires oiled knives, gloves, and a will, because you bleed glue. I've seen people stuck to you for three days. You're the only fruit that fights back like a bad breakup.

And the smell! Rotten banana, bubblegum, and gym socks, all in one. You're what Juicy Fruit becomes in a hostage situation.

Then vegans discovered you. Now you're in a can, drowning in barbecue sauce, pretending to be pulled pork. Jackfruit, you're a bland, stringy shredded mess in a tin, and you're lying to everyone. Even the tree looks at you and says, "I made that? And it's pretending to be a pig?"

Jackfruit, you're what happens when a watermelon gets a medieval weapons collection. You grow up to a hundred pounds, hang off the trunk like a tumor, and fall on people. You're the only fruit with a wrongful-death lawsuit hanging over your head.

Cutting you open requires oil on the knife, oil on the hands, and a signed waiver, because your sap is basically industrial glue. And inside? Yellow, stringy pods that smell like a gym bag soaked in bubblegum.

Then vegans discovered you. Suddenly you're "pulled pork." No. You're a fruit in a barbecue costume, sitting in sauce, hoping nobody checks your ID. Nobody's fooled. Even the vegans are just being polite.

You're Bangladesh's national fruit, which means a whole country looked at you and said, "Yes, that's us," and honestly, fair.

榴莲是唯一需要在酒店门口贴告示的水果。你什么时候见过"禁止携带苹果入内"？没有。只有榴莲，跟危险品并排站着。

这玩意儿全身都写着"别碰我"：外面是狼牙棒，里面是臭袜子。结果人类硬是徒手把它掰开，还往嘴里送。

最气的是摊主。你问"甜不甜"，他说"包甜"。你问"熟没熟"，他把榴莲怼到你鼻子底下："你闻！"大哥，我闻出来的只有"快报警"。

还有人说榴莲"闻着臭，吃着香"。这话怎么这么耳熟？这不是渣男的自我介绍吗？

吃完洗三遍手，味道还在。打一个嗝，整个电梯的人看你，像在看煤气泄漏。

所以我对榴莲的态度很明确：可以爱，但是请隔着一个国境线。

Luosifen, the only food that files a noise complaint with your nose. It's a noodle soup made from river snails, which is already a bold choice, then fermented sour bamboo shoots join in, and suddenly your apartment smells like a swamp got a divorce.

You open one packet and the whole building knows your business. Neighbors don't ask "what's cooking?" They ask "is someone okay?"

Liuzhou people say it's delicious. Sure, and a skunk says the same about its perfume.

And the cruelty is that it's actually amazing. Rice noodles, chili oil, peanuts, tofu skin, that sour-funky-spicy punch. You'll eat it and swear you'll never do it again, then smell your own hoodie three days later and whisper, "Same time next week?"

It's the only dish where the leftover smell outlasts the leftovers, and your elevator has stopped making eye contact with you.

Luosifen, you're the only food that comes with a smell warning from the neighbors. Nobody ever says "I'm having snail noodles" quietly. You announce yourself like a sewer breaking up with a pickle.

You're made from river snails, which is already a bold choice. Then you add sour bamboo shoots, which smell like a gym sock that was fermented in a gym sock. Real talk: the first time someone microwaved you in an office, HR held a funeral for the break room.

And the fans! "Just wait, the taste is amazing." Sure, so is a lottery ticket, but I'm not smelling like one for three days. Your broth is a gorgeous, glowing chili-oil red, like a warning light on a submarine, which is accurate, because I am now sealed inside with you.

Luosifen: delicious enough to eat, powerful enough to evict you.

榴莲是唯一一种有专属“禁止携带”标志的水果。地铁不让带，酒店不让带，待遇跟刀具一样。人家刀具起码不臭。

最离谱的是，爱吃的人还要劝你：“你就吃一口，吃了就爱上了。”这话我只在两个地方听过：榴莲，和传销。

它闻起来像煤气泄漏的臭袜子，吃起来却像冰淇淋。就像被绑架了，结果发现绑匪还挺会做甜点。你都不知道该报警，还是该把这块吃完。

两百块买一个，壳占九成，肉就那么三四块。吃完手臭三天，洗八遍没用。晚上牵女朋友的手，她闻了闻问我：“你刚从案发现场回来？”

我说：“对，凶手是我，受害者是我的钱包。”

Stinky tofu, you're the only food that needs a restraining order from its own neighborhood. I smelled you three blocks away and assumed a sewer had filed for divorce.

You're fermented in brine made of old vegetables, fish, and, as far as I can tell, regret. Then you're deep-fried, because apparently someone looked at a crime scene and said, "Needs crunch."

Everyone says, "Just try it, it tastes better than it smells!" That's not a compliment. That's what people say about a divorce lawyer.

And the fans! They stand in line at the night market, glowing with pride, like they've survived something. Sir, you're eating a gym sock in a pickle costume, and the pickle is also a gym sock.

Still, I'll admit it: the chili sauce is incredible. Which is exactly what you'd say about a hostage situation with good snacks.

Stinky tofu, you're the only food that gets a restraining order from its own neighborhood. I smelled you three blocks away and assumed a sewer had filed for divorce.

You're fermented in brine made of old vegetables, fish, and what I can only assume is regret. Then someone looks at that and says, "Let's deep-fry it." That's not cooking, that's giving a crime scene a crispy exterior.

And the fans! They say, "Just try it, the taste is nothing like the smell." Oh, so you're a liar with two personalities? Great. Very reassuring.

Every night market, there's a line of people holding their breath while paying for it. Nobody queues for something that smells like feet unless the feet are delicious, and somehow you are. That's the real insult. You smell like a gym sock's funeral, and I still came back for seconds.

你们见过整个的菠萝蜜吗？那不是水果，那是披着刺甲的婴儿，二十斤，抱回家还得拍嗝。

切之前，要先往刀上、手上抹油。因为它流出来的那个白浆，比502还黏。我第一次切，刀和我的手合二为一，从此不分你我。

好不容易剥开，一包一包黄澄澄的肉。吃一口，甜得像有人拿荧光笔在你嘴里签名。

最气的是，二十斤的东西，能吃的就一小碗，剩下全是皮、筋、渣，和你的尊严。

所以我现在只买盒装的。三十块钱十几瓣，我买的不是水果，是别人替我跟502搏斗的工伤费。

菠萝蜜不是水果，是一项工程。买一个十几斤，抱回家像抱着一个长满痘的婴儿。摊主还嘱咐：切之前，刀上抹油，手上抹油。我买个水果，怎么像准备去摔跤？

切开，全是白胶，粘得像502，手和刀直接结婚，洗洁精都劝不了离。

好不容易剥出一瓣，甜是真甜，但那味儿，像香蕉和烂菠萝在你嘴里开联谊会。而且每一瓣里都有核，吃一瓣吐一个，不像吃水果，像在嘴里拆弹。

最后十几斤，你吃了三瓣，剩下全塞进冰箱。第二天一开门，整个厨房都是它的味道，连冰箱里的剩菜都在发愣：我是谁，我在哪，我怎么也变甜了。

螺蛳粉最离谱的是名字。叫螺蛳粉，你吃半天，一只螺蛳都见不着。螺蛳只在汤里客串了一下，熬完就下班了。真正的主角是酸笋，那个味道怎么形容呢：像一双穿了三个夏天的球鞋，泡进下水道，然后有人问你，要不要尝尝汤。

袋子上写“开袋即食”，其实是开袋即报警。我同事在办公室拆了一包，保洁阿姨路过，问：“谁家管道爆了？”

最气人的是它还真香。吃的时候觉得人间值得，吃完发现头发、外套、整个电梯都替你记住了。上次我吃完坐电梯，进来一个人，吸了一口，默默按了下一层。他不是到了，他是在逃命。

Oat milk, you're what happens when a bowl of oatmeal gets ghosted and decides to live in a carton. You're not milk. You're oatmeal that went through a breakup and is now "finding itself" in a Brooklyn coffee shop.

You cost seven dollars, and for that, you taste like a wet cereal bowl that someone rinsed with regret. Baristas call you "creamy." You're not creamy. You're just thick, like the guy at the party explaining his podcast.

You separate in hot coffee like you've got commitment issues, then leave a gritty film at the bottom that feels like drinking a handshake from a sandcastle.

And the label says "Barista Edition." Barista Edition? Oh good, you've got a job title now. Cow's milk never needed a LinkedIn.

Your whole personality is "I'm not dairy." Congratulations. Neither is drywall, and it's got a better shelf life.

我朋友说，吃螺蛳粉之前你得先闻，闻完还不爱，说明你不懂生活。我闻了，我差点报警，我以为楼下化粪池开盖了。

关键是那个酸笋，一根好好的笋，被人泡到发酵，等于给笋办了场葬礼，然后我们把遗体煮了吃。

更离谱的是，叫螺蛳粉，碗里根本没有螺蛳。汤是螺蛳熬的，螺蛳早就下班了。你应该叫“曾经路过螺蛳的粉”。

最狠的是后劲。你中午吃一碗，晚上洗了澡，第三天坐地铁，旁边大哥突然看你一眼。你以为他嫌你臭，结果你自己闻了闻袖子，居然有点想念。

这就是螺蛳粉，它不是食物，它是一段关系：你嫌弃它，它缠着你，你离不开它，还得给它转三天账。

Oat milk, you're what happens when a bowl of oatmeal gets ghosted and starts a podcast. You're not milk. You're porridge that went through a breakup and a juice cleanse.

You cost eight dollars a carton, and the only reason is that a barista called you "creamy" once and you've been unbearable ever since. Cows have been doing this for ten thousand years for free. You needed an enzyme and a marketing team.

You separate in hot coffee like you're being deposed. You curdle at the first sign of acid, then expect me to drink you anyway.

And the label! "Barista Edition." For what? Standing near a espresso machine? You're a beige liquid with a gym membership.

Your whole personality is that you're not almond milk, which is the lowest bar in the dairy aisle, and somehow you still tripped over it. Sweet, slimy, smug. Basically a Sunday brunch in a carton.

Almond milk, you're proof that marketing can convince people to pay four dollars for cloudy water with a nut rumor attached. You're 2% almonds. Two percent! That's not milk, that's a homeopathic remedy for oat milk.

You took a nut that needs a gallon of water per single almond to grow, then sold yourself to people who say "I'm doing it for the planet." California is in a drought, Karen. Those bees are being trucked across the country like migrant workers just so you can ruin a latte.

And the texture. You're the only drink that separates in coffee like a bad breakup. Curdling in front of everyone, floating there in tiny shame flakes.

Your carton says "Unsweetened Original," which is two lies in a row. There's nothing original about you, and nothing about you is sweet.

You're what a cow would make if she gave up halfway through and just described milk to a nut.

臭豆腐是唯一把"变质"当核心竞争力的食品。别的豆腐放坏了，妈妈说扔了；它放坏了，老板说："这是老卤水，传了三十年。"那桶水比我年纪大，还比我家亲戚有话语权。

而且你永远是先闻到，再看到。隔着两条街，空气里就像有人把下水道炸了一下，你正想骂谁这么缺德，一转弯，排了二十个人。

老板还有句名言："闻着臭，吃着香。"这话只适用于臭豆腐。你跟相亲对象说"我这人闻着臭，处着香"，当场拉黑。

吃完我去坐地铁，整节车厢的人都在找味道的来源，只有我面不改色，因为我就是来源。

Almond milk, you're proof that a marketing team can convince people to pay four dollars for slightly beige water. You're 2% almonds. Two percent! That's not milk, that's a rumor of a nut passing through a carton.

You took one of the thirstiest crops in California, a state that's permanently on fire, and said, "Let's drink it, but make it weaker." A single almond needs about a gallon of water to grow, and you thanked it by diluting it back into water.

You curdle in coffee like you're having a panic attack. You separate in the fridge and need to be shaken like a Polaroid. And the ingredients list? Carrageenan, gellan gum, "natural flavors." Nothing says "plant-based wholesome" like sunflower lecithin doing the heavy lifting.

You're what a cow would invent as revenge: a drink so bland that dairy suddenly looks like a personality.

Still, I'll keep buying you. Nobody else lets me feel virtuous while eating cereal.

臭豆腐是唯一把缺点写进名字的食物。没有人卖"馊米饭"，没有人卖"糊了的烧饼"，只有它，大大方方告诉你：我臭。你还排队。

老板炸的时候，味道能传三百米。你分不清这是小吃街，还是化粪池剪彩。我每次都是鼻子在前面喊"别去！"，腿在后面说"没事，我们就看看"。

买完更惨。我拎着一袋坐地铁，整节车厢的人慢慢散开，给我让出一个圈。我手里是小吃，在他们眼里我是物证。

最气的是，吃一口，真香。老板那句"闻着臭，吃着香"，我以前觉得是广告词，现在明白了，这是受害者的共同口供。

现在咖啡店问你：要不要换燕麦奶？加五块。

我就想问，燕麦奶是什么？就是把麦片泡水、磨烂、过滤，剩下的那个汤。这玩意儿我小时候有个名字，叫"麦片没煮好的汤"，我妈当年是倒掉的，现在我花五块钱买回来。

包装上还写着"零乳糖"。废话，它压根就不是奶！燕麦又没有乳房，这奶是谁挤的？你见过哪个农民蹲在麦田里，一把一把地……那叫搓。

最离谱的是，我买的是"无糖"款，一喝，还是甜的。后来才知道，工艺里用酶把淀粉变成了麦芽糖。也就是说，它是一碗粥，不承认自己是粥，还想冒充奶，最后按奶的价钱收你的钱。

这不是饮料，这是粥的整容史。

Las Vegas, you're the only city where a $19 buffet costs $64 once you add the "resort fee," the "facility fee," and the emotional toll of the line.

You built a fake Eiffel Tower, a fake Venice, and a fake New York, because even your tourists said, "Sure, but can we get these somewhere hotter and sadder?"

It's 115 degrees, and the locals say, "But it's a dry heat." So is an oven, Brenda.

Everyone arrives in a bachelor party wearing matching shirts and leaves as a missing-person report with a wristband.

You have a million slot machines at the airport. You're the only place that starts taking your money before you've gotten your luggage.

And the Sphere? A billion-dollar glowing eyeball staring down the Strip, like even the city is judging your decisions.

What happens in Vegas stays in Vegas, mostly because it's your checking account.

Las Vegas, you're the only city where a $19 buffet requires a two-hour line and a signed waiver. You built a pyramid, a volcano, and the Eiffel Tower, but God forbid anyone find a clock. You've got no windows, no clocks, and no shame. It's 3 p.m. or 3 a.m., and either way a guy dressed as Elvis is selling me a "gentleman's club" flyer.

You call it a resort fee. I call it a cover charge to enter my own hotel room. Forty-five dollars for "amenities," and the amenity is a sad pool with a DJ who keeps yelling "Make some noise!" at dehydrated accountants from Ohio.

You're a desert pretending to be Venice, with gondoliers singing in a mall. It's 112 degrees and the canal is a puddle with a mortgage.

And the slot machines in the airport? Vegas, you're the only place that starts taking your money before you've even claimed your luggage.

现在咖啡店问你要不要换燕麦奶，加三块钱。燕麦是什么？就是早饭那碗糊糊。把糊糊过滤一下，只留上面那层汤，这东西我奶奶叫"粥汤"，以前煮完粥是倒掉的。现在装进纸盒，印个麦穗，加三块。

它喝着还有点甜，包装上写"无添加蔗糖"。对，它没加，它是用酶把自己的淀粉拆成麦芽糖。这不叫没加糖，这叫自产自销，自己给自己加。

最离谱的是倒进咖啡里。牛奶是融进去，燕麦奶是一絮一絮地飘着，像咖啡在掉皮。

又贵，又甜，还掉皮。我问店员为什么，他说："它是植物的。"咖啡豆也是植物啊，也没见谁加三块钱。

Macau, you're what happens when Portugal and Las Vegas have a one-night stand and nobody wants to claim the kid. You have a Venetian with fake canals, a fake sky, and a gondolier singing "O Sole Mio" in a Chinese province. Not even Italy does that to itself.

You make more gambling money than Vegas by a factor of several, which means you're basically a very successful casino with a cobblestone problem.

Your egg tarts are better than Portugal's, and everyone knows it, including Portugal, who's still mad. Your Eiffel Tower is half-size, your Parisian is half-French, and your Grand Lisboa looks like a golden lotus ate a disco ball.

You're 12 square miles and somehow have traffic jams at the border from people who lost everything and still want to come back. That's not tourism. That's an abusive relationship with a buffet.

Even your ruins are just a facade. St. Paul's is literally one wall. You couldn't keep the church, but you kept the slot machines.

现在咖啡店问你要不要换杏仁奶，加五块。我就想知道，这五块钱买的是啥？我专门看了配料表，杏仁含量2%，剩下98%是水。我花五块钱，买了一杯"见过杏仁的水"。

这玩意儿我们小时候就喝过，叫杏仁露，易拉罐的，过年走亲戚拎的那种。当年没人说它是奶，它就是个甜饮料。结果到了国外，换个包装，印上"植物基"，倒进拿铁，成了健康生活方式。

更绝的是，喝它的人说是为了环保，可一颗杏仁就要喝掉一加仑水。拯救地球的方法，就是先给杏仁灌满水，再把水榨出来，卖给你。

最后它一进热咖啡还分层，搅两下像豆腐脑发了脾气。我花五块钱，喝了一杯咖啡味的咸豆腐脑……哦不，是没放咸的。

Macau, you're Las Vegas that went to a Portuguese finishing school and came back with gambling debt and a custard tart habit. You make more money from gambling than Vegas does, but you're only 12 square miles. That's not a city, that's a casino with a postal code.

You've got a replica Eiffel Tower, a Venice with fake canals, and a Roman-style sky painted on the ceiling. Nothing here is original except the egg tarts, and even those are Portuguese. You even stole those, Macau, you just added a Cantonese accent.

The streets have Portuguese names, but nobody speaks Portuguese. It's colonialism's most elegant ghost town. Every sign is written in a language the entire population ignores, like a terms and conditions page.

And the traffic! A million tourists walking between hotels that are all technically the same hotel. You've got a Grand Lisboa shaped like a golden lotus, or as locals call it, a giant birdcage for losing gamblers.

Come for the ruins of St. Paul's. Stay because the ferry back to Hong Kong costs exactly what you have left.

我特别佩服杏仁奶。别的饮料是把好东西做成水，它是直接从水开始。你看配料表：水，杏仁2%。花比牛奶贵的钱，买一盒98%的水，加2%的"我认识一个杏仁"。那2%我怀疑是杏仁路过这盒水的时候，隔着包装点了个头。

还有人说它环保。可种一颗杏仁要用四升水，所以它是倒进去一大桶，换回来一盒水。

最惨的是倒进热咖啡里。牛奶进去叫融合，杏仁奶进去叫分手，当场絮成一团，咖啡面上漂着一层"我们不合适"。

喝之前，盒子上还写着：使用前请摇匀。我就想问，一个只有2%杏仁的东西，到底要我摇匀什么？摇的是那2%的自信吗？

我去拉斯维加斯，最服威尼斯人酒店。外面沙漠四十度，他们在室内挖了条运河，天花板还画了片天，永远是下午三点半的那种蓝。船夫给你唱意大利歌，我就想：我飞了五个小时来沙漠，是为了看一个假的意大利？

而且在拉斯维加斯你根本找不到路。酒店设计师就一个宗旨：从房间到电梯，必须穿过整个赌场。我下楼想买瓶水，穿过两百台老虎机，到门口已经输了二十块，水还没买。

酒店每晚还收四十美元"度假费"。我没度假，我在走路！从这家走到对面那家，看着一百米，走了四十分钟，因为中间要路过半个埃菲尔铁塔，真的是半个，比例缩小一半。

连法国人的浪漫，到了拉斯维加斯都得打五折。

Canberra is the only city in the world designed by an architect and then lived in by a committee. It's a capital built on a swamp, which was a bold choice, because nothing says "national pride" like a lake you dug yourself so the city would have something to look at.

Everyone's a public servant. Ask someone what they do and they say "policy," then spend forty minutes explaining that they can't explain it.

Roundabouts are the city's love language. You don't navigate Canberra, you get slowly interrogated by it. Exit two, exit three, back to Parliament House, you've been circling since March.

It's the only place where the nightlife is a Dendy cinema and a tense conversation about a briefing note. Even the fireworks are banned. The bush capital: eight months of frost, four of bushfire smoke, and one weekend where it's nice and everyone's at Floriade pretending they live somewhere better.

我去了拉斯维加斯，住威尼斯人酒店。人家在沙漠里挖了条运河，里面划贡多拉，船夫还唱意大利歌。我抬头一看，蓝天白云，我说真漂亮。他说，那是画的，这是商场。

你想想，外面是四十多度的真太阳，免费的，没人看。大家花钱进来，看一片画的天。

还有，我想下楼买瓶水，电梯一开，就是赌场。没有别的路，酒店是故意这么设计的。我走了十分钟，穿过两百台老虎机，每一台都在喊我：“来嘛来嘛。”我就想买瓶水啊！

水六美元。结账时还有一项“度假费”，一晚四十多。我问，我就睡在房间里，度什么假？前台说：“您正在度。”

最后，他们说：“在拉斯维加斯发生的事，留在拉斯维加斯。”

太对了。我的钱包，就留在那儿了。

Canberra is what happens when a committee designs a city and nobody's allowed to have an opinion until the subcommittee reports back. It's the only place where the lake is fake, the hills are decorative, and the excitement is a roundabout. Seriously, you can't give directions without saying "take the third exit, then the third exit again, then cry."

It's a city of 450,000 people, and 449,000 of them are named "Director of Strategic Alignment." The nightlife is a public servant having a second flat white after 2 p.m. Wild.

Every winter it hits minus five, and the locals call that "character." Every summer it's bushfire smoke, so basically a free vape.

And the Aussie icon is a giant flagpole. That's the whole personality: a pole, and a stern reminder to submit your timesheet.

Canberra: a nice place to visit if you've never wanted to.

Brasília, you're the only city designed by someone who looked at a map and said, "What if it were an airplane?" Congratulations, you're the world's largest piece of urban origami. Nobody can find anything because every address is a code. "I live at SQS 308, Bloco C, Apartamento 204." That's not a home, that's a Wi-Fi password.

You have no street corners. You have no sidewalks anyone uses. Brazilians love to gather in public, so you built a city where the only way to meet someone is by driving twenty minutes to stand near them.

Oscar Niemeyer gave you gorgeous curves, and then your politicians moved in and did the most corrupt things you could imagine inside them. A cathedral that looks like a crown of thorns, a Congress that looks like two bowls and a pair of dishes. Even the buildings look like they're waiting for a bribe.

You were built in four years. It shows. Rio had 400 to get charming.

去澳门，最诚实的景点是大三巴。一场大火烧得只剩一面墙，跟赌场里的人一模一样：正面看着特别体面，后面什么都没有。

澳门人太会照顾你了。威尼斯人里面有天空，假的，有运河，假的，船夫唱意大利歌，唱得比我高考听力还认真。赌场里没有窗也没有钟，你下午进去，出来的时候人家告诉你：后天了。

最温柔的是免费穿梭巴士。你赢钱的时候，没人送你。你输光了，立马有一辆车，空调开得足足的，把你从金沙一路送到关闸。这哪是巴士，这是全世界最体面的遣返。

我还排队一个小时买了葡式蛋挞。咬一口，烫掉一层皮，外酥里软，热气腾腾。吃完我明白了，这跟赌场是一个道理：先烫你一下，再让你觉得，要不，再来六个。

Brasília, you're the only city designed from above, which explains why it's miserable from the ground. You're shaped like an airplane, and honestly, that tracks, because everyone's just passing through and nobody's happy about the food.

Oscar Niemeyer built you in 41 months, and it shows. You have addresses like "SQS 308, Bloco C, Apartamento 204." That's not a location, that's a tax form with a doorbell.

You have no street corners. No one has ever bumped into anyone by accident. Pedestrians don't exist; they're a rumor spread by people with cars.

Your cathedral looks like a crown of thorns made by a very expensive lamp company. Your Congress has two bowls, one facing up and one down, because even your architecture can't decide whether it's receiving bribes or hiding them.

Rio gets Carnival. São Paulo gets money. You get a lawmaker who flies in Tuesday and flees Thursday. You're not a capital, you're a very large airport lounge with a flag.

澳门最让我佩服的是大三巴。一座教堂烧得只剩一面墙，现在是全城最火的景点。这是全世界最成功的烂尾工程，还没有业主维权。

然后去威尼斯人，里面的天空永远是下午四点的蓝。我问为什么，人家说赌场里不能让你知道时间。我才明白，那不是天花板，是缓释的"再玩一把"。

最自信的是那个免费接驳大巴：来的时候免费接你，走的时候免费送你。中间那段才收费，而且一次性收齐，不零敲碎打。

还有议事亭前地，人挤人，我排了四十分钟的队买蛋挞，吃完发现跟我家楼下那家差不多。但没关系，在澳门你排的不是蛋挞，是"我来过"。

Juicero raised 120 million dollars to build a $400 Wi-Fi-connected juicer, which is a lot of engineering for a bag you could just squeeze with your hands. And that's exactly what Bloomberg did. Reporters squeezed the pack by hand and got juice faster than the machine. The machine had four tons of force, and the whole thing was basically a very expensive way to say "no thanks, I'll do it myself."

It wouldn't even work offline. Your juice pack had to phone home to check if it was expired. Imagine being a kale-based hostage to a server in California. "Sorry, your carrots are out of date." Brother, I'm holding them. They're orange. They're fine.

And the packs cost eight dollars each. Eight dollars for a bag of chopped salad you'd then have to pretend was fresh-pressed. Silicon Valley looked at a smoothie and said, "What if it had DRM?"

Juicero didn't disrupt juice. It disrupted investors' bank accounts.

堪培拉怎么来的你知道吗？悉尼和墨尔本都抢着当首都，吵了十几年，最后澳洲政府说：你俩都别争了，中间找块羊场，另建一个。这是世界上唯一一座因为两个大城市互相看不顺眼而诞生的城市。

设计师是个美国人，满脑子理想，结果画出一城的环岛。我开车转了三圈，国会大厦路过我两次。

还有那个湖，人工的，专门淹了个山谷挖出来。别的城市是先有人，后有湖；堪培拉是先有图纸，人是后来被分配过去的。

周末去市中心，街上安静得像政府刚发了公告，没人想看。

堪培拉是澳大利亚首都，我每次说这句话，澳洲人自己都要愣两秒。因为悉尼和墨尔本吵了几十年，谁都不让对方当首都，最后各退一步：在两城中间找块荒地，从零造一个。这就像两口子争着不洗碗，最后决定：买个新碗。

设计师是个美国人，还挖了个人工湖，湖就叫他的名字。一座城市最大的景点，是设计师的签名。

路全是环岛，你在里面转啊转，转到怀疑人生，一抬头：又是国会山。这哪是城市，这是政治家的职业生涯。
