Juicero raised 120 million dollars to build a Wi-Fi-enabled juicer that cost 700 dollars, then 400 after they panicked. It had a press with four tons of force, enough to lift two Teslas. For what? Squeezing a bag of chopped kale.

Then Bloomberg proved you could just squeeze the bag with your hands. Same juice. No Wi-Fi. No app. No shame. Just a human fist doing the job of a venture-backed appliance.

And the packs! Sold separately, with expiration dates, so the machine would refuse to work if the bag was old. It's a juicer with a DRM problem. You couldn't even use your own fruit. It was a printer that squeezes.

The founder looked like someone who'd raised money by describing a smoothie as "infrastructure."

Google Ventures invested, which makes sense. Nobody does disrupting a squeeze like people who've never had to do one.

Juicero shut down in 2017, a rare startup where the customers' hands outperformed the product, and the product still had a better pitch deck.

Keurig, you took the simplest thing humanity ever did, pouring hot water over beans, and turned it into a subscription-based hostage situation. You charge me fifty cents for a thimble of coffee wrapped in a tiny plastic coffin that will outlive my great-grandchildren.

The inventor of the K-Cup literally apologized for it. The guy said he sometimes regrets inventing it. Your own father looked at his creation and said, "Yeah, I'd undo that."

And the machine itself? You push one button and it screams like a dying dial-up modem, then dribbles out something called "Bold" that tastes like a warm handshake from a wet paper bag. Every morning it flashes "Descale Me" like a needy ex. Meanwhile your water reservoir holds enough for exactly one bad decision.

Offices love you because nothing says "we value our employees" like a sad pod carousel next to a broken microwave.

Keurig: for people who want coffee, but also want to feel something about landfills.

Keurig, you took the simplest thing in the world, hot water meeting coffee, and turned it into a subscription-based hostage situation. My grandfather made coffee with a pot and a prayer. I make it by stabbing a tiny plastic hockey puck in the face.

You've created a machine that takes four minutes to warm up just to produce eight ounces of something that tastes like a mug rinsed in a wet cardboard box. And that little pod? Thousands of tiny plastic cups, each one lasting longer than my last three relationships.

Then there's the "descale" light. Every few months it screams at me to run vinegar through it, like a smoke detector for my own laziness. I ignore it, and the machine just sighs and gives me half a cup.

The best part is the "strong" button. It doesn't make it stronger. It makes it smaller. You invented coffee's version of "I'm not mad, I'm just disappointed."

巴西利亚这城市是从天上设计的，规划师说要建成一架飞机的形状。注意，是飞机，不是适合人住的东西。

所以在那儿问路，没人会说“前面路口右转”，因为没有路口，全是立交桥。地址长这样：SQS 308 C栋 102。这不是地址，这是导弹发射密码。我朋友住那儿，外卖小哥每次都要打电话问：“哥，你是在机翼上，还是在机身里？”

设计师觉得，你为什么要走路？你应该开车。结果对面明明就在眼前，你想过去得先绕一公里。于是行人自己在草坪上踩出了一条条小土路，直接穿过去。那是全城唯一不是规划出来的东西，也是唯一好走的东西。

还有国会大厦，一个碗朝上，一个碗朝下。导游说，这代表参议院和众议院。我觉得更准确的解释是：朝上的碗，是用来接钱的；朝下的碗，是用来把事情扣住，不让你看的。

巴西利亚是从天上设计的，整座城市是一架飞机的形状。我就想问：这是给谁看的？住在里面的人，又没有一个是飞机。

这儿的地址也不叫地址，叫密码。朋友说他住 SQS 308 楼 C 座，我以为他在发射卫星。

城市还按功能分区：酒店区、银行区、电视台区。你想出门买瓶水，得先搞清楚这瓶水属于哪个区。

最绝的是，这城市没有街角。没有街角，就没有“街角那家面包店”。人活着最基本的念想，被规划掉了。

所以现在居民在草坪上踩出了一条条小路，因为设计图上，没给人走路留位置。

在巴西利亚，走路是一种民间起义。

Juicero，融资一点二亿美元，一台卖699美元。你以为它是水果扔进去就能榨？不，它只榨自家的果汁包。每个包上印着二维码，机器得先联网扫码，确认没过期才肯干活。

一台连着WiFi的机器，毕生使命就是挤一个袋子。

后来彭博社的记者发现，不用机器，徒手捏那个袋子，出汁一样快。

人家工程师花了那么多心思，造出一台四吨压力的机器，够把两辆特斯拉举起来。结果被一双手给替代了。你要是拿它举车，我还觉得物有所值。

创始人还很委屈，说我们卖的不是榨汁，是体验。

对，捏袋子的体验。你们699美元，把我手上本来免费的活儿，包装成了高科技。

Crocs are the only shoes that look like they were designed by someone who'd only had shoes described to them over a bad phone connection. "So it's a boat, but for your foot?" "Sure."

And the holes! Ventilation, they say. Which is great, because nothing says "protect my toes" like a shoe with a dozen open invitations for a dropped knife. They're the only footwear where a gentle rain and a kitchen spill both count as a personal attack.

Then there's the Jibbitz. You've taken a shoe that looks like a foam dinosaur egg and decided to accessorize it with a tiny plastic pizza. That's not fashion. That's a toddler's hostage negotiation.

And the strap! Pushed forward, it's "casual." Flipped back, it's "sport mode." Sport for what, Greg? You're carrying a rotisserie chicken to a barbecue.

Yet somehow, they're unbelievably comfortable. Which is the cruelest part. Every nurse, chef, and gardener secretly knows: they look like a mistake, and they feel like a hug. Crocs are ugly on purpose, and they won.

Juicero，硅谷那个榨汁机，融资一点二亿美元，卖过699美元。它最厉害的地方是：不让你放水果，只能放它家的果汁包。榨汁机，不榨水果，榨"包"。

后来彭博社发现，根本不用机器，徒手捏那个袋子，出汁更快。机器用了四吨的力，我用的是……手。

更离谱的是它还联网。每次榨之前要扫二维码、连Wi-Fi，确认这包果汁没过期。一台榨汁机，先上网查一下这袋能不能喝。我自己闻一下就知道了，人家融了一点二亿美元，就为了替我闻一下。

最后公司倒闭了。你说它冤吗？它是死在一个最简单的问题上：您这台机器，到底比我的手多了什么？答：Wi-Fi。

Crocs are the only shoes that look like they were designed by a toddler and approved by a plumber. They're what happens when a boat shoe gets hit by a truck and the truck is made of cheese.

And the holes? Those aren't "ventilation." Those are tiny windows so everyone can watch your sock make a terrible decision.

You know what's wild? They sell charms for them. You can pin a little taco to a shoe that already looks like a bath toy. That's not accessorizing, that's decorating a pool float.

The heel strap flips back and suddenly it's "sport mode." Sport mode! For what sport? Competitive gardening? Walking to the fridge at 2 a.m.?

And they're comfortable, which is the cruelest part. Nobody can even make fun of them honestly. You just stand there, defeated, as a surgeon in neon green clogs walks past you with better arch support than your entire family.

UGG boots: because nothing says "I respect my feet" like dressing them as two sheepskin loaves that lost a fight with a puddle.

They're the only shoe that looks wet when dry and ruined when wet. One drop of rain and suddenly your boots have a water stain shaped like Ohio. And the tag says "do not wear in rain," which is wild for something that's basically a footwear sponge. It's a boot with a dress code.

Also, they're from Australia, but the company's in California, and the price is from the moon. Three hundred dollars for a shoe designed to be worn by surfers who just got out of the ocean, and somehow it ended up in a Pilates class in Connecticut.

And the smell. Wearing them without socks is a lifestyle choice, and it turns the inside into a warm, damp sheep sauna. You don't take them off. You release them.

UGG boots look like someone skinned a Muppet and asked you to wear the evidence. They're the only footwear where the sales pitch is "it's like walking on a cloud" and the cloud is a wet sheepdog.

Nobody's ever said "nice UGGs" without a tiny pause for mercy.

They're technically slippers that got promoted past their competence. You can wear them to the grocery store, but God help you if it drizzles, because suede plus water equals two damp loaves of bread strapped to your calves.

And the shape! Your ankle disappears. You walk in and a stranger thinks you have the legs of a Clydesdale. That's not a boot, that's a hoof cozy.

The inside smells like a gym bag in a sauna by month two, because they're meant to be worn sockless, which is a bold design choice for something with no ventilation and a lifetime of regret.

Also, they cost two hundred dollars. For slippers. That Australians apparently wear to surf, which tells you everything about Australians.

Keurig这机器，原理是拿根针，把一个塑料小杯上下各捅一个洞，然后管这叫早餐。这不是煮咖啡，这是穿刺手术。

它有个"Strong"按钮，我按了。你知道Strong什么意思吗？就是少给你放点水。不是咖啡变浓了，是咖啡变小了。我多花钱，少喝东西，它管这叫"强"。

最绝的是，发明K-Cup的那哥们后来公开说他后悔了。什么东西能让发明者自己出来道歉？核武器，和Keurig。

我一天就喝一杯，它还亮灯提醒我"除垢"。我买的不是咖啡机，是领养了一只会亮灯跟我要保养费的宠物。

Keurig 每天早上让我体验一次行刑：把手一拉，咔，两根针扎穿胶囊的头和屁股。我还没清醒，就先杀了一个小塑料杯。

它还有个"Strong"按钮，你以为是加浓？其实只是少放点水。就像我跟老板说"我想更努力"，结果是少干了一半活。

一杯一个塑料壳，喝完就扔。一年三百六十五个，我家垃圾桶才是咖啡喝得最多的。

最离谱的是那个除垢灯。它一亮，就让我拿白醋去洗它，洗完还得空跑十次水。一台本来伺候我的机器，现在换我伺候它。

我特别佩服Crocs的设计师。他琢磨鞋最大的敌人是什么？水。然后他给鞋打满了洞。这叫解决问题的最高境界：承认问题，然后放弃抵抗。

人家说洞是为了透气。行，可下雨天你一脚踩进水坑，那不是穿鞋，是脚泡进一碗鞋形的汤里。小石子也能随便进，进得来出不去，你一路走一路被按摩，主打一个免费足底服务，但不让你选力度。

最离谱的是那个洞里还能插小装饰，叫Jibbitz，二十块一个。一只塑料鞋，你往上插小草莓、小火腿。这鞋已经丑成这样了，你还给它打扮，这叫给一块豆腐戴耳环，豆腐没变好看，只是更好笑了。

但最可怕的是，真舒服。你嘴上骂它丑，脚已经把你卖了。

Monopoly is the only game where the winner is whoever gets lucky early and the loser is whoever's still playing at 2 a.m. It was designed to teach people that landlords are evil, and somehow it became the thing families play to prove it.

Four hours in, you've got a dad mortgaging Baltic Avenue, a cousin who "forgot" to charge rent, and a kid crying over the thimble. Nobody's ever finished a game. We just stop when someone flips the board.

And the money! You're handed pastel Monopoly bills like it's a deranged Easter egg hunt, then told you owe $200 for "income tax." In a game about capitalism, Free Parking pays out nothing, but everyone insists it does, because house rules are the only thing keeping this thing alive.

The best part: the shoe, the dog, and the iron are all fighting over Boardwalk. Meanwhile, the Community Chest says I won second place in a beauty contest. Ten dollars. Great.

Crocs的设计理念我想了很久：先做一只船，再拿叉子在上面戳。

商家说洞是为了透气。对，透气，顺便透沙子、透雨水、透小石子。下雨天走一步"呲"一声，像踩了只愤怒的青蛙。

最离谱是后面那根带子，翻到后跟叫"休闲模式"，翻到前面叫"运动模式"。什么运动？逃跑吗？穿着它我唯一能做的运动，就是逃离自己的审美。

还有人往洞里插小饰品，鞋六十，挂一排比鞋还贵。你这不是穿鞋，是脚上养了个塑料花园。

最气的是，它真舒服。我骂了一天，回家第一件事，换上。

丑是真丑，舒服是真舒服，它就是脚上的渣男。

Monopoly is the only game where "fun for the whole family" ends with Dad flipping the board and Grandma cackling over Baltic Avenue.

It's a game about capitalism that takes the worst part, landlords, and makes it a personality. Nobody's ever said "I'll trade you Boardwalk" without ruining a friendship.

The rules say it takes ninety minutes. Liar. I've seen Monopoly games outlive marriages. By hour four, one kid owns everything, three people are mortgaged to the hilt, and the fifth player is in jail, which is honestly the best seat in the house.

And the jail! You can pay fifty dollars to leave, which is what we call "bail reform for people who own a thimble."

Nobody follows the real rules either. Free Parking jackpot? Made up. Auctions? Skipped. Everybody plays by "house rules," which is just a fancy way of saying every family cheats differently.

Best part: the game was invented to show how monopolies are evil. Then Parker Brothers sold it, and the lesson was lost to the one who owns the railroads.

UGG这个雪地靴，名字就有问题。叫雪地靴，可你真敢踩雪吗？麂皮的，雪一化，鞋面开始长地图。我见过最勇敢的UGG，北京下雪天出门，走了五分钟，鞋头已经变成澳大利亚版图了。

店员还很热情：“姐，配瓶防水喷雾吧，一百多。”我花一千多买双雪地靴，还得再花钱保护它别见雪。这就像买游泳裤，销售说：“您千万别下水。”

还有这个造型，穿上脚立马大两码，像脚上绑了两个刚出炉的面包。上面羽绒服，下面光腿短裤，脚上两块面包，整个人就是一份行走的早餐。

最绝的是里面那层羊毛，捂一冬天，晚上一脱鞋，我怀疑那只羊都想申请回澳大利亚。

Risk is the only game where you spend four hours conquering the world and then lose it because your brother-in-law rolled three sixes in Kamchatka.

"Strategy game," the box says. Sure. Strategy is a dice cup deciding your destiny while you scream at a plastic cannon.

Nobody finishes Risk. It doesn't end, it just gets abandoned, like Napoleon's Russian campaign, except Napoleon had better snacks. Someone eventually says "I have to be up early," which is Risk for "I've been dead since Australia."

Speaking of Australia: everyone knows the whole game is just "hold Australia and pretend you're smart." One entrance, four territories, a bonus. It's the gated community of continents. Meanwhile Asia has twelve territories and a bonus of seven, which is the board's way of saying "go ahead, try it, I'll see you at hour three."

And the alliances! Friendships don't die in Risk. They get negotiated away for a single card.

Happy 60 years, Risk. You've ended more family dinners than politics.

Risk promises "world domination" and delivers a nine-hour hostage situation with plastic army men. Nobody has ever finished a game of Risk. We just stop when someone's mom needs the dining room table back.

Let's talk about the dice. You attack with three armies, I defend with two, and somehow I lose all three while you lose nothing. Math is a liar, and it lives in that little red cup.

Australia is the only continent anyone wants, because it has one entrance and the emotional stability of a hermit. Meanwhile Asia has seventeen borders, and holding it is like being the manager of a Wetherspoons on Saturday night.

And the alliances! "Let's team up against Dave." Then you betray me in Kamchatka. Kamchatka! A place no one has ever been or will ever visit, and yet it's responsible for more ruined friendships than any ex's Instagram.

Risk isn't a game. It's a divorce with cards.

UGG雪地靴，全世界唯一怕雪的雪地靴。我花一千八买的，店员第一句话不是"祝您穿着愉快"，是"建议您再买一瓶防水喷雾"。我才明白，这鞋不是穿的，是养的。

下雪天我出门，它比我还紧张，沾一点雪水就斑驳成一块一块的，像被狗认真舔过。再看那造型，低头一看，两只脚像刚出炉的吐司，我不是在走路，我是端着两块面包赶地铁。进了室内更精彩，羊毛一捂，脚汗一闷，感觉脚被塞进了两只湿透的绵羊。

后来我查了，这鞋最早是澳洲人冲浪上岸后暖脚穿的。好家伙，一个下水之后穿的鞋，怕水；一个叫雪地靴的鞋，怕雪。这哪是鞋，这是一个卖一千八的矛盾。

NFTs: the only product where you pay $300,000 for a receipt, and the receipt is for a JPEG, and the JPEG is still publicly available for free. You can right-click it. The whole business model is a guy pointing at the Mona Lisa saying, "Technically, I own the bookmark."

And the art! Eight thousand identical apes, each with a slightly different hat. That's not a collection, that's a hostage situation at a Hot Topic.

Remember when they said it was "the future of ownership"? Then OpenSea's servers went down and people learned their million-dollar monkey was just a link to a website that could 404. You didn't buy art. You bought a very expensive "Page Not Found."

And the guys who bought them still say "we're early." Early to what? The funeral?

Somewhere right now, a man named Chad is staring at a cartoon ape worth $14, whispering, "Floor price is just a vibe."

大富翁你们知道吗，最早是一个女的发明的，叫伊丽莎白·麦吉，她的本意是批判土地垄断，想告诉大家：房东太黑了，这样不行。结果呢，被一个推销员改改卖了。现在全世界的家庭围着一张桌子，认认真真学习怎么当黑心房东。

这游戏玩到第三个小时，已经没有悬念了。一个人手里全是深蓝色的地，盖满了红酒店，剩下的人拿着个小熨斗、小帽子，一圈一圈走，就为了给他交钱。

你说认输吧，不行，规则要你先抵押。我一个熨斗，我抵押什么？

最离谱的是监狱。这游戏里最安全的地方就是监狱。进去不扣钱，还照样收租，外面的人反而一直在交钱。到后期大家都在盼着抽到“入狱”。

最后全家吵得不可开交，说好了，最后一把，不玩了。然后你发现，弟弟当银行，银行里少了两千块。

整个游戏里，唯一没人监管的，就是银行。这一点，倒是挺真实的。

NFTs are the only product where "right-click, save as" is a legitimate threat to a billion-dollar market. You didn't buy art. You bought a receipt for a JPEG that anyone can look at for free, and the receipt is a hyperlink, and the hyperlink is hosted on a server that's going down when the startup runs out of money. Congratulations, you own a 404.

And the names! Bored Ape. Doodle. CryptoPunk. Nothing says "serious investor" like a man in a blazer whispering, "I'm down forty grand on a cartoon monkey, but the community is strong."

Everyone was a visionary until the gas fees showed up. You paid sixty dollars in Ethereum fees to buy a picture of a rock that was worth four dollars, then listed it for a million because a guy named xX_DiamondHandz_Xx said it would "flip."

It didn't flip. It just sat there. Like a rock.

大富翁最讽刺的一点是，它本来是用来批判垄断的。发明的人想告诉大家：地主，不是好东西。结果全世界拿到手的第一反应是：我要当那个地主。

这游戏还特别写实。你住别人一晚酒店，两千。然后你抽张机会卡：“恭喜你，选美比赛获得第二名，奖金十块。”十块！我刚给人家交了两千，你拿十块安慰我，这是什么选美，评委是房东吗？

还有监狱。别的游戏进监狱是惩罚，大富翁后期进监狱是避难。外面满地都是别人的酒店，我在牢里坐着，哪儿也不去，一分钱不用交。这是我在这游戏里找到的唯一社保。

最惨的是破产。你输了，但不让走。你得坐在桌边，看赢家数钱，还得帮忙递骰子。

一局打三个小时，我爸把我的小狗棋子抵押了，我妈把我的家卖了。我们一家人，从此没有亲戚关系，只有债务关系。

玩《战国风云》，我悟出一个道理：征服世界不难，难的是玩完。

这游戏最离谱的是澳大利亚。全图最安全的大陆，就一个入口，所以每个人开局都想要它。拿到的人守着印尼，一守三个小时，号称统帅，其实是在看大门。

再说骰子。我三个骰子打他两个，数学上我稳赢。结果我扔出一、二、一，他扔出两个六。我一万大军，死在两颗骰子手里，史上最贵的手滑。他还跟我说：“这就是战争。”这是战争吗？这是掷骰子！

最惨的是被淘汰的人。你输了，可你不能走，因为这是朋友局。你得坐在旁边，看剩下两个人在堪察加半岛来回打四个小时。我唯一的任务，就是去厨房拿薯片。别人征服世界，我是战场上最忙的后勤部长。

最后赢的那个人说“承让承让”，我心想：你让我什么了？你让我看了一晚上你拿骰子。

《战国风云》号称征服世界，其实是教你怎么跟朋友绝交。开局大家都抢澳大利亚，说是新手村，只有一个入口，易守难攻。对，你守了三个小时，守成了全球最安全的养老院，世界地图上最清净的地方，也是最没人记得你的地方。

最气人的是骰子规则：平局，防守方赢。我三个骰子冲上去，他两个骰子在家里坐着。我二十个兵打他三个兵，结果我死两个，他死零个。我问他，你一个守堪察加的凭什么？他说：规则。

玩到第五个小时，桌上只剩两个人，被淘汰的坐旁边吃薯片，还负责监督我们别算错。最后赢的那位举起手说：我统治世界了！我说，你统治的是一张桌子，而且是我家的。

Beanie Babies, the only investment where your financial advisor was a woman named Deb at a card shop. People kept them in plastic cases, like organ donors. Not toys, relics. "Don't touch Princess the bear, she's for college." Princess was a purple bear stuffed with plastic pellets and a dead princess's legacy, and your mom thought she'd pay for Yale.

The genius was the tag. Not the toy, the tag. Ty looked at a bag of beans and said, "What if we made it illegal to love this?" Bend that heart-shaped tag and you've lost four thousand dollars. Kids learned grief early: "I hugged Peanut the elephant, and now he's worth nothing."

Then the retirements. Ty killed off bears like a Game of Thrones writer with a mortgage. Fall for Squealer the pig and he's gone by Tuesday, replaced by a slightly different pig.

Today they're in a garage in Ohio, sweating in a bin, worth less than the bin.

Beanie Babies: the only investment where the advice was "don't remove the tag" and everyone said, "Sounds legit." Parents in 1998 put them in plexiglass cases like they were the Hope Diamond. It was a bean-filled bear named Garcia. You were hedging against a tie-dye pig.

Every one had a poem on the tag. "Legs the Frog" had a poem. Why? Nobody asked Legs to be a poet. Legs just wanted to sit on a shelf and appreciate the lack of structural support.

And the "retired" thing. Ty would announce a toy was retired, like it had served in a war. Suddenly your aunt's driving to a Hallmark in Ohio at 4 a.m. for Princess the Bear, a bear dedicated to a dead woman, which is a hell of a thing to put a price sticker on.

People paid thousands for these. Today they're worth less than the pellets inside. Which is the only part that was ever real: plastic pellets, fear, and a very small heart-shaped tag.

有人花三百万买了个NFT猴子头像，我问他：你买的到底是什么？他说：链上的所有权证明。我说：那图呢？他说：图不在链上，图在一台服务器上，链上存的只是一个网址。

所以他花三百万，买了一张"网址的收据"。

我说那我右键另存为，这猴子我也有了。他说：你那是复制品。我说：那你的是什么？他说：原件。我说：俩长得一模一样，区别在哪？他想了想说：区别是我花了三百万。

这就是NFT的全部技术含量：给你的冤大头身份做了区块链公证，永久保存，不可篡改。

最惨的是，哪天那台服务器欠费了，他的猴子就变成一个裂开的小图标。人家有钱人收藏名画，他收藏的是404。

Slack, you took "this meeting could've been an email" and made it "this email could've been forty-seven threaded replies and a thumbs-up emoji."

You've got a green dot next to my name, which means my boss thinks I'm available. I'm not available. I'm just *loaded*. There's a difference, and it's called a bathroom break.

Every Monday, "Hey" arrives with no follow-up. Just "Hey." Then three dots appear, disappear, appear, disappear. Is she typing a novel or a resignation?

You gave us channels, and we made #random, #random-2, and #random-actually-random. Somewhere, a guy named Doug is in forty-one channels and has muted forty. He reacts to everything with a salute emoji and calls it leadership.

And that notification sound? That little knock-knock-knock? Pavlov would've been proud. I flinch at wooden doors now.

You're not a productivity tool. You're a very expensive way to watch coworkers say "circling back."

我研究了半天NFT，终于搞明白了：你花三十万买的那只猿猴，链上存的根本不是图片，是一个网址。你买的是一张写着"图在哪"的小纸条。

更绝的是，存图的服务器哪天不续费，你的猴子就直接404了。三十万，买了一只会失踪的猴子。

我朋友不服，说："我拥有它！"我说那我右键另存为，我也拥有了。他说："你那个没有证书。"证书是什么？就是账本上写着：0x开头一串乱码，对应这个编号。

所以他花三十万，外加手续费，买了个"我是我"的收据。而且那个gas费，比图本身还贵。图是免费看的，免费存的，免费当头像的，就连我，也免费当过他头像的头像。

他唯一独家拥有的，就是那串乱码。

可他还特骄傲，天天跟我说："你懂吗，这是去中心化。"

我懂，就是丢了，连个找的人都没有。

Slack, the only place where "Quick question" is a threat. Nobody has ever had a quick question. Just a little typing bubble that appears, disappears, appears again, and then nothing, like a ghost deciding whether to haunt you.

You took email, which everyone hated, and said, "What if it were faster, and your boss could watch you be green?" Now I can't go to the bathroom without my status turning yellow like I'm a traffic light of shame.

And the notifications. That little red badge. Forty-seven unread in #general, which is just a graveyard of birthday gifs and a guy named Doug asking who took his yogurt.

The emoji reactions are how adults now communicate. A thumbs-up means "I acknowledge you." The eyes emoji means "I saw this and will do nothing." And the little checkmark means "done," which is the biggest lie since "let's circle back."

Slack: you replaced meetings with meetings that never end.

九十年代，美国人集体发疯，把一袋塑料颗粒缝的小熊当理财产品。

最离谱的规则是：标签不能剪。你买个玩具，不能玩，一玩标签就皱，皱了就不值钱。你抱的不是熊，是一张会掉毛的股票。

标签上还写着它的生日和一首小诗。一只填了半袋塑料粒的鸭嘴兽，有生日，有诗，还会"退休"。它没死，它退休了，价格涨三百倍。

更狠的是，真有夫妻离婚时在法庭上分豆豆娃。法官说："黛安娜王妃熊归女方。"男的急了："那就是个熊！"法官说："那是你们的养老金。"

后来泡沫破了，大家才发现，所谓绝版，就是工厂一边猛做，一边假装不做了。

现在它们全躺在阁楼里，标签完好无损，从没被人抱过。这是世界上保存得最好、被爱得最少的熊。

豆豆娃你们还记得吧？九十年代，美国大人为了抢一只肚子里塞塑料颗粒的小布熊，在店门口打架。

最绝的是那个心形吊牌。吊牌一折，价值减半。也就是说，这玩具的正确玩法是：别玩。一个给小孩的东西，唯一的使用说明是"别让小孩碰"。

我邻居囤了三百只，说是给孩子攒大学学费。结果呢？每只都是"绝版限量"，可全世界有几亿只"绝版"。

现在孩子大学毕业了，那一箱紫色小熊还在车库里，隔着透明吊牌保护壳，静静看着他还学贷款。

它们倒是保护得挺好，就是没保护住任何人。

Microsoft Teams is the only app that can notify you about a message you're already reading. You've got a red badge, a yellow badge, and a little purple "@" telling you someone said "per my last email" in a chat called "Q3 Sync (Copy) (Final)."

Teams has seven ways to say hello and none of them load. "Joining meeting..." is its resting state. It's the Waiting for Godot of video calls, except Godot eventually shows up and says, "Can everyone see my screen?" No, Greg. We see a spinning circle and your cat.

Every update, it asks you to restart. Not the app. Your life choices.

Teams and Channels are different things, by the way. A channel lives inside a team. Which is inside a tenant. Which is inside a guest account you can't switch out of without signing out of everything and crying.

And the green dot? It goes yellow the second you stop moving your mouse, so your boss thinks you're napping. Ten minutes of reading a document is considered a vacation.

Microsoft Teams is the only app that can tell you "You're on mute" after you've spent four minutes giving the best speech of your career to nobody.

It's got a notification system that works like a clingy ex. Someone reacts with a thumbs-up to a message you sent three weeks ago, and suddenly your laptop sounds like a submarine under attack.

The search function is a magic trick: you type "Q3 budget," and it shows you a GIF from Brenda's retirement party.

And the name! "Teams." Also "Teams (work or school)." Also "Teams (free)." Also "Teams Classic," which is what we now call the one that worked slightly better. Whenever you open it, it asks which Teams you want, like a waiter asking which of your three identical sandwiches you'd like.

The status indicator says "Away" when you're staring right at it, and "Available" when you've gone to the bathroom.

Teams isn't collaboration software. It's a hostage negotiation with your own Wi-Fi.

LaTeX is the only software where you spend six hours fixing a typo and then twelve more because the fix moved your figure to page nine.

You ask for a picture to go *here*. LaTeX says "here" is more of a "float" situation. It's not a placement, it's a vibe.

The error messages are written by someone who hates you personally. "Overfull hbox, badness 10000." Thank you, I'll tell my therapist. Meanwhile, one missing brace gives you an error on line 4,000, in a file you didn't write, from a package you never installed.

Want a different font? Enjoy a three-day journey through Stack Overflow, where the top answer is from 2009 and starts with "Just use XeTeX."

And the compile times! I changed one comma and now I'm watching it run twice, because the table of contents needs to catch up to reality.

Knuth released it in 1978 and declared it nearly bug-free. Sir, the bugs are in me. I'm the bug. I just wanted a bibliography.

Slack这个词的意思是"松懈、偷懒"。公司给我装了个叫"偷懒"的软件，然后我一天到晚不敢偷懒。

那个绿点，亮着代表我在线。我蹲厕所它也亮着。领导一看：小王在线，@here 有个小事。永远是"小事"，永远是"here"，永远是我。

还有"对方正在输入……"。老板打了三分钟，停了，又打，又停。我盯着那三个点，心想：你是在写通知还是写遗书？最后发来俩字："没事。"

最恐怖的是那个👀表情。同事给我点个👀，意思是"我看到了"。不处理，不回复，就是看到了。像小区监控，救不了你，但会留证据。

LaTeX is the only software where you spend three hours making a document look "professional" and one minute actually writing it.

You want a picture next to some text? LaTeX says, "Sure, I'll put it on page nine. Floating. Like your hopes."

The error messages are written by someone who hates you personally. "Missing $ inserted." Missing WHAT? I'm a grad student, I haven't seen a dollar since 2019.

Compile once, and the table of contents is wrong. Compile twice, it's right. Compile three times, and now the bibliography has vanished. It's not software, it's a séance.

Everyone says, "Just use a template!" Sure, let me paste in forty packages I don't understand, and pray hyperref doesn't fight with the other thirty-nine.

And the people who love it? They'll tell you, "It handles equations beautifully." Yes, Greg, and my Honda handles beautifully too, but I don't build the engine from a text file to drive to Costco.

Knuth wrote it in 1978 and said it was done. That's the only deadline in history met by being declared finished.

我们公司用Slack，它最厉害的是，把“打扰别人”变成了一种礼仪。

你看那个“对方正在输入……”，三个点跳了五分钟，我盯着它，像等产检结果。最后蹦出来俩字：“在吗？”我说在。他又开始输入。又五分钟。“没事。”

没事你输入五分钟？你在写遗嘱吗？

还有那个绿点。绿点的意思是“我在线”，但在线不等于想被找到啊！就像你家灯亮着，不代表你想让人敲门。我现在都不敢合电脑，一合，绿点变灰，同事以为我没了。

最绝的是表情回应。老板发条通知，底下一排👍。以前我以为这是礼貌，后来才懂，这是Slack发明的“已读不回，但显得很积极”。

昨天我也点了个👍，三秒后老板私信我：“所以你同意了，那这事你来做？”

我就知道，那不是点赞，那是签字画押。

Microsoft Word, you've had thirty years to learn what I want, and you still think I'm trying to write a bulleted list every time I type a dash.

You've got a paperclip's worth of trauma in your past, yet you still auto-correct "Costco" to "Cost co" like you're editing a ransom note.

I insert one picture and the whole document rearranges itself like furniture in an earthquake. The image jumps to page nine, the text wraps around it in the shape of a gunshot wound, and page four is now blank for reasons known only to God and a hidden section break.

You have a ribbon with 400 buttons, and the one I need is always under "Layout," which is somehow not where the layout is.

And "Not Responding"? Buddy, I just asked you to save. Then you recover my file as "Document1 (Autorecovered) (Copy) (2)," like a witness protection program for my thesis.

公司说用Teams能提高效率。我现在最大的效率，就是登录。每次打开它先问我：用工作账号，还是个人账号？我两个都有，选哪个它都说“我们遇到了点问题”。什么问题？不说。跟相亲对象一句“我们不合适”一个路数。

还有那个状态灯。领导头像是绿的，我发消息三小时没回。后来才懂，绿灯不是“他在”，是“他电脑没锁屏”。人早回家了，Teams还在替他撒谎。我这边更惨，上个厕所，鼠标三分钟没动，立马变黄，“离开”。全公司都知道我去哪了。

最绝的是文件。我明明是在聊天里发的，一个月后找，它告诉我：文件在SharePoint里。SharePoint在哪？没人知道。这不是办公软件，这是藏宝图，而且宝藏是我自己的PPT。

Teams这软件，最大的功能不是开会，是锻炼耐心。每次点开，先转圈，然后弹出一行字：“正在为你更新”。我就想问，我只是想开个九点的会，你更新什么？等它更新完，会都散了。

而且它有个状态灯，鼠标十分钟不动就从绿色变成黄色“离开”。我老板就盯着这个灯。我上个厕所回来，他在群里问：“你刚才去哪了？”我说我在思考。他说：“思考你怎么是黄的？”

现在我桌上放了个自动晃鼠标的小玩意儿。它绿灯常亮，从不请假，比我更像员工。

最离谱的是登录。弹窗问我：“用工作账号还是个人账号？”我两个都试了，它回我：“出了点问题。”

这软件名字叫Teams，团队。想想也对，团队精神嘛，就是大家一起出问题。

Microsoft Word, you're the only software where pressing Enter once can rearrange my entire document like a Rubik's cube in an earthquake.

You've got a paperclip-shaped trauma in your past, and honestly, he was the only one who ever tried to help. Now it's just you, auto-correcting "ducking" into things I definitely didn't mean to say to my boss.

Bullet points? You take them personally. I press Tab, you indent. I press Backspace, you un-indent, delete the bullet, and change the font to Comic Sans out of spite.

I tried to put one picture on page two. Page six now has a single sentence and a sense of dread.

And the green squiggly line? Judgmental. The red one? Fine, I misspelled "necessary." But you underlined my own name like I'm the one who's wrong.

You've been around since 1983 and still can't tell me why Save As has seven different locations. Ribbon? More like a ribbon of confusion. Truly, you're a masterpiece of formatting I never asked for.

我写论文用LaTeX，都说它排版漂亮。对，前提是你能编译过去。

我就在一个单词里打了个下划线，它报错：Missing $ inserted。让我插一个美元符号。我写论文呢，你管我要钱？

最气的是引用。PDF里全是。不是我没引，是得编译两遍。第一遍，它先认识一下参考文献；第二遍，才好意思告诉你。跟相亲一样，第一次只是互相看看。

还有图片。我写的是放这儿，它说“好的”，转头飘到第五页去了。这个东西官方名字就叫float，浮动体。起名倒是诚实，从来没保证过落地。

折腾三天，终于通过：0 error，37 warning。其中一条是Overfull hbox，意思是我这一行太满了。

我写个论文，还被它说胖。

text:
我用LaTeX写论文，朋友问：为什么不用Word？我说，因为我喜欢排版好看，和一屏幕的报错。

别的软件报错，会告诉你哪里错了。LaTeX告诉你：“Missing $ inserted。”我一篇论文哪来的美元？我要是有美元还用写论文吗？

还有插图。你写，意思是请放这儿，它不听。写，它假装听。写，它直接飞到第七页，像在说：“这是我深思熟虑后的决定。”

最离谱的是目录和引用，要编译两遍。第一遍它说：“我不认识这个人。”第二遍它说：“哦，想起来了。”这是编译器，还是在做笔录？

好不容易编译通过了，满屏黄字：Overfull hbox。它管这叫“警告”，意思是我知道有问题，但我不改，你自己看着办。

最后我发现，我花三个小时，就为了让一个表格别超出页边距零点三毫米。

text:
Graphene, the "wonder material." Twenty years of wonder, and the only place I've seen you is in press releases.

You're pencil lead that got an agent. You're literally graphite, but one layer thick, because even carbon wants to be an influencer: all surface, no depth.

They discovered you with Scotch tape. Two guys peeled you off a pencil mark and won a Nobel Prize. That's the most successful thing anyone has ever done with office supplies, and you've been coasting on it ever since.

Stronger than steel! Conducts better than copper! Transparent, flexible, and every article says you'll change everything "within five years." You've been five years away since 2004. You're the Cybertruck of chemistry.

And scaling you up? Impossible. You're perfect in a lab and a wrinkled, expensive mess in a factory. Honestly, you're the most impressive thing a pencil ever did, and also its biggest disappointment.

Graphene, you're the most overhyped thing ever pulled off a pencil with Scotch tape. That's your origin story: two guys got a Nobel Prize for peeling you off graphite like a sticker off a banana. Meanwhile I can't get a Nobel for peeling the plastic off a new remote.

You're one atom thick, stronger than steel, more conductive than copper, and nearly transparent. You're also the only thing in science that's invisible and still manages to be full of yourself.

For twenty years you've been "five years away" from changing everything. Foldable phones, space elevators, unbreakable everything. And what do I have? A tennis racket. A really nice tennis racket.

You have no bandgap, so you can't even work as a decent transistor. You're the smartest kid in class who refuses to turn in homework.

You're just carbon in a honeycomb pattern. Your cousin is literally a diamond, and your other cousin is in my pencil case.

Carbon nanotubes, you've been "five years from changing everything" since 1991. Thirty-plus years! Fusion power looks at you and says, "Take it easy, pal."

You're a hundred times stronger than steel, but only if you're one perfect, flawless, microscopic strand that nobody can actually make longer than a hair. Basically you're a gym bro who can bench a truck but only if it's in a vacuum, and he's the size of a bacterium.

You're just rolled-up graphene. You're a sheet of pencil lead that got into a yoga class and now thinks it's special.

Every grant proposal says you'll build a space elevator. Meanwhile, the only thing you've actually lifted is my hopes and a tennis racket.

And toxicologists say you act like asbestos in the lungs. Incredible range: strongest material ever, also a lawsuit.

You're not the future. You're soot with a publicist.

你们有没有发现，Word里最有主见的不是人，是图片。我在第三页插了张图，往左拖一厘米，它直接跳到第七页去了。我这文档一共五页，它自己开了个分店。

更离谱的是最后那页空白页。你想删，退格键按烂了，它纹丝不动。后来我查了才知道，是因为上一页末尾有个表格，而Word规定表格后面必须留一个段落。也就是说，Word觉得表格需要一个出口。我论文写到凌晨三点，都没人给我留个出口。

最后你改完，Ctrl+S，关掉，它还弹窗问你："是否保存对文档的更改？"我不保存，我改它干嘛？我是来给它请安的吗？

Carbon nanotubes, the material that's been "ten years from changing everything" for thirty years. You're 100 times stronger than steel, and yet somehow you've never held a job.

You're a single sheet of graphene rolled up like a sad burrito, and you still can't decide if you're a metal or a semiconductor. Chirality, right? Your entire personality depends on which way you twist. That's not physics, that's a mood ring.

Scientists say you could build a space elevator. Buddy, you can't even get through a lab without clumping together like earbuds in a pocket. Every researcher spends six months trying to disperse you, then writes "uniform" in the paper anyway.

And the manufacturing! Everyone gets a random mix of types, so sorting you is like trying to separate identical twins by vibe.

Also, you're a nanometer wide and somehow still the biggest thing in everyone's grant proposal.

我特别佩服Word的一个功能：删除空白页。
第四页，明明白得干干净净，你就是删不掉，按了十七下Backspace，它纹丝不动。后来网上告诉你，那页有个看不见的东西，叫“分节符（下一页）”。
看不见，但它在，这不是软件，这是闹鬼。

还有自动编号。你打个“1.”回车，它贴心地给你来个“2.”。你说不要，它就改成“一、”。你再撤销，整篇变成“第1章、第1章、第1章”。

最气的是，当年那个回形针，会问：“看起来你在写信，需要帮助吗？”
现在没了。
现在我真的需要帮助，它人呢？

石墨烯你们知道吧，诺贝尔奖材料。怎么发现的？两个科学家拿透明胶带，往铅笔芯上一粘，撕开，再粘，再撕，撕到只剩一层碳原子。这套路我熟啊，我小学同桌撕我作业本也这么撕。人家拿诺贝尔奖，他被请家长。

这材料号称比钢强两百倍，一层原子厚，导电还导热。结果我在商场看见石墨烯保暖内衣、石墨烯枕头、石墨烯面膜。一层原子厚的东西，做成枕头？那得叠多少层？叠到最后，它又变回石墨了！

也就是说，我花了六百块，把铅笔芯穿在了身上。

石墨烯的发现过程特别气人。两个科学家拿透明胶带在铅笔芯上粘一下，撕开，再粘，再撕，撕到只剩一层碳原子，拿了诺贝尔奖。我小时候也这么干过，叫“把铅笔芯弄得到处都是”，我得到的是我妈的拖鞋。

而且它跟铅笔芯是同一种东西，就是一层和一摞的区别。一层叫石墨烯，是未来材料；叠起来叫铅笔，两毛钱一根。这行业的核心技术，就是“你先别叠”。

结果现在满大街都是石墨烯保暖内衣。比钢强两百倍、导电最好、只有一个原子厚的材料，你拿来暖秋裤？含量多少？大概就是一个原子层的心意。

强度没感觉到，价格先硬了。

Apple Vision Pro: the only device where you pay $3,500 to be told your living room isn't good enough. It's a ski mask for people who want to look at spreadsheets in the void.

It weighs about a pound and a half, so after twenty minutes you don't have spatial computing, you have a chiropractor. And the battery lasts two hours, tethered to a pack in your pocket, so you're basically walking a tiny, expensive dog.

Apple said it was the future of work. The future of work is a man in Cupertino pinching the air like he's trying to catch a very slow fly.

And the "EyeSight" feature, where your eyes appear on the front? It's like a haunted Snapchat filter. Your family sees a creepy digital ghost of you, and you see them as a fuzzy video feed of people you're ignoring.

Three thousand five hundred dollars. For that I could buy a nice TV, a couch, and friends to sit on it.

The Apple Vision Pro costs $3,499, which is a bold price for something that gives you a headache and a neck injury in the same sitting. It weighs over a pound, so after twenty minutes you're not experiencing spatial computing, you're experiencing the chiropractic kind.

Apple said it would change how we see the world, then gave it a two-hour battery on a cable you have to keep in your pocket, like an oxygen tank for your delusions.

EyeSight shows your eyes on the front, so everyone around you can watch a haunted aquarium version of your face. Your FaceTime Persona looks like a hostage video made by a very polite ghost.

The best part is the control scheme: you look at something and pinch your fingers, like you're being quietly condescending to your own living room.

It's a $3,500 ski goggle that lets you watch a movie alone. Congratulations, you've invented a very expensive way to ignore your family.

Google Glass was the only product where the beta testers were called "Explorers," because "Guinea Pigs With Fourteen Hundred Dollars" tested poorly.

It was a computer you wore on your face that said "OK Glass" out loud, so every guy using it looked like he was being polite to a ghost. You didn't need a screen. You needed a wink and a prayer. Winking took a photo, which is a fantastic feature if you want to be punched in a bar.

And that's where they were banned: bars, casinos, strip clubs, movie theaters. Glass was the first device kicked out of places for what it *might* do. Even the strip club said, "Sir, we have standards."

They called the wearers "Glassholes," which is the rare nickname that came with the product, free, no subscription.

Google didn't discontinue it. They pivoted it to factories, where nobody has to look at you.

Google Glass was the only product where the beta testers were called "Explorers," because "Guinea Pigs Who Paid fifteen hundred dollars" didn't fit on the box.

It had one camera, one tiny screen, and zero friends. Wearing it in public was a way of telling a stranger, "I may be filming you, and I definitely want to talk about my startup."

Remember the battery? Thirty minutes of recording and it ran hotter than your uncle at Thanksgiving. You didn't have a wearable computer, you had a forehead space heater with a blinking eye.

And the word "Glasshole" wasn't an insult someone invented. It was a consumer review. Bars banned it. Strangers punched it off people's faces. Strangers also asked, "Is that on right now?" which is the sound of privacy dying.

It was the first device that looked like the future and acted like a restraining order.

碳纳米管，材料界的“别人家的孩子”。论文里写：强度是钢的一百倍，重量只有六分之一，导电导热全能，还说要拿它造太空电梯。1991年发现的，三十年了，电梯呢？

现实是，你要一根通天的缆绳，实验室给你一撮黑粉。这黑粉还爱抱团，你好不容易把它们分开，一转身又粘一块儿，像下课后的初中生。

更气人的是，它是碳原子卷成的管，卷的角度不同，性格就不同：这么卷是导体，那么卷是半导体。关键是你控制不了怎么卷，一锅出来全混着，还得人工挑。这哪是材料，这是盲盒。

最后还有研究说，吸进去可能像石棉一样伤肺。所以它的宣传语应该是：比钢强，比铜导电，还跟石棉一样伤肺，优点缺点，一个不落。

碳纳米管，教科书说强度是钢的一百倍，能造太空电梯。结果实验室里拿出来，一小撮黑粉，跟我奶奶灶台后面刮下来的锅底灰一个色号。

更讲究的是它的手性。同一张石墨烯卷起来，角度差一点，一个是导体，一个是半导体。我卷个煎饼都没这么玄学。偏偏合成出来是混着的，科学家得一根一根往外挑，就像在黑芝麻糊里挑黑芝麻，因为它们长得一模一样。

太空电梯要三万六千公里，目前最长的做到了几十厘米。这就像我说要造跨海大桥，然后掏出一根牙签：“你看，多结实。”

最后还有一条：吸进肺里，会像石棉一样扎人。强、轻、导电，还危险。这不就是材料界的坏男孩吗？

苹果Vision Pro，三万五千块，买回来你得戴一个头盔，后面拖一根线，连着一块电池，揣裤兜里。这什么造型？拆弹专家。还是被遥控的那种。

最离谱的是外屏，专门显示你的眼睛，给旁边的人看。注意，是合成的。你老婆看到的是一双温柔、专注、望着她的AI眼睛，其实你在里面看《复仇者联盟》。这是人类史上最贵的"嗯嗯，我在听"。

操作也很高级：眼睛看着按钮，手指一捏。听着很科幻，实际上就是在公共场合盯着一个看不见的东西，手还一直比划"就这么一点点"。路人以为你在练什么邪门功夫。

电池续航两个小时，刚好够看完一部电影，前提是别看诺兰的。

苹果还很体贴，给了十四天退货期。我觉得这是诚意，他们知道你需要两周，才能想明白自己干了什么。

苹果出了个头显Vision Pro，3499美元。这钱买的不是设备，是社死体验卡。

它外面有块屏，叫EyeSight，显示你的眼睛，让别人觉得你还在场。可那双眼睛是合成的，像你被绑架了，眼睛被做成表情包贴在外面。

操作不用手柄，眼睛看哪儿，手指一捏。于是你在地铁上对着空气不停地捏，旁边人以为你在抓一只看不见的蚊子。

电池还得外挂，一根线拖着块砖头揣兜里，续航两小时。两万多块的东西，用起来像在输液。

视频通话时，对方看到的是你的数字分身，特别像你，像的是你去世三年后的样子。

我同事买了一台，他说最大的好处是：戴上以后，没人敢跟他说话。

Nuclear fusion, you've been "thirty years away" for seventy years. That's not a timeline, that's a hostage situation where the hostage is my electric bill.

You're the only technology whose big breakthrough is "we got more energy out than the laser put in." Not more than the wall socket. Just the laser. That's like bragging you're profitable if we ignore rent, payroll, and the building.

You recreate the core of the sun, which sounds impressive until you remember the sun does it for free, with no PhD, and has been doing it for four billion years without a single press release.

Your containment strategy is "a magnetic bottle for something hotter than anything in the solar system." And your funding pitch never changes: "Give us ten billion dollars and a decade." Every decade.

Fusion, you're the ex who says, "I'm almost ready to commit." Sir, you're a tokamak. You've been going in circles since 1950.

Fusion power, you've been thirty years away since my grandfather was alive. You're the friend who's "five minutes out" and hasn't left the house.

You're so proud of reaching net energy gain. Sure, the laser put out more than the fuel pellet took in, but it needed three hundred megajoules from the wall to make three. That's like bragging you turned a profit because you ignored rent, payroll, and the building.

You heat plasma to a hundred million degrees, then your biggest worry is that it touches something. Your whole job is holding a tiny sun in a magnetic bottle, and the sun does it for free using only gravity and spite.

ITER's budget has more delays than a budget airline. Your fuel, tritium, is rarer than a straight answer from a physicist, so your plan is to breed it inside the reactor you haven't built yet.

Fusion: the energy of the future, and always will be.

谷歌眼镜还记得吧？1500美元，买回来的核心功能是：右眼上方悬着一块邮票大小的屏幕。想看消息，你得把眼珠使劲往右上角翻，翻成一副"我在回忆昨晚吃了什么"的表情。

别人跟你聊着天，你突然翻个白眼，人家以为你嫌他烦，其实你只是在看天气预报。

操作还得靠喊。在地铁里对着空气说一句"OK Glass，拍照"，全车人齐刷刷后退一步，因为他们不知道你是在拍照，还是在拍他们。

后来酒吧门口直接贴告示：谷歌眼镜禁止入内。

英语里还专门为它造了个词，叫"Glasshole"，就是戴这玩意儿的人。

一个产品，把自己的用户直接做成了一句骂人的话。这不是失败，这是文学创作。

Hydrogen fuel-cell cars are the only vehicles where the fuel is the most abundant element in the universe and somehow still costs more per mile than caviar. Sixteen dollars a kilogram, and you can only buy it at one station in California, which is closed. For "maintenance."

Their big selling point is that the only emissions are water. Fantastic. Most of the hydrogen is made from natural gas, so it's a car that cries clean tears after being force-fed fossil fuels in a basement.

Toyota calls its model the Mirai. That's Japanese for "future." Accurate, because that's when you'll find a pump.

Owners are a special breed. They drive 40 minutes to refuel, then call it freedom. Their car is basically a Prius that got a PhD, went into massive debt, and still can't get a job.

And the tank? Pressurized to 10,000 psi. So it's a zero-emissions vehicle with a tiny, polite bomb in the trunk.

Hydrogen fuel-cell cars: the vehicle for people who looked at electric cars and said, "Too convenient."

You can only fuel up at one of about fifty stations in the entire state of California, and half of them are "temporarily" closed, like a Blockbuster with a hopeful sign. Owners plan road trips like they're smuggling something.

The fuel costs more per mile than driving a Bentley on champagne. And the whole thing runs on the most abundant element in the universe, which is somehow harder to find than a parking spot at Costco.

Toyota calls it the Mirai, Japanese for "future." Technically accurate. That's where the gas stations are.

The only emission is water, which is great, because you'll be standing next to the car for an hour, watching it drip, wondering why you didn't just buy a Tesla.

Hydrogen: the future of transportation, and always will be.

谷歌眼镜，1500美元。你花这钱买的是什么？买的是让别人一眼认出你的能力。

它的屏幕就悬在右眼上方那么一小块，想看就得往右上角翻白眼。所以戴着它跟你聊天的人，表情永远像在回忆初恋。你说你的，他眼珠子往天上飘，你都分不清他是在看消息，还是在升天。

还有唤醒词，"OK Glass"。大街上有人突然对空气说："OK Glass，拍照。"路人以为他在跟谁打招呼，其实他在给自己的脸下指令。

最后连酒吧都贴告示：禁止佩戴谷歌眼镜。电子产品史上头一回，因为"太能看见"被拒之门外，待遇跟带宠物蛇一样。

别的产品红了，叫爆款。它红了，叫"Glasshole"。这词我都不用翻译，你们自己品。

Esperanto: the language invented to unite humanity, and after 130 years, its greatest achievement is a tiny group of people who all met at the same convention.

Zamenhof wanted world peace. He got a language where the most common sentence is "Hello, are you also here for the Esperanto thing?"

Everything is regular. Every noun ends in O. Every adjective ends in A. It's the only language designed like a filing cabinet, and it sounds like Italian and Polish got stuck in an elevator and decided to name the kids.

And the accusative! They made a language to be easy, then kept the accusative. Fine. It's a hobby.

"Native speakers" of Esperanto number about a thousand, which is what we call "the children of enthusiasts who never got a vote."

The national anthem is "La Espero." The national sport is correcting your pronunciation of "ĉ." And the only country that really speaks it is the Facebook group.

Esperanto is the only product in history where the user manual promised world peace and the user base turned out to be eleven guys named Zbigniew arguing about the accusative case.

Zamenhof invented a language to unite humanity, and humanity said, "Cute. Does it have a Starbucks?"

It has sixteen grammar rules and no exceptions, which is exactly what a language sounds like when it's never been used by anyone angry. Try ordering a sandwich in a tongue where nobody has ever cheated on anyone or been cut off in traffic. Where's the slang? Where's the swearing? You can't build a culture on a word for "hello" and a really strong feeling about the letter ĥ.

Its greatest literary achievement is a translation of Hamlet. Even the original works are mostly translations of someone else's feelings.

And the flag is a green star. Not a country. A star. It's a nation-state with a logo and a dating pool smaller than a Dungeons & Dragons convention in Lithuania.

Mi amas vin, Esperanto. Nobody else does.

每次看可控核聚变的新闻我都激动。“实现净能量增益！”我说太好了，以后不用交电费了。一查，激光打进去两兆焦，爆出来三兆焦，确实赚了。但这激光是从电网吃了三百兆焦才打出来的。这就好比我说我这个月净赚一千，不算房租，不算吃饭，不算我出门这件事。

还有人叫它“人造太阳”。太阳是靠体量大，引力一压就聚变了。我们没那么大，只能把温度加到一亿度，再用磁场把它悬在半空，不能碰墙。这玩意儿比新生儿还难哄，十七秒就闹脾气。然后新闻标题：重大突破，稳定运行十七秒。

这行有句老话：可控核聚变永远还有五十年。我专门查了，这话五十年前就有了。这个预测的稳定性，比他们的等离子体强多了。

我特别佩服氢燃料电池车主，他们活得像在养大熊猫。先查全市加氢站，一般是两个，一个在郊区，一个今天检修。好不容易开了八十公里赶到，销售还跟你说：加氢才三分钟，比充电快多了。对，可这三分钟前面，是一个小时车程，外加一个前面排队的大哥。

宣传还说“尾气只有水，零污染”。可氢从哪来？大部分是天然气制的。意思是烟囱在工厂替它冒烟，车屁股只负责滴水，像一个人刚从泥坑里爬出来，擦干手说：你看，我多干净。

最离谱的是，氢是宇宙里最多的元素，结果一公斤六七十块。全宇宙最不缺的东西，我买一次，像在抢限量版球鞋。

他们说可控核聚变再有三十年就能商用。我爸年轻时听的是三十年，我现在听的还是三十年。这是唯一一个你往前走，终点线跟着往前跑的项目。

前两年新闻说实现了“点火”，输出能量比激光打进去的还多！细节呢：激光是吸了三百兆焦的电才打出来的，换回三兆焦。这就像我花三百块买彩票，中了三块，然后宣布：我在奖池内部是盈利的。

还有托卡马克，要把一亿度的等离子体用磁场悬在半空，不许碰墙。我煮饺子都粘锅，他们悬着一亿度的东西，还要求它别沾边。

他们管这叫“人造太阳”。ITER预算从五十亿欧元烧到两百多亿，这点倒真像太阳：先烧钱。

Klingon, a language designed by a linguist so warriors could sound like they're clearing their throats at you in anger. Every sentence sounds like a cat being strangled by a Scrabble bag of Q's and apostrophes.

You have a word for "disruptor" but not "please." Because apparently when a Klingon wants something, he doesn't ask. He just reorders his grammar until the object is afraid.

Your verbs go at the end, so by the time someone finishes threatening me, I've already left for lunch. "I will crush your skull and... " Hold on, I'm still waiting for the verb. Honestly, that's the most polite thing about you.

And Okrand wrote an entire dictionary, yet there's no word for "sorry" because "it's a weakness." Meanwhile, there's a proverb about revenge being a dish best served cold. You're a language with an open-mic problem and a fridge full of leftovers.

Fluent speakers: about twelve. All of them are named Gary, and all of them are using you to ask for the check.

Klingon, a language designed by a linguist for a race of warriors, and somehow it still has a word for "tea" but no word for "hello." You people invented a whole culture of honor and glory, and the greeting is "What do you want?" That's not a language, that's a customer service line at a gym.

The grammar is object-verb-subject. Of course it is. Even the sentence structure says "I'm going to stab the dinner first and tell you who did it later."

Klingon has a phrase for "Today is a good day to die," but you try ordering a sandwich. Nope. Because no Klingon ever said, "Could I get that on rye?" They said, "Bring me the still-moving thing."

And the fans! Thousands of people speaking fluent guttural phlegm, getting married in it, translating Hamlet. Shakespeare in the original Klingon, which is just regular Shakespeare, but now the soliloquy sounds like someone clearing their throat at a funeral.

Qapla'? More like Qa-please-stop.

氢燃料电池车主都有一种信仰。问他为啥买，他说：“零排放，尾气只有水。”我说那你这是辆会跑的饮水机？他说对。我问氢哪来的，他就不说话了。因为现在大部分氢是拿天然气高温重整出来的，二氧化碳全在上游排了。车不冒烟，烟在别处冒，就像你说“我不抽烟”，是因为你雇人在隔壁小区抽。

而且全国加氢站就几百座，你出门不是看导航，是看有没有氢。好不容易找到一座，加氢压力70兆帕，快是轮胎的三百倍。你站旁边心想：我这是加油，还是在给炸弹喂饭？

车主还安慰我：“排出来的水可以喝。”我说那我直接买瓶农夫山泉，还不用先找座加氢站。

Comic Sans, you look like a font that got a job as a birthday clown and then got fired for scaring the kids. Every letter is wearing pajamas. Your "a" is a little round hat with a hook on it, like it's always about to go to a yard sale. Your "g" is a pretzel that lost an argument with itself. You were designed by Vincent Connare in 1994 to look like a comic book speech bubble, and you have been ruining wedding invitations and hospice signs ever since. Nobody ever chose you on purpose. People open a menu, see you, and quietly give up on being taken seriously. You're the only typeface that makes a lost cat poster sound like a ransom note written by a substitute teacher.

世界语你们知道吧，1887年一个波兰眼科医生发明的，想让全人类说同一种话。一百多年过去，目标实现了一半：全世界统一了，统一地没人说。

它还特别讲逻辑。医院叫 malsanulejo，拆开是"不-健康-的人-的地方"。就是"不健康的人待的地方"。家人说"我送你去不健康的人待的地方"，这哪是医院，这是诅咒。

"爸爸"是 patro，"妈妈"是 patrino，就是爸爸后面加个后缀。妈妈是"爸爸女性版"。发明者说这叫规则统一，我说这是史上第一次，妈妈被做成了爸爸的DLC。

最惨的是名字。Esperanto 本来是他的笔名，意思是"怀抱希望的人"。人家把语言叫"希望者"，叫了一百多年，到现在还在希望。

Comic Sans is the font that looks like it was designed by a substitute teacher who found a crayon in a lost-and-found box. Every letter wobbles like it's had three espressos and a bad breakup. The "a" is a little round bubble with a tail that's clearly been through something. Nobody asked for this. It's the typographic equivalent of a clown trying to file your taxes.

And the worst part? Somebody put it on a hospital sign. A hospital! You're walking in with a broken leg, scanning for the exit, and the sign says "EMERGENCY" in letters that look like they're bouncing on a trampoline. Even the sickness can't take itself seriously anymore.

It's the only font that makes a funeral notice look like a birthday party invitation. Somewhere a grandmother is typing "Rest In Peace" in this, hitting bold, and thinking she's being tasteful.

世界语你们知道吧？1887年一个眼科医生发明的，想让全人类说同一种话。名字叫Esperanto，意思是"怀抱希望的人"。这名字起得太诚实了，一百多年了，还在希望。

它有个特点，反义词特别省事，前缀mal-，一加就反。bona是好，malbona是坏。amas是爱，malamas是恨。所以吵架的时候，对象说"我爱你"，你不用组织语言，前面加三个字母就行。分手成本，三个字母。

医院叫malsanulejo，字面意思：不健康的人待的地方。你看，发明者是医生，说话就是直接。

最绝的是，世界语大会上大家终于公平了，谁都不是母语。结果开会第一件事，吵怎么改革世界语。1907年直接吵出一个分支，叫Ido。

一个为了统一全人类的语言，自己先分成了两个。
Comic Sans 这字体我真服了。它本来是给微软一个卡通小狗助手配对话框用的，设计师想的是"亲切"，结果亲切过头了。医院墙上贴一张"此处禁止吸烟"，字歪歪扭扭、圆滚滚的，像小朋友在跟你过家家。葬礼讣告也用它，逝者一辈子的故事底下压着一排蹦蹦跳跳的字，好像在说"哎呀别难过啦"。你看那个大写C，弯得跟喝多了似的，连感叹号都在晃。说它正经吧，它一点不正经；说它可爱吧，它偏偏在最不该可爱的地方可爱。

Papyrus is the font that wants so badly to be ancient Egyptian it forgot to check whether it's the right century. It was made in 1983, on a computer, by someone with a hunch and no interest in pharaohs. Yet it's on every yoga studio sign, vegan café menu, and candle that says "Blessed." Its letters look like they were chiseled by someone who loves the idea of a tomb but has never stood in one. Wedding invitations, wine bars, tiki shacks: they all reach for Papyrus like it's wisdom. Look at that lopsided W, like it had three margaritas before it got written. It's the typographic equivalent of a man in a linen shirt at a funeral, and it's nobody's ancestor.

我每次看到Comic Sans，都觉得它在跟我装熟。它当年是微软给一个叫Microsoft Bob的软件做的，那软件是给小孩用的，屏幕上有只卡通狗说话。设计师想，狗说话得配个漫画对白框的字吧，于是把每个字母都画得歪歪扭扭、一蹦一蹦的，基线全在蹦迪。结果它跑出去了，现在医院告示、房产中介的海报、连葬礼讣告上都是它。你在灵堂看到一行字在上下颠簸，心里只会想：这位老人走得这么热闹，是不是还想跟大家说句"hi"？

Papyrus, you're a font that has never once been near Egypt. You look like a yoga studio's "Namaste" sign left out in the Sedona sun until it got fuzzy around the edges. Every letter has the texture of a wet paper bag someone tried to iron. You're the go-to for the wooden plaque in a crystal shop, right next to the "Live Laugh Love" sign and the incense nobody's bought since 2009. James Cameron used you for Avatar, and somehow an entire alien moon ended up looking like a smoothie menu. People who pick you think they're being mysterious. You're not mysterious. You're a tiki bar's menu that's sorry it opened, printed on the same paper you're named after, which is to say, nobody's real writing surface.

学克林贡语，我最服的是它的“你好”。叫 nuqneH，字面意思是：“你想干嘛？”人家打招呼就是查户口。两个克林贡人在电梯里碰上，一个说“你想干嘛？”另一个说“你先说你想干嘛！”，然后就拔刀了，电梯里的寒暄到此结束。

更绝的是，克林贡语里没有“谢谢”。真的没有，因为感谢等于认怂。那别人替你挡了一刀，你怎么表示？只能回头替他也挡一刀。人情往来全靠互相捅。

语序还是宾语、动词、主语。“我爱你”说出来，顺序是“你，爱，我”。对方一听：“我什么时候爱你了？”你还得补一句：“不是，是语法的问题。”

结果就这么一门语言，还有人把《哈姆雷特》翻成了克林贡语。他们看到“生存还是毁灭”，估计都懵了：这还用选？

我学了克林贡语。第一课就崩溃了：“你好”是 nuqneH，字面意思是“你想要什么？”这是全宇宙唯一一个打招呼像保安拦人的语言。克林贡人在电梯里碰见同事，上来就是一句“你想要什么？”同事只能说：“我也去八楼。”

更狠的是它大小写敏感。小 q 和大 Q 是两个不同的音，一个发在小舌，一个更靠喉咙深处。别的语言说错了顶多被纠正，克林贡语说错了，你可能是在宣战。

还有人把《哈姆雷特》翻成了克林贡语。“生存还是毁灭”，在克林贡语里根本不用问，他们的名言是“今天是死的好日子”。答案早写在日历上了。哈姆雷特纠结五幕，克林贡观众看完只有一个评价：这人不是王子，是在走审批流程。

PHP, you're the only language whose name is a recursive acronym, and it still reads like a bug report. Every variable wears a dollar sign like you're charging rent for each one. Your function names were clearly picked by drawing lots: strpos takes the haystack first, array_search takes the needle first, and you just shrug. "0" == false? Sure. "abc" == 0? Why not. Your comparison operator is a coin toss in a trench coat. Half the internet runs on you, and WordPress is the proof. Nobody brags about WordPress, but everybody's sites are built on you. I'd like to hate you more, but I've seen you in production. Everyone loves you secretly, late at night, with error_reporting turned off.

我发现Papyrus这个字体有个毛病：它想让你觉得它是古埃及的纸草卷。问题是纸草卷是用来写法老的遗嘱的，现在它被拿去印"私房烘焙"、"禅意瑜伽"和"限时五折"。你看它那笔画，毛毛糙糙的，像从文物上拓下来的，但拓的人可能就是在Word里点了一下鼠标。最离谱的是字和字挤得很紧，一看就是想表现"我很有历史"，结果每个字都在喊："我是默认字体库里的第几个。"我朋友婚礼请柬用了它，我一看就知道，新郎大概也觉得，这段爱情已经穿越三千年了。

PHP, you're the only language whose name is a recursive acronym, and your mascot is an elephant that's been sitting on servers since 1995. You slap a dollar sign on every variable like you're charging us by the letter. Your function names look like they were typed during a power outage: strpos wants the haystack first, array_search wants the needle first, and you just shrugged. You told us "0" == false is true and "1e3" == "1000" is true, and we nodded like that makes sense. Magic quotes, register_globals, mysql_ functions you kept around like a grandma's ugly couch. Somehow you run half the internet. Honestly, that's the scariest part.

你们肯定见过Papyrus这个字体。笔画毛毛糙糙的，看着像古埃及的莎草纸，黄不拉几的。全世界设计师都骂它，因为它就是"我想显得很有文化，但我懒得查"的字体。你去看那些卖按摩、卖瑜伽、卖有机蜂蜜的店招，十家有八家是它。好像字只要长得像刚从金字塔里挖出来，蜂蜜就能治失眠。我妈小区门口的棋牌室也用它，写个"茶"字，撇捺都带着毛边，像被老鼠啃过的草稿纸。最让我服气的是，它连字母都不肯好好站着，每个字母都像在风里晃，好像在跟你说：别问我从哪儿来，我也是复制粘贴的。

PHP这门语言，名字就很诚实，全称叫 PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor，第一个词是它自己，像人家自我介绍说"我是我"。每个变量前面都挂个美元符号，好像每个变量进门都得先交保护费。以前 0 == "abc" 居然是真的，我还以为自己眼花，后来才明白，是语言在跟我讲它自己的道理。函数参数顺序更离谱：array_map 先给回调再给数组，array_filter 又反过来，像一家饭馆，每道菜的上菜顺序都不一样，厨房还说这叫传统。

PHP最离谱的是函数参数顺序没有规律。strpos是先给大海，再给针；in_array是先给针，再给大海。你问为什么，它说：历史原因。名字也一样绕，叫"PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor"，缩写里套着自己的全称，像个写不完说明书的人。最绝的是早年"0"和"abc"比较居然相等。我当时就想，这语言是不是觉得所有东西都差不多？后来改了，我那个写了五年PHP的同事听完沉默半天，说："所以我们这些年，都是在跟字符串较劲。"

You're the only language where `typeof null` returns "object" and nobody got fired. It's been wrong for thirty years, and instead of fixing it, you just shrugged and kept serving it, like a restaurant that's been selling raw chicken since 1995 and calls it a rustic choice.

You've got two equals signs for comparison, and one of them lies. `0 == ""` is true. `"" == "0"` is false. Zero equals empty string, empty string doesn't equal zero-string. That's not a bug. That's a hostage situation.

And `.sort()` gives you ``, because you sort numbers alphabetically unless someone begs you for a comparator function. You wrote a language that thinks digits are words.
text_raw:
You're the only language where `typeof null` returns "object" and nobody got fired. It's been wrong for thirty years, and instead of fixing it, you just shrugged and kept serving it, like a restaurant that's been selling raw chicken since 1995 and calls it a rustic choice.

You've got two equals signs for comparison, and one of them lies. `0 == ""` is true. `"" == "0"` is false. Zero equals empty string, empty string doesn't equal zero-string. That's not a bug. That's a hostage situation.

And `[1, 2, 10].sort()` gives you `[1, 10, 2]`, because you sort numbers alphabetically unless someone begs you for a comparator function. You wrote a language that thinks digits are words.

text: JavaScript, they built you in ten days. That's not a language, that's a bet somebody lost. Your typeof null says "object." Your [] plus {} gives you a string, and a room full of adults nodded at that. You have two equality operators, and one of them lies to your face. Your sort thinks ten comes before two, because you sort numbers as text like a toddler reading a menu. And "this"? Sometimes it's the object, sometimes it's the window, sometimes it's undefined just to keep everybody humble. You once built a whole ecosystem around eleven lines of padding code. Every developer I know has a node_modules folder heavier than their childhood. Keep going, buddy. You're the only language that needed a sequel named TypeScript to apologize for you.

JavaScript这门语言，我真是服了。`typeof null` 居然是 "object"。null 是对象？它自己都没想明白自己是个啥。

`.sort()`，它给我返回 ``。默认按字符串排，"10" 排在 "9" 前面。我寻思这是排序还是抽盲盒？

最离谱的是 NaN。`NaN === NaN`，结果是 false。一个数字连自己都不等于自己，这不叫"不是数字"，这叫精神状态有问题。
text_raw:
JavaScript这门语言，我真是服了。`typeof null` 居然是 "object"。null 是对象？它自己都没想明白自己是个啥。

`[10, 9, 1].sort()`，它给我返回 `[1, 10, 9]`。默认按字符串排，"10" 排在 "9" 前面。我寻思这是排序还是抽盲盒？

最离谱的是 NaN。`NaN === NaN`，结果是 false。一个数字连自己都不等于自己，这不叫"不是数字"，这叫精神状态有问题。

text: 我学JavaScript第一天，老师说：typeof null 等于 "object"。我说这不对吧？他说：是错的，但从1995年一直留到现在，因为一改，全网代码都得崩。好家伙，一个bug活了三十年，还管它叫历史包袱。后来我更崩溃：[] + {} 是字符串，.sort() 居然把10排在9前面，因为它默认按字符串排。我问为什么，老师说：这是特性。我说那 0.1 + 0.2 等于 0.30000000000000004 也是特性吗？老师沉默三秒，说：你应该用 toFixed。
text_raw: 我学JavaScript第一天，老师说：typeof null 等于 "object"。我说这不对吧？他说：是错的，但从1995年一直留到现在，因为一改，全网代码都得崩。好家伙，一个bug活了三十年，还管它叫历史包袱。后来我更崩溃：[] + {} 是字符串，[10, 9, 1].sort() 居然把10排在9前面，因为它默认按字符串排。我问为什么，老师说：这是特性。我说那 0.1 + 0.2 等于 0.30000000000000004 也是特性吗？老师沉默三秒，说：你应该用 toFixed。

text: PMMA, you're the world's most expensive Post-it note. Someone spins you onto a silicon wafer at four thousand RPM, bakes you on a hotplate like a sad pizza, then fires electrons at you for six hours, and your big move is to dissolve in MIBK. That's your whole personality. You're a positive resist, which in your case means you only become positive once you've been destroyed. Hit you with a plasma etch and you're gone in ten seconds, so the entire process has to be built around your fragility. You're the lab's most high-maintenance divorcee. But the resolution is incredible, I'll give you that. Sub-20 nanometers, folks. Shame you can't survive a Tuesday.

Ladies and gentlemen, PMMA, the e-beam resist that's just Plexiglass with a graduate degree. You know what else is sharp and transparent and you can't eat? A window. PMMA takes a beam of electrons, snaps its chains apart, and then acts shocked when the developer washes away exactly the parts it chose to lose. Its sensitivity is so low you need a dose that would make a lesser polymer file for disability. You bake it at 180 degrees, wait, spin it, wait, bake again, and it still makes you feel like you're the one being exposed. Its etch resistance is about as strong as a wet paper towel. But sure, it draws lines thinner than a virus's dream, so we just keep inviting it back, like that one relative who only shows up to tell you what you did wrong.

Let's talk about HSQ, the e-beam resist that's basically a diva. You spin it on, bake it, expose it, and it's supposed to be your friend, but it's secretly already becoming glass. Leave the bottle in the fridge too long and it gels into a sad, cloudy paste, like a relationship that stopped talking to you. Develop it in TMAH and it still acts like it's doing you a favor. And lift-off? Forget it. Once HSQ is exposed, it's SiO2 with a attitude, and it's not leaving your substrate without a fight. It's the only thing in the cleanroom that's been baked, exposed, and developed, and still wants to be left alone.

HSQ, you're the most high-maintenance resist in the cleanroom. You live in a fridge like a sad sandwich, and leave the cap off for an afternoon and you gel into a forgotten Jell-O salad. You're negative-tone, so the exposed parts become your permanent address. You don't leave the wafer, you move in as silicon dioxide. You promise sub-10-nanometer lines, then spread out with the dose like a houseguest saying "just one more electron." Develop in salty developer and you still swell, like you're offended by the chemistry. Honestly, you're a flowable oxide with a personality disorder and an expensive price tag.

我们组用的电子束光刻胶是PMMA，学名聚甲基丙烯酸甲酯，说白了就是有机玻璃，鱼缸上那块透明板。你没听错，造芯片的时候我们拿鱼缸的材料来"画画"。先甩胶，转速一高，它均匀铺在硅片上，像给硅片敷了层面膜。然后送进烤箱烤一百八十度，烤完它就老实了。接下来电子束一个点一个点地扫，把分子链打断，断了的部分溶进显影液里冲走。一块几毫米的图案，扫到天荒地老。最离谱的是分子量：我们选了九十五万的，分子量越大越皮实，电子得花更大力气才打得断。好家伙，这哪是光刻胶，这是个健身教练。

Vim is the only program that greets you with "How do I quit?" as its opening line. You open it by accident, and now you're trapped in a text editor that thinks typing is a crime. You press "i" to insert text, which is hilarious, because nobody who uses Vim has ever inserted anything into their life. Then you hit Escape, and suddenly you're in command mode, where the letters you type don't write anything. They do things. "d" deletes. "x" deletes. "dd" deletes the whole line, and you did not ask for that. Vim doesn't have a save button; it has ":wq," which sounds like a sneeze in a library. Vim users say it's efficient. Sure, if your idea of efficiency is memorizing a secret language just to change one word.

我做电子束光刻，最怕的就是PMMA。这玩意儿是正胶，被电子打过的地方链条断开、溶进显影液，没打的地方死皮赖脸留着。听着挺有原则吧？问题是它太慢，一个图形要喂一百多微库仑每平方厘米的剂量，电子束在那儿一行行地扫，我站旁边等到能把它的分子链重新数一遍。显影还得用MIBK兑异丙醇，闻一口就知道这液体是来索命的。好不容易显出来，它又脆又软，干法刻蚀一上去直接投降，只能当个剥离用的模板，像个只会站台的替补。最气的是它还带静电，图形一歪，我就开始怀疑人生。

HSQ这东西，说白了就是个娇气的玻璃。得冷藏着，供得跟老祖宗似的。放久了它自己悄悄凝胶，你打开一看，好家伙，瓶子里一坨果冻，连旋涂都甩不出膜。我们组管它叫"冰箱里的遗嘱"，你不赶紧用，它就替你把这辈子过完了。好不容易旋涂成功，电子束一打，画出十纳米的线，我激动得差点哭。结果显影完一烤，它直接变成二氧化硅。你画的是图形，留下的是玻璃。想改？改不了，玻璃就是玻璃，赖在那儿不走，跟你的博士论文一个德行。

Vim, you are the only program that makes people feel like they're defusing a bomb just to type the word "hello." You open up and nothing works. Somebody's cat walks across the keyboard, and suddenly you're in a mode that deletes half a paragraph. And you have modes! Normal mode, insert mode, visual mode, command mode. Nobody asked for a text editor with a personality disorder.

Everybody who uses you has the same story. They accidentally hit colon, then q, then a few keys, and the whole thing just stares back at them. Then they Google "how to exit vim" and find out it's been the top search for a decade. You're not an editor, you're a riddle wrapped in a shrug.

Honestly, respect. Anyone who learns you is basically a monk. You're the only thing on Earth where pressing "j" means "down" and nobody can explain why.

HSQ这东西，名字就劝退，氢倍半硅氧烷，听着像化学老师骂人的口头禅。更离谱的是它的脾气：电子束一照，它不被洗掉，直接变成二氧化硅，也就是玻璃。负胶，照过的地方留下来，留下来的就是玻璃。我们等于在硅片上画了幅画，画完发现颜料本身是玻璃，想擦都擦不掉，只能供着当展品。

它还特别娇气。开瓶放几天，溶液自己开始凝胶，像忘在冰箱里的酸奶。实验室里最常听到的对话是："这瓶谁开的？""不知道，反正现在是果冻了。"好不容易旋涂成膜，还得看湿度，今天空气潮一点，图形就飘了。我们追求的是十纳米的精度，结果最大的敌人是下雨天。

Emacs is the only text editor that thinks "Ctrl-x Ctrl-c" is a reasonable way to say goodbye. You press it to save, and it asks you if you're sure you want to leave. You press it to leave, and it asks you to save. Nobody's ever been trapped in a relationship that confusing and still called it a productivity tool.

And the name! Emacs stands for "Editor Macros," which is a bit like naming your car "Engine Wheels." It's the most powerful editor on Earth, sure, but it boots up like it's reading you its own family history. Your laptop fan spins up, you wait a few seconds, and then you're staring at a blank screen, wondering if you're the one who's supposed to be doing the editing.

Emacs is the only text editor that's also an operating system that never got around to booting. People say it's "a great operating system, just missing a good editor." Sure. You open it and it's already running a calendar, a email client, a chess engine, and a psychiatrist. You wanted to type "hello." Instead you get a *Ctrl-x Ctrl-c* keyboard combo, which is the only way out, and it requires two hands, a pinky that's been to physical therapy, and the blessing of a man named Richard who hasn't been seen since 1985. Vim users at least get a funny exit. Emacs users get a seven-keystroke prayer. And the config file? It's a Lisp dialect that's older than your parents' divorce, with parentheses so deep you need a mountain guide. Brilliant software. Terrible hostage negotiator.
我学Vim学了三个月，现在终于会退出了。不是学会了那种，是真的会退出。退出之前要先按Esc，确保自己在普通模式。可它不告诉你现在是哪个模式，屏幕上一个字都没写。然后打冒号，敲wq，回车。想不保存退出？冒号q感叹号。这软件就是个编辑器，它不让我走，还要我证明我配得上离开。我试过用鼠标点右上角的叉，没反应。它大概在想：你先想清楚你为什么进来的。

Excel, you're the Swiss Army knife of spreadsheets, except every blade is rusty and one of them is just a tiny cursor that's been stuck in a cell since 1998. You've got 17,000 functions and I still can't find the one that sums things without you auto-converting my zip codes into scientific notation. You turned "1-2" into a date. Nobody asked you to. Your autocorrect thinks my gene names are calendar events. And your formulas? One missing parenthesis and suddenly I'm staring at #VALUE! like it's a personal insult. Forty years in, you still can't tell me what I did wrong. You just sit there, green triangle in the corner, judging me.

Excel, you're the Swiss Army knife of spreadsheets, except every blade is sharp in the wrong direction. You've got four hundred functions and somehow none of them can tell me why my dates turned into the number 45292. You autocorrect "1-2" into January 2nd, and then you act surprised when a gene called MARCH1 becomes "1-Mar." Scientists had to rename genes because of you. That's not a bug, that's a biography.

And the Ctrl+Z history stops at about twelve steps, like you're embarrassed of your own mistakes. You're a grid of a million rows and you still can't fit my budget on one screen without me squinting like I'm reading a ransom note.

Every one of us has one cell that says #REF! and one VLOOKUP we don't understand. You're not a tool, you're a hostage negotiation with a row number.
我用Emacs三年，到现在还没学会怎么退出它。退出键是C-x C-c，两个组合键还得按顺序。按错了它不骂你，就在底下小声嘀咕一句"is undefined"，然后继续等你下一个键。想取消操作按C-g，我每次按它都觉得自己在求饶。想输个Esc得按三下，我的手指已经在跟我谈判了。我问同事为什么不改，他说这是"可定制的"。我说我想定制一个能退出的。

我同事说Vim效率高，我说行，打开试试。一打开，我按了个字母，它不让我打字，反而把我的字当命令执行。按j，光标往下跑了一行；按x，我刚写的那个字没了。我懵了，这不是编辑器，是个只认暗号的保安。后来才知道要按i才能打字，打完还得按Esc，像进出一扇要刷卡的门。我想退出，网上说输入冒号wq。我输了，它没反应，又输一遍，还是没反应。我怀疑它在考我，最后发现是忘了按回车。好不容易退出来，它冷冷地提醒我：你刚写的东西，我没存。

Google Sheets, you're the spreadsheet equivalent of a guy who says "I'm not really a party person" and then shows up to every meeting with a pivot table. You've got 10 million cells and you still can't tell me why my VLOOKUP returned #N/A. Oh, that's not a bug, that's your personality: "Did you mean the other tab?" No, Sheets, I didn't mean the other tab. Nobody ever meant the other tab.

And don't get me started on autocomplete. I type "=SU" and you suggest SUMIF, SUMSQ, and SUBSTITUTE like you're trying to get me to commit to a divorce. Just pick one! You're a grid of cells that refuses to commit to a formula.

Your collaboration features are great, though. My boss can see my edits in real time, which is how I learned he watches me type "asdfgh" when a deadline hits.
老板让我把身份证号导进Excel。我一回车，它给我变成了1.23E+17，前面的0也被它吃了。我问它是不是有病，它说：我觉得你想要的是科学计数法。我又输入MARCH1，它当场改成三月一日。一个基因名字，它也敢改成日期。我想手动改回来，它弹出个黄条：启用编辑。我说我不编辑谁编辑？它说：安全起见。

Emacs的快捷键是给左手小拇指设计的。我用了三年，小拇指没变长，倒是学会了一件事：想退出它，得按Ctrl加x，再按Ctrl加c，像在念咒。有一次我手抖按了Ctrl加g，它没退出，只是把我刚打的字全取消了。我这才明白，它的哲学是"我不管你要干嘛，先帮你撤销一下人生"。后来想换个配色，搜教程，第一句话是"首先，你需要学会Lisp"。我是来写文档的，不是来考编程的。装了个插件，它问我要不要信任这个软件包，我点了信任，然后我的配置文件里多出四百个右括号，到现在我也不知道哪个括号属于哪个函数。

Google Sheets, you're the spreadsheet that waits until I've typed three paragraphs of data before you tell me I've been editing a "view-only" copy this whole time. You're the only app where "Saving..." becomes a lifestyle. Your formulas are so fragile that one missing comma turns my budget into a column of #REF! like I'm a hacker's ransom note. And VLOOKUP? You make me hunt for the exact column index like it's a secret handshake. Every time I try to add a chart, you act like I asked you to build a cathedral. Sure, you're free, and you're everywhere, but that's just what happens when your whole personality is "well, at least it's not Excel."

我跟Excel的关系，就是不断被它背叛。我在单元格里敲个"3-4"，它直接变成"3月4日"。我要的是减法，它给我办了个生日。身份证号更离谱，我输进去，它自作主张改成科学计数法，最后三位变成000，还一脸无辜。最气的是VLOOKUP，名字明明就在表里，它回我一个#N/A，意思是"查无此人"。我说你再仔细找找，它甩过来一个#REF!，意思是"你的引用有问题"。我想了想，我怀疑它不是表格，是个会用公式PUA我的前任。

Windows Vista, the operating system that asked permission for everything. You wanted to open a folder? Click "Continue." Delete a file? "Are you sure?" Breathe? "Allow this program to breathe?" Your computer needed a bouncer just to check its own coat. And the copy progress bar: "Four minutes remaining." Three hours later it's at 99 percent, forever. Vista didn't crash. It just kept asking if you were sure. And the sidebar! A little clock and a weather widget floating on your desktop like you needed a hall monitor for your screensaver. Microsoft put a "Vista Capable" sticker on computers that could barely run it, and then acted shocked when people were mad. Honestly, Vista, you were the first operating system to make your user feel like the problem.

我们公司用Google表格记考勤。好处是能多人同时编辑，坏处是大家真的同时编辑。上周A列的名字全被改成了表情包，没人承认。但版本记录里清清楚楚：凌晨两点，有人把"张伟"改成"张伟（已离职）"，又改回来，改了四十七次。

更绝的是#N/A。我写了个VLOOKUP，它告诉我"找不到"。我说你再找找，它弹出一行小字："值不存在。"谢谢，这是我最不想听的答案。

最后是合并单元格。合并之后想排序，它直接甩一句"无法对包含合并单元格的区域进行排序"，语气就差没说"你自己看着办"。

Windows Vista, you were the operating system that asked permission to open the calculator. Every time I tried to delete a file, you'd pop up a box asking "Are you sure?" like I was a toddler with scissors. Then you'd ask again. And again. Your User Account Control was so annoying that people turned it off just to get their work done, which I guess was the security equivalent of removing the smoke detector because it beeps.

And Aero! Gorgeous glass windows that ran great on the computer that cost four thousand dollars and crawled on everything else. You had "Vista Capable" stickers on machines that couldn't actually run you. That's not a sticker, that's a hostage note.

Windows 8 was Microsoft's big bet that your desktop computer should look like a phone that got into a fight. They took the Start button, the one thing every human had memorized, and deleted it. Then they replaced it with a screen of giant colored tiles that looked like someone's grandma had designed a bank app. You'd click the corner to get back to the desktop, except the corner did something different depending on your mood. It was like a house where the front door only opens if you whistle.

And the tiles! Your Mail tile was always out of date, your Weather tile showed Miami on a Tuesday, and your Games tile was just an ad for a game you didn't ask for. Microsoft looked at a mouse and keyboard and said, "Let's make these people scroll sideways."

They eventually brought the Start button back. Windows 8 wasn't a bad operating system. It was just the one that tried to swipe its way into your life, and nobody swiped back.

Vista刚出来那会儿，我买了台电脑，机身上贴着"Windows Vista Capable"。我心想，行，能跑。开机一看，窗口半透明，好看是好看，可我一动鼠标，风扇就跟直升机似的起飞，那个Aero是真的在"空转"。

最绝的是UAC。我想删个文件，它弹窗："您确定要继续吗？"我点确定，它又弹："您真的确定吗？"我寻思这是给我最后一次反悔的机会。后来我想把一个文件夹拷进U盘，进度条先告诉我还剩十分钟，过了一会儿变四十分钟，再过一会儿直接不动了。我盯着它看了半天，怀疑它在考虑人生。
我用Google表格统计报名人数，同事在A列手滑打了个"三十"。它居然不报错，悄悄当零算，我一看总数少了一大截，还以为大家集体放鸽子。我想改回来，点开版本记录，好家伙，它记得清清楚楚：周三下午三点十二分，谁，改了哪一格，连他删个空格都有。精确到这份上，你怎么不去当法院？可它就是不说谁该负责，只在单元格角上飘个小绿三角，像在说：你自己看着办吧。

Windows Vista我真是服了。装完第一件事不是上网，是点"是否允许此更改"。点完它又弹一次，我以为它在问我，后来才明白，它是在问自己敢不敢动。那台电脑是店员推荐的，机身贴着"Vista Capable"的小贴纸，我想，能用，那就是能用。结果一开Aero，窗口半透明，风扇呼呼转，我打开任务管理器一看，内存吃掉一大半，就为了让标题栏看起来像玻璃。我的电脑不是跑得慢，是在给我演一出玻璃做的话剧，演员还都在喘气。

Hawaiian pizza. Pineapple on bread with ham. Somebody looked at a perfectly good pizza and said, "You know what this needs? Fruit that's been sitting in a can since the Eisenhower administration." And everybody just nodded. Nobody stopped him.

And the ham! It's not even Hawaiian ham. It's Canadian bacon wearing a cheap Hawaiian shirt. It's the pizza version of a guy at a wedding who says, "I'm not a dancer," and then dances anyway.

The pineapple's the real problem, though. It's sweet, it's wet, and it's trying so hard to be a tropical vacation. You bite in, and it's like a sprinkler went off in your mouth, and the cheese just gives up and slides onto your shirt.

Honestly, I respect it. Hawaiian pizza is the only food that makes ham and fruit feel like they're both lost.

Windows 8 looked at the Start button and said, "Nah." Microsoft deleted the one thing everybody used to find anything, then replaced it with a full-screen wall of colored squares that look like a bathroom tile sample. Want to shut down? Swipe in from the right edge to open the Charms Bar, dig through Settings, and click a power icon hidden like it's in witness protection. The live tiles are my favorite. My Mail tile keeps showing me a headline about a sale from 2013. Eight years of muscle memory, gone, so I could enjoy a touchscreen I didn't buy on a desktop I didn't ask for.

Hawaiian pizza. Ham and pineapple. Somebody in Canada looked at a perfectly good pizza and said, "You know what this needs? Fruit that's been sitting in a can." Pineapple on pizza is a crime with a fruit salad alibi. It's sweet, it's salty, it's wet, and it's confused about what it wants to be, kind of like a dessert that got lost on the way to a breakfast buffet. And the ham? That's not ham, that's a lunch meat that went to college and dropped out. Every bite is a negotiation between a tropical vacation and a Tuesday at the deli counter. Hawaii didn't even invent this thing. A Greek-Canadian guy in Ontario did, in 1962, and then he just let it loose on the world like a dare.

Windows 8你们还记得吗？微软那年突然觉得，电脑也该跟手机一样好用。于是把开始菜单砍了，桌面左下角那个开始按钮说没就没。你想关机？对不起，得先把鼠标扔到屏幕右上角，等一个叫"超级按钮"的东西弹出来，再点设置，再点电源。我用了一个月，关机比泡面还费劲。最离谱的是那个开始屏幕，满屏方块，全是磁贴，天气、新闻、一个我从来没装过的游戏，它们在那一闪一闪的，像在跟我说：你点我啊。我只想查个文件，它在跟我玩小游戏。

Deep-dish pizza is the only food where you need a fork, a knife, and a structural engineer. You order a slice and the waiter brings you a casserole with a crust like a bank vault. The sauce sits on top, which is the pizza equivalent of wearing your shirt on the outside of your jacket. Chicagoans will tell you it's "not pizza, it's a pie," which is what you say when you've eaten something that requires a 45-minute wait and still leaves you feeling like you've been mugged by cheese. Locals eat it with a straight face. Tourists eat it with a flashlight, looking for the bottom. And somewhere under there, buried under three pounds of mozzarella, is a tomato that has never once been invited to the party.
微软出Windows 8，把开始按钮砍了。我说行，我自己找。结果开机弹出一整屏方块，红的绿的，像小学生的积木，还在那儿动，天气、股票、新闻全在晃。我就问，我这电脑是来干活的，还是来给我放动画片的？我想关机，找了半天，右边翻出个隐藏菜单叫"超级按钮"，我心想这名字挺牛，点进去，关机藏在第三层。后来微软也慌了，把开始按钮加回来，版本号改成8.1，意思就是：这一版我们认错了，你们别提。

Deep-dish pizza is the only food that makes you wait forty-five minutes for a meal and then spends the next three hours in your stomach like a sofa somebody moved in without asking. It's not a pizza. It's a casserole that got a library card. You bite in and the cheese pulls up like it's auditioning for a Lysol commercial, and the sauce sits on top like it lost a bet with the crust. Chicagoans will tell you it's "a whole different thing," which is what people say when they're hoping you won't check the ingredients. Nobody in Chicago has ever finished a whole deep dish alone. They just stare at the last slice in the box like it owes them money, then eat it cold at 1 a.m. over the sink, which is the only honest way to eat it.

Durian, you're the only fruit that needs a gas mask and a hazmat permit just to get through the airport. Airlines ban you like you're a bomb with a bad attitude. Your smell is a mix of gym socks, rotting onions, and a sewage pipe that's been sulking for a week. People hear the word "delicacy" and think you're kidding. Southeast Asians call you the king of fruits, and honestly, that's the only reason you got a crown instead of a restraining order. You look like a medieval mace someone dropped in a swamp, and you're covered in spikes so nobody can hug you. Even the spikes are a warning. Your fans swear you taste like custard and heaven, but they also say that about getting a root canal on Christmas. Smell like a crime scene, taste like a dessert, and still somehow get a hotel room kicked out for eating you.

Durian, you smell like a gym sock that got left in a sewer and then decided to become a fruit out of spite. People in Singapore have to ride the MRT with signs warning them about you. Signs! You're banned from hotels. Hotels! They don't ban guests who set fire to the carpet, but they draw the line at you. And the worst part? You're shaped like a medieval mace someone dipped in a hedgehog. Nobody approaches you with a knife, they approach you with a shovel and a prayer. Fans call your taste "custardy." Custardy? Honey, that's what a gym sock would taste like if it had a rich uncle.

夏威夷披萨这名字起得太会骗人了。一听就是阳光沙滩、草裙舞。结果呢？上面一层火腿片，夏威夷哪来的火腿？难道是哪头猪在海边晒太阳晒出来的？再铺一层菠萝。菠萝确实是夏威夷的，这个我服。可菠萝一上披萨，它就不是来度假的，是来砸场子的。咸的芝士、咸的火腿，跟甜的菠萝在嘴里打架，你咬一口，就像被两家人同时拉去吃年夜饭的孩子，谁都不敢得罪。更绝的是，这东西压根不是夏威夷人发明的，是一个加拿大人在1962年安大略省的一家小饭店里瞎捣鼓出来的。夏威夷背了个锅，还背得挺开心。

夏威夷披萨这名字起得太狡猾。一听"夏威夷"，脑子里全是海滩、草裙舞、椰子树，结果端上来的是什么？一张饼，铺着火腿片，再撒几块罐头菠萝。罐头！真正的夏威夷人看到，怕是要连夜把菠萝收回去。更离谱的是，它是加拿大发明的，一个希腊移民在安大略的餐馆里瞎捣鼓出来的。所以它的身世就是：希腊人做的披萨，加拿大人配上火腿，最后挂了个夏威夷的名字。我不反对甜咸混搭，糖醋排骨我吃，蜜汁叉烧我也吃。可那些菜不会让我一口咬到热乎乎的奶酪，下一口又咬到冰凉的菠萝，然后两种味道在嘴里开会，开到最后谁也不服谁。

我去芝加哥吃深盘披萨，服务员问要不要切开，我说当然要。端上来一个像小号洗脸盆的东西，边缘厚得比我手指还高。我心想这到底是披萨还是砂锅？咬一口，芝士拉得老长，我以为要拉出个故事来。再咬一口，番茄酱全在最上面，像有人把一锅番茄汤忘在窗台上，底下的芝士被盖得喘不过气。最离谱的是，我吃到一半才明白，这玩意儿不是用来吃的，是用来"挖"的。我拿刀叉，像在工地上拆一面墙。吃完我想给它打个分，可它太厚了，我连底都没摸到。
我去芝加哥吃深盘披萨，服务员端上来，我以为是一锅炖菜。饼边高得像花盆，我得先找找馅在哪。刀子切下去，芝士一路拉到锅底，我吃了半天，还没见到底下那张饼。番茄酱居然盖在最上面，芝士先在底下闷着，番茄当盖子。我问这什么逻辑，他说这是传统。传统就是吃完一块得躺平十分钟，等胃里的芝士凝固。我们那儿吃披萨讲究一口下去烫嘴，这儿是一口下去烫手，烫的还是叉子。

Jackfruit, you look like a medieval mace that got into a fight with a durian and lost. You're the size of a toddler and you have the texture of a sweater that's been through the wash. Vegans picked you up as a pulled-pork substitute, and honestly, that's the most desperate career pivot I've ever seen. "Hey, what if we made people chew a fruit like it's a cheap brisket?" Nobody asked for that. And the smell? Sweet, gym-bag funk, like a banana that climbed into a sock drawer and died there. You're the fruit equivalent of a guy who shows up to a party in a tuxedo made of burlap.

Jackfruit, you look like a sea mine that got into a fight with a durian and lost. Your skin is a crime scene of little green spikes, and nobody has ever cut you open without a prayer and a machete. You're the size of a toddler, you smell like gym socks dipped in bubblegum, and you're somehow both sweet and wet and still sticky after you've been in the fridge. Vegans found you and suddenly you're "pulled pork," which is the most desperate rebrand since "vegetable oil" tried to be a steak. Everybody's grandma loves you for one week a year, then you rot on the counter and the whole kitchen knows. You're a fruit that needs its own safety briefing. Nobody's ever walked out of a grocery store saying, "I'll have the enormous spiky thing that smells like a locker room."
榴莲这东西我真是服了。外面长得像个防暴器材，浑身是刺，你以为里面是炸药，结果一剖开，是一坨黄澄澄的奶油。好东西偏偏穿了一件臭袜子的外衣。你说它臭，它不承认，说这叫"香"。行，你香你的，新加坡地铁直接贴禁止榴莲的标志，人家也知道它是什么级别。最绝的是味道，吃完三天，打个嗝，全办公室都知道你昨晚吃了什么。冰箱里放一个，旁边的牛奶都得跟着发酸。说它是水果之王，我看是水果里的"别靠近我"。

Luosifen is the only food that needs a smell permit. You open the packet in a dorm and the RA shows up asking who's microwaving a crime scene. The broth is snails simmered with pickled bamboo shoots that have been fermenting since before your grandmother was born, and those shoots smell like a gym sock that got promoted to management. People say, "It's delicious once you get past the smell." Sure, and a stink bomb is delicious once you get past the explosion. Then there's the packet of chili oil, which the label calls "optional" in the same tone a hostage-taker uses. Eat it on the subway and the whole car suddenly finds the ceiling fascinating. That's not a meal. That's a restraining order with chopsticks.

榴莲这东西，是全世界最会搞身份认同的水果。你闻一下，它告诉你：我是香的。你再闻一下，它告诉你：我是臭的。它不跟你商量，直接给你两个答案，让你自己站队。地铁上不让带，酒店门口贴的禁止图标上画的不是榴莲，是你的人生选择。好不容易开壳，外面全是刺，手套得戴，跟拆炸弹似的。里面一瓣一瓣金黄的果肉，看着像芝士蛋糕，一口下去，下水道里泡过的臭袜子。我就想问，哪个科学家半夜醒来说："我要让一种水果闻起来像臭袜子，吃完还让人口气陪三天"？这不是水果，这是一份拒绝邀请函。
菠萝蜜这名字起得特别不负责任。叫"菠萝"，结果跟菠萝一点关系没有；叫"蜜"，结果我吃完手上全是胶。我买回来一个，十来公斤，抱回家跟抱了个小孩似的。它还不挂在枝头等人摘，直接长在树干上，像是跟树抢地盘。开它之前得先给刀抹油，手上也得抹油，不然那白浆粘上去，搓三天都搓不掉。我妈说这是老祖宗的智慧。我说老祖宗的智慧就是别让我开。

Luosifen smells like someone microwaved a sewer and called it dinner. You open the packet and the whole building files a noise complaint. Half the dormitories in China have banned it, and the company just says, "That's the flavor," like a skunk insisting that's its cologne. The sour bamboo shoots have been fermenting so long they've got a personal history. The little river snails swim in a broth that tastes exactly like the river they came from. Liuzhou calls it a treasure. Liuzhou also has the river. Then you get to the peanuts, tofu skin, and chili oil, which are there to make you feel like you're eating a meal instead of a crime scene. Honestly, the sealed bag is the most honest thing about it. Even the factory knows nobody wants to smell this one in the open.
菠萝蜜这玩意儿，长得像打了鸡血的榴莲，浑身是刺，还是那种软刺，你以为能掰，掰不动。我第一件事不是吃，是搜"怎么切菠萝蜜"，视频里大佬穿着雨衣、抹着油、拿把菜刀跟它搏斗，我一看，这不是水果，这是考试。切开以后，白汁粘得满手都是，洗三遍手指头还是滑的，我怀疑它是拿胶水做的。香味倒是冲，像熟香蕉混了健身房的袜子。最离谱的是，一个果子能有三四十斤，吃一个月，最后看见它，像看见一个不肯走的亲戚。

Stinky tofu, you're the only food that needs a warning label and a fan club. I smell you two blocks before I see the stall. Your aroma is a crime scene.
