Somebody left a gym sock in a brine barrel for three months, and you're the evidence. Then you get deep-fried so you look like a golden nugget, innocent and crispy, until people bite in and get a faceful of bad decisions. Everyone swears you "taste better than you smell." So does a gas leak, if you're hungry enough. The vendor hands you over with pickled cabbage and chili sauce like he's apologizing on your behalf. Nobody has ever ordered you on a first date.

Stinky tofu is the only food that files a complaint before you've even found the stall. You're three blocks away at the night market and your nose is already asking questions. It's tofu that spent a week soaking in brine that smells like a gym bag left in a hot car, then got deep-fried so the whole street knows what you're doing. They serve it with pickled cabbage, like it needs a chaperone. You bite in, the crispy outside is great, and the inside is basically a fermented cloud. Your jacket smells like it for three days. Your coworkers ask if you were dragged through a sewer. Honestly, though, it's the only snack that shows up to the party knowing it's a mess, and it's still having the best time.

螺蛳粉这东西，开袋那一下，全宿舍就知道你要干嘛了。酸笋一开盖，跟下水道盖子被人掀了似的，还是放了三天的那种。最离谱的是它特别自信，你闻着臭，它吃着香。粉丝滑溜溜的，汤里飘着几根腐竹，还有一撮花生米，你说它到底是个什么东西？我同事中午在工位上吃，整层楼都在问哪来的烧焦袜子味。那层红油浮在汤上，一勺下去，嘴唇红得像刚被人打过，白T恤上溅了两个点，洗不掉。你问我还吃不吃？吃，明天还吃，因为它臭得太有道理了。

螺蛳粉这东西，我真服了。打开袋子那一刻，整层楼的人都知道你在吃什么，那味道不是闻到的，是被它"通知"到的。最绝的是那包酸笋，封得严严实实，像一个被关起来的秘密，一开封，它就想跟你讲道理。我室友说闻着像臭袜子泡在下水道里，我说你说得太客气了，袜子都没它有个性。关键它还特别会"上头"，你明明只想吃一口，最后汤喝得比谁都干净，第二天衣服上还留着它的味道，洗衣机都嫌弃我。偏偏吃完你还得夸它好吃，不然显得你没品位。

Oat milk, you're the Prius of dairy alternatives. You show up at brunch with a tote bag full of opinions, and everybody claps like you saved the planet. Meanwhile you're just oats that got put through a blender and came out looking like wet cardboard with a lawyer. You froth beautifully, sure, but you froth like a guy who just found out his barista certificate expired. And don't get me started on "barista edition." Nobody's a barista because they bought a carton with a cartoon on it. You're basically a shampoo that gave up on being a shampoo and decided to be a latte. Nobody asked you to be creamy. You just showed up creamy-adjacent and expected a parade.

Oat milk, you're not a milk. You're a breakfast cereal that got lost on the way to the cereal aisle and decided to become a beverage out of spite. Somebody took a bowl of oatmeal, ran it through a blender, strained out the dignity, and called it "barista blend." Barista? You've never made a latte in your life. You just foam up like a bubble bath and tell everyone you're the sustainable one. Congratulations, you're the only drink that needs a wellness influencer to explain what's in it. Cows just stand there and produce; you need a whole marketing campaign with a sunrise on the carton. And that sad grey sediment at the bottom of the glass? That's you, admitting the truth.
臭豆腐这东西很诚实，不藏着掖着，三百米外就跟你打招呼。我走在街上闻到味儿，还以为哪个下水道在搞促销。循着味儿一看，排队的人个个捧着一小袋黑乎乎的东西，跟捧着刚从垃圾桶里捡来的宝贝似的。招牌上写着"闻着臭，吃着香"，我真想问一句：你这是承诺还是预警？吃完回家，女朋友捏着鼻子问我："你身上什么味？"我说臭豆腐。她说："你是把厕所抱回家了吧？"

Almond milk, you're not milk. You're almonds that got lost on the way to a smoothie and decided to lie about it. Milk comes from a cow, and a cow has some dignity. You come from a nut that's been soaked in water until it gave up. Somebody squeezed a almond, looked at the sad little puddle, and said, "Yep, that's breakfast."

You're so thin, I can read a newspaper through you. Your idea of creamy is a rumor. You've got less body than a Tuesday. And every carton of you says "Unsweetened" like you're proud of it, like there's a single person alive who wanted to taste nothing.

Almond milk, you're the guy who says he's "not really into drinking" and then orders the oat latte.

我这辈子最诚实的食物就是臭豆腐。别的东西还藏着掖着，它直接在门口把底牌亮了。一股味儿先飘过来，像一双穿了三个月的球鞋泡进了下水道，又拿去油炸。我每次都跟自己商量：鼻子说不吃，嘴说想吃，最后嘴赢，因为钱已经递出去了。老板把黑乎乎的方块丢进油锅，滋啦一声，咬下去，外壳咔嚓脆，里面软嫩嫩，我心想：好家伙，原来你是香的。然后我回家，我妈在门口一闻，说：你又去吃那个了？我说没有。她说，那你身上的味儿是哪来的？我说，那是我的自信。

Almond milk, you are the only thing in the dairy aisle that's named after a nut and still somehow lies about it. Your almond content is roughly the same as the average Tuesday's ambition. Somebody squeezed one almond over a bathtub of water, waved it at the carton, and said, "Yep, that's almond." That's not milk. That's a rumor.

And the color! You look like a glass of wet drywall. Put you next to real milk and you're the sad cousin who showed up to the wedding in the same beige as the tablecloth. Nobody asked you to be white. You're just gray with a vague sense of purpose.

You also taste like you're trying to apologize for something. Every sip says, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry." Pour yourself into a latte and the barista's already plotting how to hide the foam.

Vegas, you're the only city where the pyramid has a light beam that's brighter than the sun, and you still can't find the sun. You built a fake Eiffel Tower, a fake Venice with fake gondoliers singing fake opera, and a fake New York with a roller coaster around the Statue of Liberty. Honestly, that's the most accurate tour of America I've ever taken. Everything's a copy, and nobody wants to leave. You've got clocks with no windows, casinos with no clocks, and a wedding chapel open at four in the morning for people who forgot what they agreed to at ten. Your motto should be "What happens here stays here," but your hotel bills say otherwise.

Vegas, you're the only city where the pyramid has a light beam shooting into space, and somehow the most depressing thing is the hotel. You've got a fake Venice with a gondolier who's clearly on a break from his real job at the Gap. Eiffel Tower at 1/4 scale, so the French are just fine with you as long as you keep the Eiffel Tower a little embarrassed. Your slogan is "What happens here stays here," which is a lie, because I've seen what happens here, and it's all showing up on my credit card statement in the spring. You run on oxygen that's pumped into casinos so nobody notices the clock. Your buffets are all-you-can-eat, which is a dare. You're a city built on the idea that the house always wins, and honestly, Vegas, you're the house.

我现在点咖啡，店员总要问一句：要燕麦奶吗？好像不喝燕麦奶，就是对地球不负责任。行，我喝。端上来一看，颜色是那种米汤色。你说它是牛奶，它比牛奶脏；你说它是豆浆，它又没那股豆腥味，就是一种很诚实的灰白。我仔细想了想燕麦奶是什么：一把燕麦泡水，打碎，过滤，然后告诉你这是奶。我小时候喝粥，碗底总有一层糊，我妈说那是好东西。现在好了，粥不用煮了，直接兑水，卖你二十八。最离谱的是喝到杯底，还有一层白沙，我都不知道是该吞下去还是该嚼一嚼。

我最服燕麦奶的一点是，它明明是燕麦磨的，非要叫"奶"。燕麦说它不是奶，奶说它不是燕麦，最后它自己站在超市货架上，说："我是植物基。"植物基？听着像是要去当卧底。

你看它那颜色，灰不溜秋的，跟刷完锅的洗碗水一个色号。可咖啡店偏拿它打奶泡，拉花拉得特别好看。我一看，哦，洗碗水穿上西装了。

最离谱的是价格。牛奶是奶牛一口草一口奶产出来的，燕麦奶就是机器把燕麦泡了泡、磨了磨，一瓶还比牛奶贵。我就想问一句：牛呢？这头牛是不是连班都不用上，工资还比它高？

我喝杏仁奶，就是冲着"杏仁"两个字去的。结果翻开配料表，第一位是水，第二位还是水，杏仁排到第四，前面还站着白砂糖。这哪是杏仁奶，这是"路过杏仁的水"。

你说它有没有杏仁味？有啊，就是那种甜腻的、像便利店蛋糕的味道。可真杏仁是苦的你知道吗？苦得舌头发麻那种。商家一看，好，那就加糖吧，糖加到压住苦味，最后喝起来既不像杏仁，也不像牛奶，像一杯在努力假装自己有营养的糖水。

还有那个包装，上面画着一堆饱满的大杏仁，颜色金黄，阳光打在上面。结果倒出来是灰白的，放两小时还会分层，底下沉着一层不知道是什么的白渣。我摇了半天，摇出来的还是一杯失望。

杏仁奶这东西，我是服的，它把"我是水"这件事干得很有格调。包装上画满杏仁，像刚从树上摘下来。翻到背面配料表，第一位是水，第二位是糖，杏仁排第五，挨着"食用盐"。意思很明白：这不是杏仁奶，是水里路过过一次杏仁。

我去咖啡店点杏仁拿铁，店员特别认真地问：加杏仁奶吗？加了多收五块。我说行，给我加个有文化的水。

最离谱的是冲咖啡。牛奶倒进去，乖乖变成奶咖；杏仁奶倒进去，咖啡表情管理失败，整杯变成灰的，像一杯没写完的作业。

它还特别爱标"无乳糖"。废话，它本来就没奶。你跟一瓶水说"我不含牛的东西"，水也很无辜。
我去拉斯维加斯，最诚实的东西是金字塔顶上那道光柱。它告诉你这儿埋着三千年的法老，其实是家酒店。威尼斯人酒店里面有运河，船夫在里面唱歌，抬头是画上去的蓝天。你在里面待三天，以为外面还是白天。出门一看，是四十五度的沙漠。我回去问荷官现在几点，他说："先生，我们这儿没有钟，只有筹码。"

我去拉斯维加斯，发现这儿最会骗人的是时间。赌场里没有钟，没有窗，你进去玩三个小时，出来太阳已经换了一轮。他们把时间藏起来，就为了让你忘了今天几号，等结账再提醒你。

酒店也一样。沙漠中间盖了座巴黎铁塔，还是缩小版的。我问为什么不盖大的，服务员说，大的在巴黎。

最绝的是“度假费”。房价写一百，结账多收四十，名字叫度假费。他们的标语是“在这儿发生的事，留在这儿”，我信了，结果留下的是我的工资。我住的是个房间，度假的是他们。

Macau, you're the only city where the fake Venice has better canals than the real one. You dredged your land out of the sea, built a replica of Venice on top, and hired gondoliers to sing to tourists who just lost their rent at baccarat. Your economy is one enormous slot machine with a Portuguese accent. Your most famous landmark is a church facade with nothing behind it, which is the most honest thing on your skyline. You're 33 square kilometers, so small you can walk across yourself before your egg tart cools. Everybody comes to you to lose money, and you're thrilled to take it. Keep the lights on, little sinner.

Macau, you're the only place where a fake Venice has a fake gondola and the gondolas still lose money. You're about ten Central Parks wide, so your casinos can't spread out and have to go up, like a city that got lost looking for space. Your cathedral is just a facade, a church that gave up on the church part. Your egg tarts are the best thing you've ever exported, and you did it by accident, like a bank robbery that ends with pastries. The bridge to Hong Kong took the better part of a decade, which is the most patience you've ever shown anyone. Nobody comes to Macau to see Macau. They come to lose money, and they leave with an egg tart and a receipt.

Canberra: the only city where the traffic jam is a roundabout with a sculpture in the middle. A century ago, someone looked at a sheep paddock between Sydney and Melbourne and said, "Let's put the whole country's government here so nobody has to visit." And it worked. Parliament House sits on its hill like a very expensive filing cabinet. The lake is named after an American architect, and it's the most exciting thing that happens here. Winter mornings hit minus four, and the only people outside are joggers with a grudge. Friday night out means the Civic bar, where everyone's a public servant with a lanyard still on. Nobody lives in Canberra. They're just waiting for a posting.
我去澳门，最大的感受是这地方小到离谱。半岛走一个下午就走完了，想坐车，站牌上葡文加中文我还没看懂，车已经开到氹仔了。后来去威尼斯人酒店，里面有运河，有船夫唱歌，抬头一看，天花板画的是蓝天白云。我说这才是真威尼斯，比真的还干净。朋友拍我一下：小声点，你看那边赌台上坐着个大哥，三天没见过太阳了，现在还以为自己在过早上。
去澳门，我本来以为是来看历史的。一下船，大三巴就在那儿，人挤得跟春运似的，还没看清，就被导游推进一家杏仁饼店。出来又排了四十分钟队买葡挞，结果一问，葡萄牙人都不这么排队。走到威尼斯人，天花板画着假天空，贡多拉在假运河上划，船夫还给你唱歌。我问他水是从哪儿引的，他说引的是赌场的钱。最后我明白了，这座城市很讲道理：古迹给你看，假天空给你看，出门前你的钱包已经在老虎机上旅行了一圈。
堪培拉是两个城市吵架吵出来的。悉尼和墨尔本都想当首都，谁也不服，最后干脆在中间盖了一个。所以堪培拉就是澳洲的"和事佬"，一个专门负责两边都不得罪的城市。晚上八点你去市中心看看，街上的人比袋鼠还少。袋鼠好歹还敢在马路上蹦两下，堪培拉的人都窝在家里等着第二天上班。环岛也多得离谱，像是设计师画图的时候喝多了，一圈接一圈画不停。导航在环岛里转了三圈，最后把你原样送回出发的地方，像在说：来了就别想走。

Canberra is the only capital in Australia built from scratch, which explains a lot. Sydney and Melbourne were so busy hating each other they agreed to put the country's brain in a paddock halfway between them, and it has been sulking ever since. Walter Burley Griffin drew it up as a neat wheel of boulevards around a lake, then the public servants arrived and discovered that every road in town is a roundabout. Nobody has ever found the way out of Civic. The nightlife shuts at nine because the whole city is in bed before Question Time ends. The lake is named after Griffin, which is a shame, because he's the only man ever to design a city and then get a lake named after him instead of a train station. In winter the frost is so thick the ministers need a scraper before they can go inside and be lied to.

堪培拉是澳大利亚的首都，但你问一个澳洲人首都在哪，他多半说悉尼，然后停顿三秒，想起来还有这么个地方。这城市是当年悉尼和墨尔本吵得没完没了，最后大家一拍桌子："那就盖一个谁都不想住的城市吧。"结果真盖出来了。全城设计得太规整，规整到你根本不会迷路，只会在同一个环岛上转到怀疑人生。晚上八点，街上空无一人，倒是袋鼠成群结队地蹲在马路边。它们是全城唯一还在营业的，看着你开车路过，像在问："你也是来这儿找乐子的？"

Brasília is the only city where the architects designed everything except a reason to go outside. Niemeyer built the Cathedral like a flying saucer that gave up halfway, and Lúcio Costa laid the city out like an airplane, which explains why everyone's been circling the same runway of traffic since 1960. The superquadras all look identical, so when you get lost, you're not lost, you're just on a different block of the same block. There are no corners to lean on, no street to wander, just six lanes and a bus stop that's more of a rumor. The people who clean the ministries live out in Ceilândia and commute two hours to get there. And it's so dry your lips file for divorce.

Brasília is the only city where you need a car to get lost. Lúcio Costa drew it as an airplane, which explains everything: it was built to be admired from 30,000 feet and never walked in. Every superquadra looks identical, so locals give directions like "third block, the one with the tree." Niemeyer's cathedral looks like a concrete UFO that landed in a bad mood. Congress has one bowl facing up and one facing down, which is the most honest thing about the government. The air is so dry your nosebleeds have nosebleeds, the lake looks like a screensaver, and the nearest bar is eleven kilometers away on a highway with no sidewalk.

Juicero raised over a hundred million dollars to build a $400 juicer that squeezed packets of pre-chopped kale. Then a reporter showed you could get the same juice by squeezing the packets with your bare hands. That's not a juicer. That's a hand. Your hand already came with the machine. The press checked a QR code on each pack before it would run, so you paid for a Wi-Fi juicer that needed the internet to tell it to do the job a towel does. And people paid it! Venture capitalists looked at a $5 bag of spinach and thought, "Yes, this needs a server." The company shut down in 2017. Honestly, that's the most productive thing the press has ever done.
巴西利亚是1960年从一片荒地上凭空造出来的首都，设计图据说是一架飞机，或者一只鸟，反正从天上看挺有格调。问题是我们是在地上走的。这城市的人指路不说"前面左拐"，说"你去308区，到了往北走"。308是什么？是一栋楼的编号！所以你得先背楼号，再背方向，最后还得背自己是怎么落到这儿的。我在那儿迷路三次，每次都怪那些楼长得一模一样，像同一个建筑师在同一个下午被催了七遍稿。

Juicero built a $400 Wi-Fi press whose entire job was squeezing a bag. Not a fruit. A bag. Somebody looked at a pouch of pre-chopped kale and decided it needed a computer. Then a reporter showed everyone you could wring the packs out with your bare hands, and the venture capitalists went quiet, like they'd just realized their $120 million bought a very expensive pair of hands. The press checked a QR code before it would crush your spinach. That's the most Silicon Valley sentence ever written: the machine needed permission to juice. The packs cost about five bucks each, so you were paying premium prices to do what a Capri Sun does on its own.

Keurig, you're the only appliance that makes a cup of coffee and then apologizes for it by making you wait four minutes while it hums like a dying refrigerator. You're a single-serve machine with the commitment of a Tinder profile: one pod, one cup, and you'll never call back. Every morning I stare into your little plastic mouth, feed you a pod that cost more per ounce than gold, and you spit out something that tastes like a coffee bean's ghost. And the recycling? Those pods are tiny landfills with lids. You didn't make coffee, Keurig. You made a subscription plan wearing a drip tray. Even your name sounds like a sneeze that got a corporate loan.

Keurig, you're the coffee maker that treats a cup of coffee like a hostage negotiation. Eight minutes of whirring, gurgling, and blinking just to produce a lukewarm thimble of brown water. Meanwhile my grandma's percolator makes a full pot before I finish reading the Wikipedia article about pour-over.

And the pods! Every cup creates a little plastic tombstone. You're basically a landfill with a power button. You've got more recyclable-pod-related guilt than my Catholic school.

Then there's the "strong" setting, which is just the regular setting with a dramatic pause. Nothing about you is bold except your price per ounce.

Keurig, you're not a coffee maker. You're a vending machine that got a cardiology degree.

巴西利亚是个飞机形状的城市，我一直没搞懂，设计者是想让它起飞，还是想让人降落？我去找一家小卖部，发现这座城市几乎没有拐角。所有房子都是按图纸一排排摆出来的超级街区，地址长得像飞机票：308区B座302。我问出租车司机能不能送我去，他说："哦，你朋友住那儿？"我说不是，那是地址。最惨的是你没法走路，走去买瓶水要四十分钟，路两边只有草和风。在这儿待了三天，我终于明白，全国的政府机构都搬来这里办公，是因为在这座城市里，没人能轻易找到谁。
我看到一台榨汁机，要四百多美元，还要联网。它不是直接榨，是先用摄像头扫一下你那袋蔬果包上的二维码，确认是正版，才肯把压板往下放。我就想问，这么大阵仗，防的是谁？防我偷吃菠菜吗？后来有人试了，把那袋东西拿出来用手一挤，汁哗哗地流，压根不用它。四百块买的不是榨汁机，是一个要先通过安检才能开工的压板。最离谱的是，我的手不用联网，力气也不用付月费，居然比它还好用。

我前两天看到一个新闻，说有个榨汁机叫Juicero，要价699美元。我以为是什么黑科技，结果就是个铁盒子，上面一块扫码的屏幕。你得先买它家专用的果汁包，塞进去，它扫一下包上的二维码，确认你买的是正版，然后用很大的力把包压扁。

我就想问：你买的是榨汁机，还是保安？果汁包已经切好、装好了，你要的就是压一下，结果机器先得验明正身。那我用手捏行不行？记者真去试了，两只手一捏，果汁照样出来。699美元的机器，输给了两只手。

后来公司倒闭，我一点都不意外。一台要联网认证的榨汁机，最后被用户用手拧死了。

Crocs are shoes designed by someone who saw a bath mat and thought, "Yes, but what if it had holes so my feet could breathe while I pretend I'm a surgeon at a Cracker Barrel?" They look like the foam that sits on a hot dog's bun. They're the only footwear where the heel is basically a suggestion. You can't run in them, you can't hike in them, and you definitely can't sneak up on anyone, because every step sounds like a duck being slowly squeezed. And somehow they're on the feet of grown adults who own a mortgage. Nobody wears Crocs to look good. You wear Crocs because you've accepted that your feet have given up, and you've decided the shoe should match that energy. Honestly, respect. You're the only person at the Target parking lot who's fully at peace.

Crocs are the only shoe that looks like it was designed by a committee of ducks. Every pair is a foam clog with holes in it, like someone started making shoes, got bored halfway through, and said, "Eh, the air can have the rest." Nobody has ever bought Crocs to look good. You buy them because they're the only shoe that can survive a flood, a hospital shift, and a barbecue at the same time. They come with little charms you snap into the holes, which is how you know the company has given up on fashion and moved into hostage negotiation: "Fine, you want a shoe, we'll give you a shoe with a pizza slice stuck in its side." And somehow they're everywhere. Grandpas, nurses, teenagers, and one guy at every Costco who hasn't left the house since 2009. Crocs don't walk, they waddle. That's not a shoe, that's a rubber duck that lost a bet.

我家那台Keurig，我一直觉得它不是咖啡机，是个要我每天做仪式的怪人。先把水箱拔出来灌水，掀开盖子，塞一颗K-Cup进去，再把盖子用力压到“咔”一声，它才肯动。一启动就嗡嗡响，跟直升机起飞似的，我还以为它要带我去上班。最绝的是那个“浓度”按钮，我按了三年，出来的咖啡还是一个颜色，那按钮纯粹是给用户的安慰剂。还有那颗胶囊，撕开铝箔一看，里面的咖啡渣泡成了饼。我这一杯，花的时间比手冲还长，喝起来像是温水加了点悔恨。

我家那台Keurig，我管它叫"咖啡界的自动贩卖机"。每次开机都轰隆隆响半分钟，跟火箭发射似的，结果流出来的是一杯颜色像洗碗水的东西。我就想问，它到底是在煮咖啡，还是在发射咖啡？那个Strong键我按了三次，味道一点没变，跟我前任的承诺一个道理，按了等于没按。最离谱的是那个胶囊，一个塑料小杯，顶上封一层铝膜，喝完还得自己扣出来扔掉。我每天早上都要先面对一堆小塑料杯的尸体，像个凶案现场的法医，然后才能喝上一口。

Ugg boots are the only footwear that looks like it was made from a dead sheep and then slept in. They're basically two slippers that gave up on their dreams and went to college. You don't wear Uggs, you just stop trying in a boot shape. Nobody has ever run for a bus in Uggs. Nobody has ever been caught in the rain in Uggs. They're for the Starbucks line at 8 a.m. and the Costco parking lot, and that's it. And the name! "Ugg." That's not a brand, that's a noise you make when you step on a Lego. Somebody in a boardroom said, "Let's sell people shoes that sound like disappointment," and everybody nodded. Then they charged two hundred dollars for them.

Ugg boots are the only shoe that looks like a sheep ate a pair of slippers and then apologized by giving them back. You didn't buy Uggs, you bought a pair of carpet remnants that wandered into a shoe store and got lucky. Nobody's ever run in them. Nobody's ever been chased in them. They're designed for one thing: standing in a Target parking lot holding an oat milk latte like you just finished a marathon. And the name! "Ugg." That's not a brand, that's a noise you make when you step on a Lego in the dark. Somewhere, a shearling farmer is looking at these and saying, "I didn't raise sheep for this, I raised them to be respected." Stay warm, I guess. You look like a hot dog that gave up.

Monopoly is the only board game where the goal is to bankrupt your friends and somehow everyone still agrees to play it again. Four hours. Four hours! Nobody has ever finished a game of Monopoly. The game just ends when someone's dad flips the table, or when the banker quietly starts pretending they didn't count the money properly. And the banker, by the way, is always the least trustworthy person at the table, because they're the one holding the stack of cash and they're the one who "forgot" to collect Free Parking. Free Parking! That's not a gift, that's a lie you tell children. And Boardwalk? Nobody's ever landed on Boardwalk and felt lucky. They just felt the rent go up like a hostage negotiation. Monopoly: where your uncle buys every railroad and calls it a "strategy."

洞洞鞋我真服了。鞋上打一堆洞，说是为了透气。行，我信。可那些洞的位置，正好对着地上的沙子、小石子、头发丝，它不是透气，是专门给外面的东西留的后门。我穿它去趟海边，回家脚底下像带了个采集队。

最离谱的是那个Jibbitz，专门卖小挂件，一双鞋能挂二十个。走起路来叮叮当当，跟个卖烧烤的推车似的。我一个成年人，鞋上挂着小草莓、小恐龙，去开会的时候脚一抬，全桌人都在看我的鞋。

我买了双洞洞鞋，店员说这鞋透气。我说好啊，穿上才发现，它不是透气，是根本没拦着。脚趾头在外面迎风招展，跟路人打招呼。那些洞你以为是设计，其实是专门给沙子留的门，走两步鞋里就开了个小集市。

鞋上还能挂小挂件，叫Jibbitz。我一个成年人，鞋上挂着小草莓、小恐龙，走路叮当响，像个移动的文具盒。每次低头看见，都觉得这双鞋在说：你已经放弃治疗了。

最离谱的是那材料，软得跟刚出锅的年糕似的。走路"啪嗒啪嗒"响，像后面有人一直鼓掌。我回头看，没人，就是鞋自己在拍手。
UGG这个名字真诚实，念出来就是一声“呃”。买之前你“呃”一下，买完穿上你又“呃”一下。它长得像什么？像一只羊把自己的卧室剪下来，套在你脚上，还要你花三千块。说是取暖，其实就是让你的脚住进一头羊的被窝。最绝的是下雨天，那层羊毛一沾水，立刻从雪白变成厕所地砖的颜色。你跟朋友说这是雪地靴，他低头看一眼说：你这是在雪地里滚了一圈的拖鞋吧。

我买UGG那天，店员说："这是澳洲羊皮，内里是羊毛，保暖。"我一想，这不就是把一只羊整个扒下来，毛朝外套我脚上吗？羊都没这么穿过自己。穿上一低头，两个栗子色的大团子踩在地上，像两只刚从狗窝爬出来的小熊。鞋口那圈毛一直往外翻，我走在路上，感觉路人都以为我是刚从冰柜拿出来的烤羊腿。最离谱的是鞋底，薄得跟纸一样，我在小区雪地上走了两步，差点劈个叉。店员还说"雪地靴就是要在雪里穿"，我说行，那我到底是进了雪，还是进了羊？

Risk is the only board game where the map is the villain. Australia is one continent with four borders, and somehow it's the thing everyone wants to fight over. Kamchatka is a Russian peninsula nobody could find if you paid them, and it becomes the most important place on Earth for six straight hours. You know the game's dragging when you're hoping someone rolls a three just to end the suffering. The dice are cheap six-siders you shake in a cup, so entire wars get decided by two guys who could lose a continent in the time it takes to say "I'm not mad, I'm just disappointed." And there's always that guy eliminated since nine o'clock, still sitting at the table holding his cards like a hostage negotiation, begging someone to betray their ally and save him. Nobody has ever finished Risk. You just stop when the pizza's cold.

Monopoly is the only board game where the goal is to bankrupt your friends, and the game itself bankrupts the friendship. It's been around ninety years and nobody has ever finished it. Your cousin Dave, who owns Boardwalk and two hotels, isn't a real estate mogul. He's a man who spent three hours shorting the bank. And the banker! The one person trusted with the stack of pink fives, and every single time he "accidentally" gives himself two hundred bucks. Free Parking is a lie. Nobody has ever landed there and collected the jackpot. The little top hat has been in the same spot since 1935 and still gets no respect. Let's be honest: the only property you can afford is Baltic Avenue, and that's because the game put it there to make you feel bad.

Risk is the only board game where the goal is world domination and somehow everyone ends up furious about it. You spend four hours conquering continents while your friend sits there holding Australia, which is basically a fortress with one door and a view of nothing. Kamchatka is the most dangerous place on Earth. It's one territory, and it eats two of your tiny plastic armies every time someone looks at it. Then there's the dice. Three red against two blue, and the fate of the entire planet comes down to a guy yelling "I'm rolling for Siberia!" every game ends the same way: Greg, who swore he'd only be a few minutes, owns Asia, a grudge, and your Alaska.

Nobody's ever bought an NFT. They bought a receipt that says "you own this JPEG," and the JPEG is a cartoon ape with a bowler hat, the same JPEG you can right-click and save in four seconds. So they paid four hundred thousand dollars for a screenshot with a certificate. It's the only art in history where the certificate is the art. The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre with a crowd of tourists, and this guy's ape is hanging in a folder called "wallet" that nobody else can see. Ownership, they call it. Congratulations, you own the ape, and the ape doesn't know you exist.

玩大富翁，我最服的是那个银行家。发钱、收钱、管账，一辈子不出门，还穿得跟来参加婚礼似的。我呢？绕着棋盘跑一圈，路过起点领两百块，现实里路过起点，只能领一张外卖券。

最离谱的是监狱。进去不用干活，还能在里面收租。我要是在现实里能这么坐牢，早报名了。

还有Free Parking，免费停车场。规则写着停这儿什么都不发生，我停了三回，停到我妈来接我。

最狠的是我兄弟，他把木板路和海滨大道都买了，盖满酒店。我们一路踩进去，踩到个个破产。他一边收钱一边说："都是朋友，不用客气。"这话我在现实里听过，是房东说的。
大富翁我玩过一次，就再也不想碰了。绕一圈领两百块，绕十圈还是两百块，通货膨胀在这儿根本不存在。好不容易买了条"木板路"，人家一踩上来就得给我交一大笔租金，我心想这下发了，结果三圈下来，房子全抵押给银行了，我还在给人打工。进监狱更离谱，掷不出双数就得在里面耗着，别人在外面吃香喝辣，我在牢里数骰子。最后赢家是那个银行，它从头到尾没掷过一次骰子，光坐着收钱。

Nobody's ever been mugged for an NFT, and that's the scam. You can't steal it, you can't hang it on a wall, and you can't even right-click save it without the cartoon ape judging you. You paid four thousand dollars for a receipt. A receipt that says, "I own the JPEG of a bored monkey," and the JPEG is still sitting on a server in Ohio, unbothered. Your grandma bought Beanie Babies and at least she got a fabric bear she could hug. You bought a hyperlink with a pulse. And the best part? The guy who sold it to you already cashed out and bought a yacht named after the ape you didn't get to keep.
《大战略》这名字起得很诚实，叫Risk，风险。我开局占了澳大利亚，四块地，只有一个出口通印尼，等于在自家门口被锁了门。老王一把骰子扔下去，我三个兵没了，骰子还是他自己带来的。最离谱的是堪察加，隔着一条白令海峡跟阿拉斯加对望，老王在那边憋了两个小时，就为了从西伯利亚跳过去跟我决斗。玩了四个小时，三个人聊了一下午，最后谁都没统治世界，桌上只剩一个人还在扔骰子，他的兵全是一。
我花一万块买了一张NFT，卖家说这叫不可替代代币。我问：那图片我能拥有吗？他说当然，链上写着你是唯一持有人。我说那我右键另存为行不行？他沉默三秒：可以，但你存下来的是图片，所有权不在里面。我说那我买的到底是啥？他说是一串哈希值，指向一个服务器。我说服务器要是倒了呢？他说那你就拥有一个不可替代的空链接。我说那我想换一个行不行？他说不行，这叫不可替代。

Beanie Babies, you're the only toy whose value depends on a tag announcing you're dead. "Retired." That's not a collectible, that's a hospice with a barcode. Ty Warner figured out that if he stopped making a bear, grown adults would panic-buy it like the last lifeboat on the Titanic. Parents mortgaged houses for Peanut the Elephant. Now your grandma's attic holds forty thousand of you, each worth less than the postage to mail it. And you were the only stuffed animal with a birth certificate stapled to your butt. You're not even stuffed with beans. It's plastic pellets. Honestly, that's the most honest thing about you.

我前年花三千块买了个NFT，一张猴子头像。卖家说，你买的是独一无二的数字所有权。我问，所有权在哪？他说在区块链上。我点开证明链接，一串0x开头的乱码，看得我眼都花了。然后我右键“另存为”，三秒钟，我就拥有了一模一样的猴子。我问他：那我跟你的猴子有什么区别？他说，区别是你没有证书。我说证书呢？他说在链上。我说那能不能打印出来挂墙上？他想了想，说可以，但是要先付gas费。我一算，我花三千买了一张免费的图，外加一串打印不出来的乱码，还要交手续费。这猴子看我的眼神，比我还无奈。

《战国风云》最狠的地方，是名字叫"风险"，玩了才知道，最大的风险是盟友。开局说好一起守亚洲，他转头就把堪察加的兵全调走，我眼睁睁看着自己的堪察加没了。我问他为什么，他说："这叫战略。"规则书写的是"可以攻击任何相邻领地"，没写"不许背刺"。骰子更离谱，我进攻掷三个六，他防守掷两个一，结果我还是输了。我花三个小时打下的澳大利亚，就这么被一把骰子送走。最惨的是被淘汰的人，要坐在旁边看另外两个人打到天亮，连手里的牌都没地方放。

My mom bought forty Beanie Babies in 1998 because a man on the news said they'd pay for my college. They didn't. They're in a bin in her garage, each one still wrapped in its plastic tag protector like a tiny hostage. Ty Warner pulled off the greatest con in toy history. He retired a bear, announced it like a celebrity death, and watched grown adults panic-buy the thing they were supposed to play with. You weren't allowed to touch it, though. Touching meant fingerprints, and fingerprints meant it was worth nothing. So you didn't get a teddy bear. You got a bag of plastic pellets with a face, sitting on a shelf, guarded like the Crown Jewels.

You know what Slack is? It's a meeting that refuses to start. Somebody's typing for four minutes, and then it's just "k." Thanks, Dave. Four minutes for a letter.

And the little dots! Everybody's watching those dots like they're a heart monitor. "Dave is typing..." Dave has been typing since Tuesday.

Slack is where we go to "circle back" and never come back. Then there's the huddle. You can't call it a meeting, because that would be too honest. It's a "huddle," like we're a bunch of football players who just need a quick word about the Dorito situation.

And the status emoji! Little palm tree, "OOO." Sure, Brenda. You're on a beach, and you're replying to #marketing-updates from a beach.
豆豆娃这玩意儿，我小时候家里人人都买，说是投资。我妈给每只都套上透明塑料套，吊牌缝在屁股上，她天天擦，跟供祖宗牌位似的。最离谱的是它叫"Beanie"，里面却是塑料小颗粒，一捏沙沙响，压根不是豆子。一只叫"豆"的娃娃，肚子里一颗豆都没有，这是我见过最诚实的营销失败。后来它宣布"退休"，我妈当场就哭了，说早知道该留着当养老金。结果现在二手市场上，一只"绝版"的企鹅卖的还没我当年的零花钱多。
Slack最狠的是那个绿点。你一上线，绿点亮着，全公司都知道你在。你不回消息？绿点在那儿看着你呢。更绝的是@here，一按下去，全频道几百号人手机同时震，就为了问一句"有人吗"。我说，你要真有事，你打电话啊。结果没人接，全都回一个表情包，"收到👍"。还有那个"正在输入…"三个小点，闪了五分钟，最后发过来一个"好的"。我盯着那三个点，比等开奖还煎熬。
我小时候，我妈给我买了一只豆豆娃，说这是"未来的退休金"。我当时还真信了。它屁股上缝着一张吊牌，写着出生日期，精确到哪天，像户口本似的。后来我才知道，它肚子里填的不是棉花，是塑料小珠子，摇起来哗啦哗啦响，跟一包拆了口的薯片差不多。它不是玩具，是一个有编号的小布袋。我妈把它锁进玻璃柜，说千万别碰，一碰就掉价。这些年我才明白，她不是在保值，她是在替一只没人要的熊保管身份证。

Slack, you're the only app where a little green dot controls people's moods. We all stare at it like a heart monitor. "Dave's active? Dave's ignoring me personally."

You turned "quick question" into a four-hour ordeal. Somebody types "hey," then nothing, and the whole office watches three little dots dance for twenty minutes like they're drafting the Gettysburg Address. Then comes "can you hop on a huddle?" Nobody has ever hopped.

And #random? That channel has never been random. It's a graveyard of cat GIFs and a 2019 poll about lunch.

You're the reason we have 47 unread notifications and zero idea what's going on. Do Not Disturb is your most-ignored feature, and you know it.

You know what Teams is? It's the office that's always on fire but nobody's ever seen the smoke. Every message comes with "...is typing" for six minutes, and then it says "Hi." Your green dot says "Available" while you're literally in the bathroom. You join a meeting and the first ten minutes are "Can you hear me?" "You're on mute." "Wait, I'm sharing the wrong screen." Then somebody says, "Let's take this offline," which, in Teams, means it's now a 45-minute call titled "Quick Sync." And the app eats more RAM than the entire Windows 95 installation. Teams, you're the only thing that's ever made my laptop fan sound like it's begging for a transfer.
Slack最损的是那个绿点。我下班关电脑，它还亮着，像门口保安盯着你："还没走？"同事在#随便聊聊频道里@我一句"在吗"，然后就没下文了。我盯着那三个跳动的小点"正在输入…"看了四分钟，最后他打出一句："哈哈，算了，没事。"我谢谢你，差点让我把晚饭都想好了。还有那个"勿扰模式"，开了跟没开一样，头像旁边还是那个绿点，别人一看就知道你在装死。

Microsoft Teams, you're the only app with the nerve to open itself the second I log in, like a hall monitor who got promoted. Every meeting starts with the same ritual: "Can you hear me?" "You're on mute." "Sorry, you're on mute." Thirty seconds of people unmuting like it's a hostage situation. And that little "Someone is typing..." bubble? It's been there since Tuesday. Nobody's typing, Teams. Nobody's ever typing. You tell me I'm "Available" while I'm literally in a meeting, then ping me four minutes after everyone else has already replied. "Let's take this offline," says the guy, and then he schedules a Teams call about it. Teams, you're not a chat app. You're a conference room that follows you home.
Teams最绝的是那个绿点。我下班关了电脑，它还亮着绿灯，意思是"这人还在线"。半夜老板@我，我一看状态是绿的，我能怎么办？只能装死。结果三分钟后它自动把我变成黄色的"离开"，全公司都知道我在装。开会更离谱，我明明按了静音，全场却听见我妈在喊吃饭。那个静音按钮，在它眼里大概只是个建议。

LaTeX, you're the only program that makes a document look like a Pulitzer and then sends you a nine-hundred-line error log because you forgot a bracket. "Missing $ inserted." Where? Everywhere. Your error messages read like a ransom note. And the figures! I put a picture in, and it floats off to page nine like it has somewhere better to be. I write to say "here," and you say, "Mm, I'll be the judge of that." Centering a table takes three hours, a booktabs package, and a prayer. Then I compile, get a PDF so beautiful I almost forgive you, and you hit me with "Overfull \hbox, badness 10000." Badness. You named it. You're the only typesetter honest enough to put its own insult in the log.
text_raw: LaTeX, you're the only program that makes a document look like a Pulitzer and then sends you a nine-hundred-line error log because you forgot a bracket. "Missing $ inserted." Where? Everywhere. Your error messages read like a ransom note. And the figures! I put a picture in, and it floats off to page nine like it has somewhere better to be. I write [h] to say "here," and you say, "Mm, I'll be the judge of that." Centering a table takes three hours, a booktabs package, and a prayer. Then I compile, get a PDF so beautiful I almost forgive you, and you hit me with "Overfull \hbox, badness 10000." Badness. You named it. You're the only typesetter honest enough to put its own insult in the log.

text: LaTeX, you're a word processor that makes me pass a programming exam just to type "hello." I need a backslash, three curly braces, and a prayer to make one word bold. Forget a single dollar sign and you scream "Missing $ inserted," like I personally mugged your math mode. Then you throw "Emergency stop" at me, which is rude, because I'm the one who's supposed to be panicking. Want a table? Enjoy three hours wrestling ampersands and \hline like they owe you money. Bibliography? Run the compiler three times, like a coach yelling "one more lap" because the first two didn't count. Your fans swear the output is gorgeous. Sure, so is a cathedral, and nobody builds a grocery list out of one.
Teams最让我服的是它的"状态"。我早上九点一登录，它就自动把我标成"离开"。我人明明坐在工位上，它比我还会摸鱼。老板在频道里@我，我一看自己显示"忙碌中"，心想：我忙什么？我在这儿给你装忙啊！最绝的是开会。我想共享一个PPT，手一滑点到了旁边那个"共享屏幕"，全组十二个人看见我浏览器标签页里挂着"如何体面地离职"。那一刻我的状态只有一个：离线。

Microsoft Word, you're the only program that's been around for forty years and still can't tell me where the bullet point ends. I type one dash, hit enter, and suddenly you're deciding I'm running a whole bulleted empire. I try to undo it and you go, "Nope, here's an indented sub-bullet instead." Thanks, Clippy's grumpy cousin.

And the "Track Changes" feature? You're named after a document, but you treat every edit like a crime scene. Someone changes "the" to "a" and suddenly the whole page looks like a kindergarten finger painting, red lines everywhere, and nobody knows who did it.

Then there's the page numbers. Page one is perfect. Page two is fine. Page nine just quietly starts itself over at one because you got bored.

Forty years, Word. You've seen everything. Still can't center a title without me holding my breath.

Microsoft Word is the only program that has a paperclip for a mascot, and it still managed to be the most annoying thing on the screen. You type one space in the middle of a sentence and the whole document rearranges itself like it's moving apartments. Every image you insert becomes a hostage that refuses to stay on page four. And that blue squiggle under your name? Word thinks *you're* the typo. Then there's Compatibility Mode, the program's way of saying, "I've seen your file, and I'm not going to pretend I understand it." Twenty years of updates, and the only thing it's truly mastered is looking shocked when you press Ctrl+S.

我用LaTeX写论文，感觉不是在排版，是在跟一个很较真的老古板打交道。

想放张图，我写，它说："好的，我尽量。"结果图被它踢到第十页，像个离家出走的孩子。

打个下划线想写变量名，它直接报错：Missing $ inserted。我说我就想要个下划线，它说："下划线在我这儿是下标，没有美元符号你休想。"我就想写个a_1，它给我整成了高数考试。

好不容易编译通过，一看，右边的字都跑出页边了，还弹一句Overfull \hbox。翻译过来就是：你话太多，我装不下，但我不吭声，我就溢出给你看。

最气人的是，它每次报错都告诉你行号，你一查，错在上一行。

text: 我用LaTeX写论文，写到第三年才明白，Word是所见即所得，LaTeX是所写即所祈祷。我在公式里打了个\alpha，后面跟了个空格，它直接把空格吞了，和后面的字粘成一个词，然后报错：Undefined control sequence。我查了半天才发现要写成\alpha{}。我问它为什么不提醒我，它说：这是特性。图更离谱，我明明把图放在第二页，它非要浮到第五页去。我说你给我放这儿，它说：我觉得它更适合那儿。我说我是作者，它回我一句：你是在\begin{document}前面的那个人吗？

我用Word写东西，最怕的不是写不出来，是它开始"帮我"。我打个"1."，回车，它自动给我编号成2、3、4，我还夸它智能。结果我想删掉这个编号，按Backspace，它不删编号，把我整段缩进了。我再按一下，整段又变回去了。我当时就想问它：我让你帮忙了吗？还有那个图片，我一敲字，它就往下跳，跳到第九页去了，跟个不想上班的同事一样。我说你给我回来，它弹出一句"兼容模式"。我的文档是今天刚建的啊！我最后只能把文件存成"最终版_真的最终版_这次绝对最终版.docx"，它倒是一点都不兼容我。

Graphene, you're one atom thick and still the biggest presence at every party. Scientists keep calling you the strongest material ever measured, which is wild, because you've never once held your own in a conversation. You're basically pencil lead that went to the gym and never came back. Since 2004 we've been told you'll revolutionize batteries, phones, and bridges. Meanwhile, companies slap your name on golf balls and socks like it's a free upgrade. Two Nobel-winning guys isolated you with Scotch tape, which tells you everything. The most advanced substance in the universe was found by somebody with a roll of tape and too much time. And you're still "five years away" from being useful. Honestly, that's the most relatable thing about you.
我写论文用Word，最怕的不是写不出来，是它太"热心"。我打个"一、"，回车，它自动给我编成"二、"。我删掉，它又给我加项目符号。我想去掉，它问我要不要撤销自动编号，我说要，它说好，下一行又给我编上了。我感觉不是在写字，是在跟一个实习生吵架。最绝的是目录：我改了个标题，右键"更新域"，它弹个框问我只更新页码还是整个目录。我选整个，它把我手打的标题全吃了，还一脸无辜地给我重新排版。

You're one atom thick, the only thing about you that's ever been thin. Two guys won a Nobel for peeling you off a lump of pencil lead with Scotch tape. Pencil lead! Your whole family tree is the stuff kids chew in exam halls. You're stronger than steel pound for pound, you conduct electricity, you're transparent, and you still can't get out of the lab. Every year it's "graphene will revolutionize batteries next year." That's been going on for twenty years. Meanwhile companies slap your name on tennis rackets and face cream with about as much of you as a rumor. You're basically a pencil lead that got a personal trainer and a Nobel, and you still can't get a callback from a battery company.
石墨烯这东西我真服了。它就是一层碳原子，排成蜂窝状，薄到只有一层原子那么厚。你知道铅笔芯是啥吗？石墨，一层一层叠起来的。石墨烯怎么来的？拿胶带粘在铅笔芯上，撕啊撕，撕到最后撕出一层，诺贝尔奖就这么来了。我小学也干过这事，老师没给我发奖，让我把桌子擦干净。现在商家在袜子上印"石墨烯"三个字，我寻思，你这双袜子里的碳原子，大概连一个六边形都凑不齐，它是在等你脚臭的时候自己站出来吗？

Carbon nanotubes are the most stressed-out material on Earth. They're stronger than steel, and they've been "five years from revolutionizing everything" since 1991. They're just graphene that got rolled up and never recovered. Ask one whether it's a metal or a semiconductor and it genuinely can't tell you until someone tests it. In the lab they clump together like cold spaghetti. For thirty years industry has promised them in batteries, bike frames, and space elevators. The only space elevator I've seen is the one in my dorm, and it doesn't work either. Their best feature is that under a microscope they look exactly like asbestos, which is a bold thing for a material to bring to a party.

Carbon nanotubes, you've been "five years away from changing everything" since 1991. You're stronger than steel, lighter than aluminum, and conduct electricity like a champ, which is impressive until someone asks you to leave the lab. You're a sheet of graphene that rolled itself up and called it a personality. Your big selling point is being incredibly small, and honestly, that's the only thing you've ever fit into. Every time someone tries to disperse you in a solvent, you clump together like a group project at 2 a.m. Meanwhile, the press releases keep calling you "revolutionary," and the only thing you've revolutionized is the grant budget. Stronger than steel, lighter than aluminum, and still the guest nobody's ready to invite into the real world.

石墨烯这东西我又爱又怕。你知道它多薄吗？就一层碳原子，排成六边形的蜂窝，厚度基本等于零，科学家管它叫二维材料。据说它强度是钢的两百倍，我就纳闷，这么薄，风一吹不就卷走了？结果现在什么都往上贴："石墨烯袜子""石墨烯保温杯""石墨烯面膜"。我买了双袜子，包装上写着"导热快、抗菌"。我琢磨了半天：一层碳原子铺在纤维上，你脚上那是一张平面在跟汗打架。它要真有那本事，不如去给鸡窝当网，至少网眼还能装个鸡蛋。
碳纳米管这东西，我服它，但我不太喜欢它。你知道它多细吗？一根头发丝的直径，能并排塞下几万根它。强度是钢的一百倍，密度却只有钢的六分之一，听着就是别人家的孩子。可它的脾气全看你怎么卷。同一张石墨烯纸，顺着卷就是导体，斜着卷就成了半导体。我卷个春卷都没这么讲究，卷歪一点，性格就全变了。科学家管这叫"手性"，我管这叫：全世界最有才华、也最难伺候的春卷。

Apple's Vision Pro costs $3,499, which is more than most people's first car and buys you goggles that make you look like you're about to get hypnotized at a Best Buy. The front has a screen that shows your eyeballs to everyone around you, so now you're not just wearing a computer, you're wearing one that makes eye contact with strangers. You click things by pinching the air, which is great, because you already look like you're conducting an invisible orchestra in the middle of Target. The battery lives in a puck on a cable, so you're a tethered astronaut who paid four grand to watch a movie alone in a room full of people staring at your face.

我一直不理解碳纳米管。它就是一张石墨烯卷起来，卷成了管。这画面太熟了，跟我宿舍那张瑜伽垫一个德行，卷一卷塞进箱子就能寄走。科学家说它强度是钢的几十倍，我就问：那你怎么不去修桥？结果人家跑去电池里当配角了，专门负责导电，全程没有名字，标签上印的都是"导电剂"。

最离谱的是，同样是这一张皮，卷的角度一偏，它就能变成导体，也能变成半导体。材料还是那个材料，就看你怎么卷。我们班也这样，同一届进来，有人卷得方向对，保研了；有人卷歪了，天天在宿舍当绝缘体。

Google Glass, the glasses that made everyone around you feel like they were being recorded for a documentary nobody asked for. You wore them to a dinner party and suddenly you weren't a guest, you were a surveillance operation with a nice haircut. Nobody could tell if you were looking at them or at the tiny little screen floating in your eyeball, which, let's be honest, is the exact same energy as a guy who keeps checking his phone while you're talking about your dead dog.

And that little camera! It was always pointed at people's faces like a tiny, judgmental lighthouse. People said "Glasshole" and honestly? They weren't wrong. Google spent years saying "you'll get used to it," and the public said, "We won't, but thanks for the offer."

The Apple Vision Pro costs 3,500 dollars, which is a used Honda, for a headset that makes you look like a welder who wandered into the Apple Store. The front screen shows your eyes to everyone around you, so people don't see a person. They see a dead-eyed aquarium. You click by staring at things and pinching the air, like you're trying to hypnotize your own hand. The battery lives in your pocket on a cable, so you're not free, you're tethered to a fanny pack. Apple calls it spatial computing. I call it the only device that lets you wander your living room in a 3,500-dollar blindfold and still walk straight into the couch.
我花3499美元买了台Vision Pro，戴上一称，六百多克，脑袋像顶着个烤箱上街。它最神的是眼动追踪，我看哪，哪就亮。我就瞄了一眼右上角的时间，眼睛多停了半秒，系统以为我要点它，我手指一捏，天气预报就弹出来了。更离谱的是正面那块外屏EyeSight，它把我的眼睛投在上面，别人看我，是一双亮晶晶、不太属于我的眼睛。我老婆问我在干嘛，我说在办公。她说：你现在看起来像一条戴着泳镜的鱼。

Google Glass was the only gadget that made you look like a robot and a creep at the same time. You'd walk into a bar, and before you ordered, everyone had already figured out you were filming them. "Don't worry, I'm not recording." Sure, buddy, and that's why there's a little red light blinking on your face like a smoke detector with a grudge.

And the battery! It lasted about as long as a Google product lasts before they cancel it. You'd spend the whole day with a computer on your head that could barely make it to lunch. Your own eyeballs had better uptime, and they're held together by tiny veins and spite.

Then there was the name. "Glass." Nothing says "I'm trustworthy and affordable" like a device you'd have to tape a sign to, reading "Please don't break my face."
Apple Vision Pro三千五百美元，我戴上以后学会的第一件事不是空间计算，是"盯着按钮，捏一下手指"。我看一眼，它说你点了；我真想点的是退款。外面还有块屏，能显示我的眼睛，别人跟我说话，像在跟一个眼睛发光的面罩聊天。电池用线挂在脖子上，像遛狗的绳子，续航两个小时。两小时一到，我脸上还顶着六百多克的玻璃盒子，人已经没法出门了。

Nuclear fusion is the energy source that's always thirty years away, and it has been since your grandpa was in diapers. Scientists figured out how to bottle a star. Unfortunately, the star is 150 million degrees, and it refuses to stay in the bottle. Every time the plasma touches the wall, it's like a toddler discovering the fridge is cold. The machines are shaped like donuts because nothing else can handle the pressure. We got net energy gain for a few billionths of a second, and the press release was longer than the experiment. Meanwhile, the sun does it for free, with no magnets, and it still manages to be more reliable than the people promising us a fusion plant by 2030.

Nuclear fusion, you're the energy source that's been "thirty years away" since Eisenhower. Every decade there's a press conference, and every decade it's the same promise: "Net energy gain!" for a glorious few seconds, measured very carefully, and then the lights go back to coal. You're trying to recreate the sun, which is impressive, except the sun did it for free with gravity doing all the heavy lifting. You need a doughnut-shaped magnetic bottle hotter than the sun's core, held in place by superconducting magnets that cost more than a small country. ITER was conceived in 1985 and is still "a few years out." Your whole brand is "it'll be ready next year," and somehow you've made nuclear physics sound like a guy promising to fix your sink.

谷歌眼镜我真是服了。戴上它，别人看你的眼神就一个意思：这人是不是在录我？你还没法解释，因为那个小摄像头正对着人家的脸。最绝的是那块小屏幕，悬在右眼上方，你得斜着眼睛往右上角瞟，才能看见"您有一条新消息"。整个人看起来像在努力回忆自己为什么走进这个房间。我在地铁上戴过一次，对面大叔盯了我三站，最后问："小伙子，你是在看天花板的广告吗？"我说不是，我在对空气喊"OK Glass，回复"。他那表情，好像我在跟鬼说话。

Hydrogen fuel-cell cars are the most ambitious thing ever built to avoid a charging cable. Think about it: the whole plan is to take electricity, use it to split water into hydrogen, compress that hydrogen to ten thousand PSI, drive it across the country in a tank that's basically a rocket casing, then turn it back into electricity. That's not a green car, that's a magic trick with a chaperone. And the hydrogen stations? Good luck. You'll find one in California, and it's closed for "maintenance," which I'm pretty sure means someone realized they were hydrogen stations and got nervous. Meanwhile, my Tesla just asks if I'd like to plug in at home, like a normal car.

谷歌眼镜我真是服了。一千五百美金，戴脸上，别人第一眼不看你帅不帅，看的是你右眼上方那块小屏幕。你得斜着眼看天，像在等外星人发消息。操作更绝：镜腿上一块小触摸板，你得用手指划太阳穴，划一下切菜谱，再划一下关机。出门还得对着空气喊"OK Glass"，路人以为你在跟鬼说话。最要命是那个摄像头，小灯一亮，全场都觉得自己被录进了某个不知哪天的视频。后来大家管戴它的人叫"Glasshole"，眼镜混蛋。这名字其实挺冤的，眼镜什么都没干，是戴它的人自己把自己活成了混蛋。

Hydrogen fuel-cell cars are the most optimistic thing ever built. Think about it: you take the most abundant element in the universe, and then you spend a fortune compressing it to 700 bar, bolting it into a tank, and driving it to a station that's closed. Toyota's Mirai has more hydrogen stations in its dreams than in California. Some states have exactly one, and it's always broken. You pull up, the pump says "Out of Service," and you realize you've just become a very expensive lawn ornament. Meanwhile, your electric neighbor is charging in his garage in his pajamas. Hydrogen cars are like a guy who proposes on a first date and then can't find the ring.

可控核聚变是我见过最诚实的科研项目，宣传语就一句：再等三十年。我小时候听人说三十年后有聚变电，现在我都三十多了，它还是三十年后。它每年都在进步，只是进步的方向是往后推。

原理我听懂了：太阳靠自身引力把氢压到一起融合，我们没那块头，只能把氘和氚加热到一亿度，比太阳芯部还烫好几倍。问题来了，这团火碰到容器壁就熔。于是科学家造了个甜甜圈形状的磁笼子，叫托卡马克，用磁场把火球悬在半空。人类动用上万吨磁铁，去托住一团比太阳还烫的东西，就为了烧一锅水。
我一直很想要可控核聚变。原理多浪漫：把氢挤成氦，放出能量，这就是太阳每天在干的活。问题是，太阳在天上烧得好好的，我们想在地上复刻，得先把燃料加热到上亿度，比太阳芯还烫。然后呢？没有锅能装，只能用磁场把它悬在半空，像托着一个烫手山芋，还不能碰壁，一碰就融。这哪是能源，是杂技。每年都有"重大突破"，点开一看，输进去的电比放出来的多，还是亏。科学家说再等三十年。我想问，这句话是不是七十年代就开始说了？

我有个朋友买了辆氢燃料电池车，说这是未来能源。我问他加油去哪儿，他说加氢站。我问附近有吗，他想了想说：有，就在四百公里外那个城市。

我说你这车排出来的是水，环保得很啊。他说对，我说那你开一路就是一路洒水车，还不收钱。

加氢那一下我是真服了。加氢枪往车上一怼，压力七百个大气压，跟给潜水艇打气似的。他加完手都在抖，我说你冷吗，他说不是冷，是心疼。

最让我害怕的是，他后备箱里装的是一排高压储氢罐。我就问他，你这车是跑车还是移动炸药包？他说人家叫它储能系统。我说行，那你下次停车能不能别停在加油站旁边，哦不对，你连加油站都不用去。

Esperanto was built in 1887 so everyone on Earth could finally talk to each other, and 140 years later the main conversation is still, "Oh, you speak it too? Where are you from?" "Also Esperanto." Silence. Every speaker is one hug away from running out of things to say. The grammar is famously logical: every noun ends in -o, every adjective in -a, and every direct object gets an -n, which is the only place this language ever shows emotion. It promised to be easy to learn, and it kept that promise the way a diet pill does. You master it in a month, then spend the rest of your life waiting for a stranger to answer you back.

我有个朋友买了氢燃料电池车，说这车环保，尾气只排水。我说厉害，你开车就是在给地球浇花。他说三个月后他发现，全城加氢站一共五座，两座在郊区，一座在维修，一座只给公交车加。现在他的车是油箱满的，但是没处加。这大概是全世界唯一一种"加满了也不敢出门"的车。

后来他终于排队去加氢，工作人员让他先预约。我问为什么，他说氢气要压到七十兆帕，车等于开着一个高压锅上路。我说那你不是在开车，是背着个炸药包溜达。他说没事，有安全阀。我说安全阀是给你用的，还是给路人用的？

Esperanto is the language of hope, which is a polite way of saying nobody has needed it since 1887. Dr. Zamenhof built it so everyone on Earth could talk to each other, and it worked beautifully, provided everyone was a Polish optometrist who already spoke German. Every noun ends in -o and every adjective in -a, like the language is labeling its own furniture. Then it split over a rival called Ido, because Esperantists love a universal language so much they needed a second one to be mad at. The conferences are the best part: a thousand people who learned the same made-up language, hugging in a Bulgarian youth hostel, recognizing each other by little green star pins. Then they fly home, and the nearest person they can talk to is the one who only speaks English.

世界语号称好学，我信了。规则确实少，十六条，一张纸写得下。问题是它把名词全钉在-o上，像给全世界的东西统一发了一个工牌。猫是kato，狗是hundo，连"生活"都叫vivo，我不知道该感动还是报警。最离谱的是宾格，宾语后面要加个-n，主语不加。我每次想说"我爱你"，都得先想清楚谁是宾语，感觉不是在表白，是在做语法题。发明它的柴门霍夫，想让全人类能互相理解。一百多年过去，会说的人还是那几十万，其中一半在开会，另一半在去开会的路上。

学世界语最难的不是单词，是它的"穿衣规则"。名词必须穿个O，形容词必须穿个A，副词必须穿个E。你说一句话，就像在给每个词派制服，少穿一件，老师就站你后面拿尺子敲你。动词倒是省事，不分人称，我、你、他全是一个样子，懒得有原则。宾格还要加个N，主语和宾语的位置全靠这一个字母区分，一个字母就是一个人的身份证。最离谱的是那张"相关词表"，把"谁、什么、哪里、从来、所有、没有"排成九宫格，一个词根变四种脸。我学了三个礼拜，只会说"我爱你"，还得先确认这个"你"穿没穿N。

Klingon is the only language where clearing your throat counts as a complete sentence. Its creators looked at English and said, "Too soft." So they built a tongue where every word sounds like a dog choking on a gravel driveway. Ask a Klingon for "good morning" and you'll get a cough from the sewer, followed by a threat about your mother's forehead. The apostrophes are everywhere, like someone sneezed punctuation across the page. Qapla'! Qapla'? Qapla'. Half the vocabulary is for dishonor and the other half is for knives. Fans spent decades memorizing it, which tells you they really wanted to be insulted with conviction. Even the Duolingo owl looks nervous when it comes up.

我学了三个月克林贡语，终于能跟人打招呼了。结果一开口，对方说："你想要什么？"我一查，"nuqneH"就是这个意思。我以为是"你好"，人家以为我在找碴。

这语言的语法也怪。宾语先上台，动词跟在后面，主语最后才出场。我平时说话习惯先铺垫，它连铺垫的机会都不给我。还有那些辅音，全是从嗓子眼里刮出来的。我练了一周，邻居以为我在吐痰，敲门来问我是不是需要医生。

Klingon, you sound like a man hacking up a hairball during a hostage negotiation. Every word starts with a throat-clearing gargle, and somehow "nuqneH" still sounds like a threat. Apparently "please" is a sign of weakness, so you just bellow "Qapla'" and hope the guy behind you agrees. Your grammar treats every sentence like a dare: object first, verb second, subject whenever you feel like it. Your big literary achievement is *Hamlet*, and its most famous line comes out as "taH pagh taHbe'," which sounds like a dog choking on a sock. Your dictionary has more ways to say "your mother" than "I'm sorry," and I'd respect you more if you apologized once.

我学克林贡语学了三个月，最大的收获是：克林贡人吵架不用脏话，他们的词典本身就是脏话库。你跟克林贡人打招呼，他张嘴就是"nuqneH"，翻译过来是"你要什么"。不是"你好"，是"你要什么"。我每次进门都像去土匪窝抢东西。还有"Qapla'"，意思是"成功"，我考完试喊了一声，监考老师以为我在咳嗽。最离谱的是语法，它是宾语在前、动词在中间、主语最后。我想说"我吃饭"，得先说"饭吃我"。这哪是语言，这分明是一个被吃掉的人在做遗言。

You scrolled past every font on that dropdown menu, past the ones built for hospitals, courts, and airports, and picked the one designed for a cartoon dog's speech bubbles. Congratulations. Your notice about the mandatory layoffs is now technically being narrated by Rover from Microsoft Bob.

I know what you were after. You wanted to seem approachable. You're the office manager who says "no worries!" while ruining someone's Friday. You wanted the boil-water advisory to feel like a hug. Instead, your tenants read it in the voice of a birthday clown and assumed the water was fine and the clown was just excited.

Here's what it got you: a screenshot on Reddit, a group chat full of strangers, and a legal department that now reads your memos aloud to each other for fun.

The pet had a better career than the font you chose to speak for it.

You're the office manager who wrote "Parking permits will now be enforced" and thought, this needs to feel like a hug. You wanted approachable. You wanted everyone to know you're not a monster, you're Deb, you bring bundt cake. And it worked! Nobody's afraid of you. Nobody's afraid of the notice either.

The landlord who slides "Rent is 30 days late" under the door in Comic Sans isn't collecting rent. He's opening negotiations. The HR rep announcing layoffs in it isn't softening the blow, she's making a grown man feel like he got fired by the cartoon dog from Microsoft Bob. And the HOA president threatening fines over bin placement? Congratulations, you've made a tyrant look like a substitute teacher on movie day.

You wanted warmth and authority and picked the one choice that guarantees neither. CERN did it for the Higgs boson and still hasn't lived it down, and they had a particle going for them. You've got a fish-in-the-microwave memo.

You had every font in the world available, and you picked the one that says "authentic" the way a gift shop pyramid says "Egypt." You wanted ancient wisdom. You got a sign that tells customers your hot stone massage was learned from a video.

You're the owner who said "my nephew says it looks organic" and considered that a design process. You're the guy whose "Mediterranean-inspired" menu includes a wrap. You wanted to be exotic, and you ended up in the same category as a quarter-billion-dollar blockbuster that got publicly roasted on SNL by Ryan Gosling, who played a man in actual tears over this exact decision.

Everyone else in your strip mall hired a designer. You hired a feeling. Your five-star review says "clean," which is what people write when they're being kind about the sign.

我们公司人事上周发裁员通知，用的Comic Sans。我问为什么，她说：“想柔和一点，减少冲击。”

姐姐，这字体当年是给微软一只叫Rover的卡通狗设计的，专门用来写对话气泡。你这是让一条狗通知我下岗。

结果呢？“因业务调整，您的岗位将被取消”，每个字都圆滚滚、歪歪扭扭，读起来就是“汪！你被开除啦～”

冲击确实没有，因为根本没人信。有个哥们儿回复了一串“哈哈哈”，周一照常来上班，被保安拦在门口，还委屈：“你们那个通知不是在搞笑吗？”

最惨的是人事自己，月底被优化了，通知也是Comic Sans。她盯着屏幕看了十分钟，说：“这肯定是恶作剧。”

行，你的柔和，终于轮到你自己了。

You opened a "Himalayan salt cave and wellness sanctuary" with a small-business loan and a dropdown menu. Around 11 p.m., exhausted, you scrolled past the fonts that cost money and landed on the one that whispers "ancient healing" to everyone, including your nephew, who "does graphics" and approved it.

You wanted timeless. You got the exact look of every other spa, the falafel place two doors down, and a yoga studio run by a guy named Dave who says "namaste" like a threat.

Somewhere, Ryan Gosling is staring at your awning with the same haunted silence he gave the Avatar title, and he's right. You didn't build a brand. You built a $14 "Pharaoh's Bowl" for people who think Epcot counts as a passport, and you told yourself it was authentic.

每个公司都有这么一位行政，觉得通知太严肃，大家会有压力，于是打开Word，把字体改成Comic Sans。图什么？图亲切，图“有温度”。

结果上周公司发通知：“因业务调整，将优化百分之三十人员。”Comic Sans。全办公室第一反应：哟，团建？还有人回了句“收到，开心”。

你知道这字体当初是给谁做的吗？一只卡通狗，专门给它的对话气泡用的。你拿一只狗的字体宣布裁员，狗看了都觉得不妥。

最后，这位行政自己也在名单里。他去找HR，说能不能给我开个正式点的离职证明，宋体的。HR说：不用，已经打好了，Comic Sans，右下角还有个笑脸。

他说：这笑脸不是我加的。

HR说：对，是你上次培训时教我的。

You write PHP for a living, which means you've said "modern PHP is actually really good" more often than you've said "I love you," and you meant it less. You've been announcing the comeback since 2012, like a guy outside a bar insisting his ex is about to call.

Your dream is a Laravel job at a real company. Your reality is a client named Brenda who wants the contact form to "pop." You tell people PHP runs most of the web as if the web sent a thank-you card. Your deploy process is dragging a folder into FileZilla, and your staging environment is Brenda's other site.

Every January, a blog declares PHP dead, and you feel something. It's the closest anyone has come to checking on you.

开养生馆的老板选招牌字体，预算四百，又想显得有五千年底蕴，于是选了Papyrus，就是那个边儿像被猫挠过、笔画细得像没吃饱的字。他的逻辑是：这字一看就古埃及，古埃及一看就神秘，神秘就能卖六百八的艾灸套餐。我说艾灸是中国的，跟尼罗河有什么关系？他说：“反正是古的。”

结果隔壁新开了家埃及烤肉店，也用Papyrus。两块招牌并排一挂，顾客全懵了：有人进养生馆问有没有鹰嘴豆泥，有人进烤肉店问能不能刮痧。设计师路过也不进门，就站门口拍照发朋友圈，配三个字：“又一个。”

老板花四百块，买了个跟《阿凡达》同款的“独一无二”。

You've said "PHP isn't what it used to be" so often it's basically your LinkedIn headline. Nobody asked. You bring up Facebook at parties like it's your cousin's startup. You switched to Laravel and call it a fresh start, which is a man putting a tuxedo on a Honda to prove he's going places.

What are you after? Respect. What do you get? A client named Brenda who wants her WordPress site "just a little different" and pays by Venmo, sometimes.

You tell recruiters "we're on PHP 8," meaning staging is. Production is a file called final_v2_REAL.php, with a comment from a guy who quit in 2014: "don't touch."

You've been meaning to learn Go since 2019. Your fear isn't that PHP will die. It's that it never will, and neither will your on-call rotation.

我们这条街，艾灸馆、素食馆、足疗店，招牌全是Papyrus，就是那种笔画毛毛糙糙、像拿烧焦的树枝在牛皮纸上划出来的字体。

老板们图什么？图"古法""天然""千年底蕴"。设计师报价三千，他一想：Word里自带的，免费，还自带古埃及气质，血赚。

可《阿凡达》砸了二十多亿美元，片名用的就是Papyrus，被全世界笑了十几年。你一个六十平的刮痧店，凭什么觉得自己扛得住？

现在客人走到门口，抬头一看"古法艾灸"，字还带着焦边，真不知道是进去放松，还是进去防腐。

最惨的是素食馆老板，招牌、菜单、外卖袋全是Papyrus，一份麻婆豆腐，看着像刚从墓里刨出来的。他还纳闷生意怎么越来越淡。兄弟，你卖的是出土文物。

写PHP的人，我一直很佩服。这门语言每个变量前面都要加个美元符号：$name、$age、$salary。写了十年，满屏都是$，工资卡里一个都没见着。

他们当初为什么入行？因为好上手。培训班三个月，出来就接单，接的全是老板表弟的商城、装修公司的官网。入行时都背过那句"PHP是世界上最好的语言"，十年过去，这话喊得最响的，永远是正在改前任祖传代码的人。

下场更惨。每年都有人宣布PHP死了，他们不反驳，因为手上那个WordPress插件，作者三年前就跑路了。面试官问："你还在写PHP啊？"他们只能说："我们现在升到8了，支持类型了。"

这就像有人说：我家一直漏雨，但是现在，我们有伞了。

写PHP的人，都是被"好找活"骗进来的。全世界四成网站是WordPress，意味着永远有活。就像殡仪馆，永远有生意，但没人羡慕。

入行第一天，每个变量前面都得带个美元符号。你以为是兆头，结果是嘲讽：满屏的$，一分不进兜。

接手的全是前任留下的，一个文件三千行，HTML里插SQL，SQL里插HTML，中间一行注释："别动，会炸。"写注释的人早跑了，你接手的不是项目，是文物，还得原地保护。

每年还有人宣布"PHP已死"，他们都练出来了，一边点头一边给来宾递茶。

最惨的是记函数。in_array先写要找的针，strpos先写草堆。干了十年，每次还得去查文档。

别人的职业生涯叫积累，PHP程序员的叫：十年了，我还在大海里捞针，而且先放哪个，我还得查。

You wrote your backend in JavaScript, your frontend in JavaScript, your build scripts in JavaScript, and your smart fridge dashboard in JavaScript, and you call it "full-stack" because "only-stack" sounds like a cry for help. You said you wanted to avoid context switching. Congratulations: you now switch between four frameworks that all launched this quarter.

You're not a polyglot. You're someone who learned one language and renamed every problem until it fit.

What did it get you? A node_modules folder heavier than your product, a notepad app that ships its own browser and eats two gigs of RAM, and a TypeScript migration to apologize for the original decision. Your Hello World has 1,400 dependencies, one of them maintained by a guy who once deleted eleven lines and broke the internet.

But you're hireable. Every posting wants you. That's not a career, that's a hostage situation with stock options.

You heard "full-stack" and decided it meant one hammer and a stack of whatever you're hitting. You wrote the backend in JavaScript to avoid context-switching, which is adorable, because you've switched frameworks four times since March. Your Electron app uses 900 megabytes of RAM to show a to-do list, and you call that "cross-platform" the way a man towing a boat calls it "a sports package."

What are you after? Hireability, and the warm feeling that every job posting has your name on it. What do you get? A node_modules folder heavier than your personality, a loyalty to a package called is-odd that you'd defend in court, and a weekend "migration to TypeScript" that you'll describe as "mostly done" until you retire.

You didn't pick one language to rule them all. You just refuse to learn a second one and gave it a LinkedIn headline.

You're the person who says "it's a classic" about a process you inherited from a postdoc who left in 2009. Your lab notebook is just a bottle of 950K with someone else's handwriting on it. You say ZEP is "too finicky" while spending nine hours writing a 200 µm array because you chose a dose that could cook an egg.

You say you want 10 nm resolution, but your liftoff has the edge profile of a torn receipt, and you've been "optimizing the bilayer" since your qualifying exam. You treat MIBK:IPA 1:3 like a family recipe and cold development like a personality.

Meanwhile the group next door switched resists, graduated, bought houses, and now send you LinkedIn requests. You stay loyal. Loyalty is great. It's just that your beam time costs more than their weddings.

我同事学了三个月 JavaScript，现在看什么都像 JS。前两天他说要做个记事本，用 Electron。我说记事本？他说对，打出来 300 兆，因为里面自带一个 Chrome。我说你一个记事本为啥要带浏览器？他说：“我不想学第二门语言。”兄弟，你省的是学习时间，吃的是我的内存。

他连判断奇偶数都不自己写，npm install is-even。装完 node_modules 两个G，他自己的代码三行。

我考他："1"+1 等于几？他说 11。"1"-1 呢？0。我说你就这么接受了？他说：“习惯了。”

各位，这不是程序员，这是被 JavaScript 虐出斯德哥尔摩综合征的人。

现在有一种人，什么都要拿 JavaScript 写。网页写完写后端，后端写完写桌面软件，现在在研究拿它控制烤箱。你问他图啥，他说："我不想再学一门新语言。"

兄弟，你为了不学一门语言，每周都在学一个新框架。

他写的记事本用 Electron，打开占八百兆内存。因为里面塞了一整个浏览器，就为了让你输入"买菜"两个字。

他还跟你解释："1"加 1 等于 11，"1"减 1 等于 0，这叫灵活。灵活到最后，项目源码三千行，node_modules 两个 G。

上线那天报错：undefined is not a function。他盯着屏幕，一脸茫然："到底是谁 undefined 了？"

我觉得是他的职业规划。

Oh, you're still on PMMA. Let me guess: your advisor's thesis used it, your advisor's advisor used it, and somewhere on the group drive is a recipe called "DO NOT CHANGE," last edited by a postdoc who now sells insurance in Ohio.

You call it "reliable." You've run the same dose test eleven times because you refuse to admit the variable is you. Your big optimization this year was going from 950 A4 to 950 A3 and calling it a paper.

You queue a pattern Friday night, check on it Sunday, and tell people the beam is "just taking its time." Then you say you don't trust anything without forty years of citations, which is also how you feel about your dentist and your Windows XP tool PC.

What does it get you? Gorgeous 10-nm lines, a lift-off you pray over, and no social life. The chip is perfect. Your weekend is exposed and overdeveloped.

"We're switching to HSQ for the resolution." Sure you are. Because your PMMA wasn't humiliating enough, you wanted a resist that's also a deadline. You're chasing sub-10 nanometer lines so you can put one SEM image in a paper, the one nice picture out of forty-one fallen-over grating samples.

Your resist lives in the freezer like a tiny, expensive yogurt, and by the time you've booked the beam it has gone off anyway. You'll expose at a dose that makes the e-beam tool bill you like a hotel minibar. Then you'll develop in salt water, because apparently you wanted to cook pasta in the cleanroom.

And what do you get? Silicon dioxide you can't strip. A permanent souvenir of your ambition, fused to the wafer forever. Congratulations, you made glass lines. Your advisor wanted devices.

做电子束的人，你得理解，他们是一群对新材料过敏的人。你问为什么还在用PMMA，他一脸骄傲：“分辨率高，十纳米以下！”

对，这玩意儿六十年代的，跟你家鱼缸、亚克力牙托是亲戚。他们拿牙托在刻十纳米。

图什么？图稳。师兄留下的配方：950K，A4，4000转，180度烘三分钟，MIBK兑IPA一比三显影。没人知道为什么，但谁改谁延毕。

下场呢？曝光剂量几百微库每平方厘米，一个图案写一晚上。第二天一看，束漂了，套刻对不上。好不容易写完去刻蚀，PMMA一见等离子体就没了，像纸糊的盾牌。

最后博士五年读六年，论文里还得写：“PMMA以高分辨率著称。”

是啊，胶是分辨率高、灵敏度低，人也是。对新材料，毫无反应。

干电子束光刻还在用 PMMA 的，基本都是博士生。图什么？图一句“PMMA 分辨率高，业内金标准”。金标准，对，这玩意儿跟你家鱼缸的亚克力、牙医给你做的牙托是一个东西。人家做牙托的，做完下班回家吃饭。咱们呢，拿它刻十纳米，电子枪在里面扫一整夜，剂量大得像给它做理疗，早上进实验室，机器还在写，你俩互相看着，谁也不好意思先走。

好不容易写完了，MIBK 加 IPA 一泡，线条漂亮。结果一刻蚀，胶比我工资涨得还慢，消失得比导师的承诺还快。

师弟问：“师兄，为什么不换个胶？”

我说：“导师说，当年师兄就是用 950K 毕业的。”

师兄毕业了，我还守着一块有机玻璃，等它给我一个答辩。

You switched to HSQ for the resolution. Of course you did. PMMA gave you 20-nanometer lines, which is fine for science but not for the cover of a journal your advisor brings up at dinner parties. Now you're writing 8-nanometer lines that nobody can see without a $2 million microscope you booked three weeks ago.

You pay triple for a tiny bottle that expires faster than your funding. You keep it cold like insulin and spin it knowing it's already going bad. Your dose is ten times higher, so your "quick write" runs overnight, and the e-beam tool manager who used to love you is now drafting an email. You develop in TMAH like you're brewing something, and the lines collapse anyway.

And the best part: it never comes off. You wanted resolution, and you got permanent glass sitting on your device. Congratulations, you made something incredibly small that doesn't work.

You told the new intern you use Vim before you told him your name. He just wanted to know where the printer was.

You say you never leave the home row. Correct. You never leave the house either.

You spent forty hours on your .vimrc to save eleven seconds a day, so you break even in 2031, assuming you don't switch to Neovim, which you will, and then announce it like a religious conversion.

You're not after speed. You're after the moment someone glances at your screen and asks, "How do you even quit that?" so you can say "Oh, it's simple" and type something that looks like a ransom note: `:wqa!`

What does it get you? A macro that renames forty variables, a pinky built like a bodybuilder's, and one guy at a meetup who nods at you with exactly your kind of loneliness.

You told the intern you use Vim before you told him your name. He didn't ask. Nobody asked. You just stood near a monitor and the urge took you.

You're not after efficiency. You're after a witness. You spent forty hours on your .vimrc to save eleven seconds a week, and the only payoff is someone watching you type "ciw" and gasping. They don't gasp. They say, "Is it frozen?"

And what has it gotten you? A pair-programming partner who stopped pairing. A relative line number column you explain unprompted. A macro you recorded once, for a task you'll never repeat, that you still bring up at parties.

You say you never leave the home row. Buddy, you never leave the house either, but at least that one isn't a personality.

Meanwhile Dave opened a file, changed a word with his mouse, and went to lunch.

做纳米加工的博士生都有一个信仰：PMMA 分辨率不够，换 HSQ。换完你才发现，这不是换胶，是领养了一个早产儿。

它得在冰箱里供着，用之前先回温，像伺候祖宗。旋完胶它就开始老化，你俩的关系是"每天都不一样"。显影用 25% 的 TMAH，有人为了对比度还往里加盐。头一回听说做精密加工往显影液里放盐的，厨子都没这么讲究。

灵敏度还低，电子束机排队三个星期，一个小图案写一整晚。好不容易写出 8 纳米的线，一显影，塌了，粘一块儿，跟煮过头的面一样。

就算没塌，HSQ 曝光完变成二氧化硅，洗不掉，永远留在你的器件上。你图啥？图论文里一张 SEM 图。导师看完说："挺好，再做个大面积的。"

有人为了分辨率，把 PMMA 换成 HSQ。我就想问，你图啥？PMMA 便宜、好剥离、导师不骂你。HSQ 呢？得放冰箱，一开瓶就倒计时，跟生鲜外卖一个待遇。剂量要几千，写一小块图形，电子束扫一整夜，你在机房陪着，比陪对象都久。早上显影，一根 8 纳米的线，倒了，跟隔壁那根粘一块了。再来一轮，终于立住了，你想把多余的去掉？不好意思，曝光完它就是二氧化硅，想洗掉得上氢氟酸，连你的器件一块洗。最后论文里写“sub-10 nm”，那是三十张电镜图里挑出来的那一张，剩下二十九张，叫 preliminary data。

公司里总有一个用 Vim 的人，你不用问，他自己会说。入职第一天就官宣："我不用鼠标。"没人问啊，我问的是厕所在哪。

他图什么？图你从背后路过，看他光标嗖嗖飞三屏，你"哇"一声。就这一声，够他吃一个月。

下场呢？.vimrc 调了六百行，花了三个周末，省下的时间还没调的时间多。最惨是帮你改代码，你电脑上开的是 VS Code，他自信满满先按 Esc，再敲 :wq，保存退出，一气呵成。结果文档里多出一行 :wq，像他的墓志铭。

他还不认，说："你这编辑器，不行。"

咱公司有个哥们，从不说"我在写代码"，他说"我在用 Vim 写代码"。重点不是写，是 Vim。

他图啥？图你路过他工位，看见他手指在键盘上弹钢琴，嘴里念着 hjkl hjkl，像在做法。你问他干嘛，他说"移动光标"。移一格十分钟，但"不用离开主键区"。省下摸方向键的半秒，代价是 .vimrc 调了三年。

下场呢？有天重装系统，.vimrc 没备份。他对着裸奔的 Vim，像被扒了铠甲的骑士。第二天，他偷偷装了 VS Code，再装个 Vim 插件。

现在他是：用 VS Code 假装用 Vim，还得让所有人知道。

You people don't use a text editor. You adopted a pet that you have to feed Lisp.

You open Emacs to write one email, and three weeks later you've written a mail client, but you still haven't sent the email. Your init file is 4,000 lines long, and you understand maybe nine of them. The rest is a Stack Overflow answer from 2011 that you're afraid to remove.

You've got an Org-mode agenda so elaborate it has its own org chart. It tracks every task you'll never do, in beautiful nested bullets. You don't have a to-do list. You have a to-do *liturgy*.

And the pinky! Thirty years of Control and your left hand looks like a lobster claw. You call it "ergonomic." Your chiropractor calls it "a recurring client."

You say it's an operating system. Sir, it's a hobby with a splash screen.

You've lived in Emacs for eleven years and written four thousand lines of config and zero lines of the novel your Org-mode agenda says you're "drafting." You don't edit text, you tend an init.el that collapses every time a package updates. You read email in it, browse Reddit in it, and tell people at parties you "just haven't needed to leave." Nobody asked where you've been.

Your left pinky is a war veteran. You remapped Caps Lock to Control, and your therapist to M-x doctor. You installed evil-mode so you could escape Emacs keybindings, then defended Emacs keybindings in the comments. You spent a Saturday writing Lisp to automate a ten-second task, break-even in 2031, then published a blog post about it for the four other people who have the same blog post.

Your whole personality is a tool that does everything except make you look up from it. Stallman would be proud. That's the problem.

You run a 40-million-dollar company on a file called "Final_v7_REAL_use-this-one." You're not a CEO. You're a hostage negotiator for a spreadsheet.

You say you're "scrappy." No. You're a guy who refuses to pay for software but will happily pay Brenda eleven hours a week to color cells yellow. Yellow means pending. Light yellow means pending but emotionally.

Your entire infrastructure is a macro written by Dave, who left in 2016, and nobody knows where Dave went. You light a candle for Dave. You're afraid to scroll past column AZ because that's where Dave's curse lives.

You wanted control. You got a file locked for editing by "Karen," who's on vacation in Portugal.

And every quarter, your VLOOKUP returns #N/A, and you stare at it like it's a diagnosis you're choosing to ignore.

You don't run a company on Excel. You run it on Dave. Dave built the macro in 2014, Dave left in 2017, and now you pray to a button labeled "DO NOT CLICK."

You tell investors you're "data-driven." You're data-hostage. Your inventory system is a file called Final_v7_REAL_USE_THIS_ONE, and it's locked because Karen opened it at lunch and went on vacation.

You said you didn't want to pay for software. Congratulations, you've paid for it in nine hours a week of someone typing "VLOOKUP" with the face of a hostage reading a statement.

Your ops manager is proud of having forty-seven tabs. That's not a business model, that's a hoarder's garage with a color-coding system.

And every quarter, one cell says #REF!, and the whole leadership team stares at it like it's a diagnosis.

我认识一个把Emacs当操作系统的哥们。他用Emacs收邮件、看新闻、听歌、管日程。我问：“那你干嘛不直接装个操作系统？”他推了推眼镜：“Emacs就缺一个好编辑器。”说完笑得特别得意，那种全世界只有我懂的得意。

他的待办用Org-mode管，第一条是“优化Org-mode配置”，已经挂了三年。init.el写了八千行，比他这辈子写过的业务代码都长。启动一次要四十七秒，所以他从不关，上次重启是因为搬家断电。

小指因为按Ctrl已经变形了，医生问怎么弄的，他说“写东西”。女朋友说出来吃个饭，他说等我写个函数。函数写好了，女朋友没了。

现在他唯一的倾诉对象是M-x doctor，一个七十年代的假心理医生。他说我好孤独，它说：“你为什么这么说？”

他说，这是他用过最懂他的软件。

我有个朋友，把 Emacs 当操作系统用。邮件在里面收，网页在里面看，连聊天都在里面聊。我问他图啥，他说：“不用切窗口，专注。”专注？他的 init.el 五千行，每个周末固定修配置，修的是上周为了省事写的配置。最绝的是，他最后装了 evil-mode，就是在 Emacs 里模拟 Vim 的按键。折腾十年，把全世界装进 Emacs，最后为了好用，把宿敌请了回来。现在他小指已经废了，他管这叫“Emacs 小指”，语气跟领了勋章似的。我说哥们，你这不是在用操作系统，是在给操作系统打工，还是不发工资的那种。

有种老板，用 Excel 管整个公司。图什么？图省钱，还觉得自己特别“数据驱动”。结果公司里权力最大的不是他，是“表哥”，全公司唯一看得懂那张表的人。表里 VLOOKUP 套了七层，没人敢动，谁动谁 #REF!。发工资那天，财务像拆炸弹。员工身份证号被自动变成 1.23E+17，十八位全军覆没。想打开文件，弹窗说：“已被张三锁定”。张三在三亚休年假。最后表哥一跳槽，老板才明白：自己不是在管公司，是在给一个人打工。而那个人，把工作表保护密码带走了。

You're not a manager, you're a guy who got comfortable with IMPORTRANGE and mistook it for leadership. You said "we don't need Jira, a sheet works fine," and now you have eleven tabs, three named "Final," and one called "Copy of Final (Dave's)."

What are you after? Control, disguised as transparency. You want everyone to see everything, as long as only you understand the formulas. Your team doesn't update the sheet. They open it, spot an anonymous capybara hovering over cell F14, and quietly leave.

What does it get you? A color-coding system only you can decode, a Status column that has said "In progress" since March, and the rush of a stakeholder clicking "Request edit access," the closest you'll ever come to being feared.

Meanwhile, Version History knows who broke it. You know it too. You just won't say.

You're not a manager, you're a guy who discovered conditional formatting and mistook it for leadership. You call it "our single source of truth," which is adorable, because there are nine tabs, and three of them are named "Copy of Q3 (DO NOT USE)."

One IMPORTRANGE holds your entire department together, and you're the only one who knows. When it breaks, "Loading..." becomes your team's mission statement.

You wanted visibility, and you got it: an anonymous capybara hovering over your cell while someone you hired quietly overwrites your formula with a hardcoded 47. You wanted accountability, so you @-tagged Greg in a comment eleven times. Greg has never opened a comment. Greg's row is yellow. Yellow means something. Nobody remembers what.

You say you'll "move to a real tool next quarter" while building a dropdown menu like it's a cathedral.

Your career highlight is a pivot table. Your legacy is "Request edit access."

见过拿Excel管整家公司的老板。问他怎么不上个系统，他说："Excel挺好用的。"是挺好用，好用到库存、工资、客户全塞一张表里，VLOOKUP嵌了七层。这哪是做表，这是写遗嘱。

图什么？图不用学新东西。结果为了不学新东西，公司专门养了个人来学这张表。刘姐，没职位，大家只说"问刘姐"。她请一天假，公司就瘫了，因为只有她知道D列不能动，一动，#REF!就像瘟疫一样往下传。

下场更惨。上周我想打开订单表，弹窗："文件正在被张伟使用。"张伟三年前就离职了。现在公司发工资，得等一个幽灵把文件保存关掉。

You installed Vista on launch day. Nobody needed you to. You just wanted to be the guy at the office who says "oh, you're still on XP?" in the voice of someone judging a flip phone.

You were after transparent window borders. You spent three hundred dollars on the upgrade, then another eighty on RAM, so your title bars could be see-through. Your computer now has the glass look of a luxury hotel and the speed of its elevator.

Day one got you a printer with a driver that was "coming soon," and a sticker on your laptop that said "Vista Capable," which turned out to be a legal term. You clicked Allow so many times your finger filed for workers' comp. You plugged in a flash drive to make it faster, and called it ReadyBoost like that's a normal sentence.

By March you were hunting for your old XP disc, and it was waiting for you, no hard feelings.

我特别佩服那种用Google Sheets管团队的领导。他们的口头禅是：“不用买系统，一个表格就够了。”省了一年三千块软件费，代价是自己变成全公司的人肉服务器。

刚开始就一个标签页，三个月后四十七个，名字叫“总表”“总表2”“总表最终”“总表最终（别动）”。他还觉得自己是工程师，因为他会VLOOKUP。全组只有他会，别人看见公式栏，就像看见祖传药方。

最离谱是开会。他共享屏幕，右上角蹦出个“匿名水豚正在查看”。全场安静，没人知道谁是水豚，只知道水豚刚把C列改成了红色。

他请一天假，团队就瘫痪了，因为没人知道红色是“已完成”，还是“老板生气了”。

后来他离职，交接文档就一句话：“有问题，看版本历史。”

Congratulations to everyone who installed Vista on launch day. You read "wait for Service Pack 1" and thought, "That's advice for people with something to lose." You bought a new graphics card just to make your windows see-through. Finally, your windows are as transparent as your reasons.

Now your printer is a paperweight, your scanner is a rumor, and the driver is "coming soon" from a company whose website still says 2004. Every click triggers a box asking if you meant it. You've said yes forty times today. You're not secure, you're just trained.

But you'll tell coworkers it's "actually smooth once you turn a few things off." Sir, you paid four hundred dollars to turn things off. Meanwhile Dave, on XP, finished his spreadsheet and went home.

第一天就升级 Vista 的人，我研究过，都是那种等不及第一个补丁的人。他们图什么？图那个毛玻璃窗口。Aero，半透明的，能隐约看到后面的桌面，就像前任的 QQ 空间，什么都看不清，但就是忍不住盯着。

结果装完发现：打印机没驱动，声卡没驱动，连他那个二手摄像头也认不出他了。电脑配置 1G 内存，风扇转得像要起飞，机身还贴着“Vista Ready”的贴纸，Ready 的是风扇。

最惨的是那个弹窗：“Windows 需要您的许可才能继续。”他想删个文件，系统问他：“你确定吗？”他点“允许”。系统又问：“你真的确定吗？”他再点“允许”。这哪是操作系统，这是我妈。

三天后，他的 MSN 签名改了：“Vista 用户，求 XP 安装盘，在线等，挺急的。”

每个团队都有这么一个人，说：“不用买Jira，太重了，我拿Google Sheets搞一下就行。”他不是图省钱，是图全公司只有他看得懂第七个标签页。

三个月后，表里十四个标签页，条件格式红黄绿：红是延期，黄是风险，绿是“没人来骂我”。有个标签页叫“勿动”，全组都动过。

直到有天，同事只选了B列，点了“A到Z排序”。从此任务和负责人各过各的，张三在干李四的活，李四在给一个叫“待定”的人打下手。

最后他休年假，全组停摆，因为只有他知道IMPORTRANGE为什么报#REF!。他离职那天，交接文档就一个链接，点开写着“需要访问权限”，申请已自动发送给：他的个人邮箱。

第一天就升级Vista的人，你们公司肯定有一个，就是那个说“我对电脑懂一点”的。

他图什么？图毛玻璃。Aero，窗口是半透明的，他觉得自己电脑一下子有钱了。结果他那台机器贴着“Vista Capable”的贴纸，意思是“能运行Vista”，但只能运行没有毛玻璃的Vista。花钱升级，就为了得到一个不透明的窗口。

然后是UAC。他点一下，弹窗：“是否允许？”允许。又弹：“您确定吗？”确定。一天里被问“确定”的次数，比他求婚还多。

打印机没驱动，声卡没驱动，最后他默默把XP装回去。同事问：“怎么样？”

他说：“挺好，我体验了一下，什么叫花钱买降级。”

Who puts Windows 8 on a desktop? You. You looked at a perfectly working Windows 7 machine and said, "What this needs is a touchscreen experience, and I don't own a touchscreen."

So now you sit at a 27-inch monitor, flinging your mouse into corners like a man hunting for a light switch in a stranger's house. You've Googled "how to shut down" at eleven at night. Your wife watched.

You wanted the future. You got a full-screen weather app you can't close and a Mail tile that's been "Getting things ready" since August.

Eventually you downloaded a program to bring the Start button back, so you paid to get Windows 7 with extra steps.

And sometimes you still tap the screen. It's not a touchscreen. Those fingerprints are just hope.

You put Windows 8 on a desktop. A tower. Under a desk. With a mouse. Nobody in your house has ever touched that monitor except to wipe it, yet there you are, dragging your cursor into the top-right corner like a man feeling for a light switch in a stranger's house.

You wanted to be early to the future. Instead you got a full-screen weather report you never requested and a ten-minute hunt for the shutdown button, which you finally found by Googling it on your phone, like someone searching for the exit in a building they own.

Then you downloaded a third-party Start menu, so now you've spent a weekend undoing the upgrade you chose on purpose.

And when your friends ask how it is, you say, "It's fine once you get used to it." That's also what hostages say.

给台式机装Windows 8的人，我特别好奇你图什么。图新鲜。结果开机，满屏彩色方块，我就想打开个文件夹，它给我弹出个"体育"。

关机更绝。台式机，没有开始按钮，你得把鼠标甩到屏幕右下角，等侧边栏像幽灵一样滑出来，点设置，再点电源。我第一次关机找了十分钟，我怀疑这是微软的智力测试。

而且这帮人的显示器根本不是触屏，可Windows 8整套设计就是让你拿手指划。所以你会看到一个成年人，坐在台式机前，手指悬在半空，犹豫要不要戳。

最后下场都一样：第二天下载Classic Shell，把开始菜单请回来。花钱升级，就为了把它打扮成Windows 7。这不叫升级，这叫花钱请个演员，去演你的前任。

Ordering Hawaiian pizza is a cry for help from someone who wants to be called a rebel. You've never been to Hawaii. The dish is from Ontario. You're defending a Canadian restaurant accident like it's your homeland.

You order it for the office party, then wait for someone to gasp. Nobody does, so you announce, "I know, I know, pineapple doesn't belong on pizza," to a room that wasn't talking. You've been waiting years for this fight. Nobody's coming.

You call yourself adventurous. It's the only risk you've ever taken, and you retake it every Friday. Your entire personality is a defense of a topping that never hired a lawyer.

And what do you get? Three leftover slices, because everyone else quietly ordered pepperoni, and a reputation as the "random" one at work. You wanted to be dangerous. You're just Greg, with ham.

给台式机装Windows 8的人，我太了解了。这种人，朋友聚会必说一句："我这个是尝鲜。"尝鲜，你家台式机是个五斤重的铁箱子，插着鼠标键盘，哪来的"鲜"？

图什么呢？图开机快，四秒。是，四秒就进去了，进去以后花四十分钟找关机。

开始按钮没了，换成一整屏磁贴，天气、股票、应用商店，全对着你闪。他们对着显示器伸手去戳，显示器说："大哥，我不是触屏。"

关机更绝。鼠标得甩到右上角，等超级按钮栏冒出来，点设置，点电源，才能关。关个机像密室逃脱。

下场呢？他们最后都去搜"Windows 8 怎么把开始菜单弄回来"，下载个第三方软件，把微软删掉的东西，亲手装回去。

等到8.1出了，开始按钮回来了，他们热泪盈眶，一点：跳到磁贴屏。

那不是按钮，那是个门铃，按了还是那帮磁贴来开门。

You order Hawaiian pizza the way a man buys a motorcycle at forty-five: you need everyone to know you're dangerous. Nobody asked. You say "I know, I know, don't judge me" to a room that wasn't judging you, and now it is. That's the plan. It's the only controversy you can afford. You'll never skydive, never quit the job, never tell the group chat what you actually think, but you will die on this hill, and the hill is a Friday night in your own kitchen.

You think you're ordering a tropical getaway. It was invented in Ontario in 1962 by a Greek guy running a restaurant called the Satellite. You're not on vacation. You're the loyal defender of a Canadian accident.

You wanted to be a maverick. You got a twenty-minute argument with your brother-in-law and a second pizza, pepperoni, that someone quietly ordered to cover for you.

每桌聚餐总有那么一个人，菜单翻到最后一页，清清嗓子：“要不……来个夏威夷？”

这人图什么？图个性。他觉得自己在叛逆：“我不走寻常路。”兄弟，夏威夷披萨是全世界最出名的争议披萨，你点它，就像在摇滚圈穿皮衣，一点都不稀奇。而且它跟夏威夷没关系，发明它的是个住在加拿大的希腊人。你连“异域风情”都没沾上。

下场呢？披萨一上桌，全桌人都去拿别的，只有它孤零零摆着。你只能说“我就爱这口”，然后一个人硬啃六块。菠萝出水，饼底泡成湿毛巾，火腿片在上面游泳。吃不完打包回家，第二天微波炉一转，咬一口，热乎乎的菠萝配咸火腿，就像前任突然发来一句“最近好吗”，说不上哪里不对，就是哪都不对。

Let's talk about the people who call it pizza. Mostly Chicagoans, who haven't eaten it since their cousin visited in 2019. You order tavern-cut thin crust every Friday, but the second a New Yorker opens his mouth, you're a martyr for the Gino's East gift shop.

And the tourists. You stood outside for an hour in a Michigan Avenue wind to be told your pie takes 45 minutes. You said "when in Chicago" like it was a vow. You got a photo of one slice held up by a spatula, a nap in a hotel bed at 4 p.m., and the right to say you "did it."

What do you get for calling it pizza? An argument with a stranger from Brooklyn, which is the only reason you came. Congratulations. Mayor Daley would be proud.

每桌都有那么一个人，菜单一翻就说：“来个夏威夷的。”全桌瞬间安静，像有人宣布要在群里发起投票。

他图什么？图人设。他想让你知道他不随大流，可他点的是每家店菜单上都有的第三个披萨。他心里还有本账：菠萝算水果，火腿算肉，一块下去，营养均衡。

下场呢？别人点的都见底了，只剩他那盘，菠萝汁把饼底泡软，拎起来像拎一条热毛巾。他还硬撑：“真的好吃，你们不懂。”

你知道夏威夷披萨是谁发明的吗？一个住在加拿大的希腊人。夏威夷不认，意大利不承认，全世界最后就剩你一个人替它出头。

Let's talk about the people who call it pizza. Chicagoans, mostly, from a city that spent a century being called the "Second City" and finally found a hill to die on. You don't love it. You're defending it.

You put your name in at 5:15 and eat at 7:00, then tell everyone it was worth the wait, because the alternative is admitting you spent your anniversary on a bench with a family from Ohio. You're after one thing: a fight with a New Yorker. And you win, in the sense that he stops texting you, which in Chicago counts as a civic victory.

What do you get? A two-hour nap, a ruined evening, and a Goldbelly order shipped to Phoenix, where you eat it alone in a kitchen, defending a city you moved away from in 2011.
